tourDays.title: Depart for Lisbon Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.description:
Depart for Lisbon
Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.

tourDays.title: Day 2
tourDays.description: Arrive in Lisbon Upon landing at Lisbon Airport, head to baggage claim and collect your luggage. Proceed to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. After meeting your group in the hotel lobby at 2:30 PM, board the bus and begin a panoramic sightseeing tour of Lisbon. We will stop at St. Jeromeâs Monastery, built to give thanks to the Virgin Mary for guiding Vasco da Gama on his voyage that linked Europe and Asia. Continue to drive by the Belem Quarter, which contains the iconic entryway to the Lisbon harbor, the Belem Tower. This important historic structure has many beautiful sculptures, such as depictions of St. Vincent and Our Lady of Safe Homecoming. The next stop is St. Anthonyâs Church, built upon the site of Saintâs birth; it is here that we will celebrate Mass. Although the patron Saint of lost things is known as St. Anthony of Padua (Italy), he was born in Lisbon, Portugal. This Church is built upon St. Anthonyâs birth site and is also where Saint John Paul II visited in 1982. After Mass, we will drive to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 3
tourDays.description: Lisbon - Santarem â Fatima Today, we will travel north to the old city of Santarem. We will attend Mass at the Church of St. Stephen, which holds a 13th-century Eucharistic Miracle. Continue to Fatima and visit the Hamlet of Aljustrel, the home of the three shepherd children. Visit the Parish Church and Fatima Parish Cemetery. Continue to your hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 4
tourDays.description: Fatima Today will be a memorable experience as you pray and meditate upon one of Our Blessed Motherâs apparition sites. Our Lady appeared to three shepherd children: Venerable Sister Lucia (age 10), St. Jacinta (age 7), and St. Francisco (age 9). These apparitions occurred monthly from May until October of 1917. Historically, as the entire world was in turmoil, Our Ladyâs most prominent message was to pray for world peace. The destruction of the world at that point in history was also mentioned by Our Lady, particularly in her second secret to the children. Our profoundly reflective day begins with a visit to the Little Chapel of the Apparitions. This simple yet modern chapel is where the Virgin Mary first appeared on May 13, 1917. Next, you will see the stunning neoclassical church, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary. This Sacred space contains the tombs of St. Francisco, St. Jacinta, and Sister Lucia. View the monument that commemorates the Sacred Heart of Jesus in the square. In honor of Our Ladyâs requests to pray the Rosary, the Basilica also features fifteen altars each dedicated to a mystery of the Rosary. Visit the Museum with the âFatima: Light and Peaceâ exhibition. Continue with a visit to the Holy Trinity Basilica. After free time for lunch, we will experience Christâs unconditional love by participating in the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra. The âSacred Wayâ marks the path taken by the shepherd children of Fatima to their first apparition with Our Lady. It is composed of fifteen small chapels commemorating the Passion of Our Lord. The fifteenth station, the Resurrection, can be found close to the Chapel of Calvary, dedicated to St. Stephen, King of Hungary. Ending the day with a visit to Valinhos, the site of Our Ladyâs August 1917 apparition and the first and third apparition of the Angel. Your night will conclude with private devotions and a candlelight procession, as requested by Our Lady in 1917. Enjoy dinner and a comfortable nightâs rest in Fatima.

tourDays.title: Day 5
tourDays.description: Fatima â Salamanca Depart Fatima and head to Salamanca, following a full breakfast at the hotel. Salamanca is a city in the Castilla y Leon region known for its large university. It is the oldest university in Spain that is still active. Our walking tour will take us to many famous sites. Visit the grand Plaza Mayor, an iconic square filled with food, shopping, and city events. See La Clerecia, a church and college of the Jesuit Order that was constructed in the 17th century. Next, visit La Casa de las Conchas, which is currently a public library and a monument decorated with shells, which symbolizes the ever-famous pilgrimage to Santiago (El Camino). Walk by the University of Salamanca, the oldest University in Spain and the third oldest in Europe. Walk across the Roman Bridge, which extends along the River Tormes and is a national monument. See La Iglesia de San Marcos, which is constructed in the Romanesque style and contains breathtaking paintings that portray many scenes of Our Ladyâs life. You will also see La Iglesia de San Martin, a Church devoted to St. Martin of Tours, the patron saint of beggars and those most in need. Visit the inside of the two joint Salamanca Cathedrals (old and new). The first is a Romanesque style, and the other is a Gothic style. Following this eventful day, you will return to your hotel for a delicious meal with your group and an overnight at your hotel in Salamanca.

tourDays.title: Day 6
tourDays.description: Salamanca - Alba de Tormes - Avila - Burgos This morning, after breakfast, you will board the bus and enjoy a short transfer to the village of Alba de Tormes. This town is home to the Carmelite Monastery that Saint Teresa founded in 1571. Upon arrival in Alba de Tormes, your group will celebrate Mass at this Monastery where the Saint died and is buried. Following Mass, you can visit the museum dedicated to St. Teresa of Avila, which also holds her incorrupt heart and left arm. Your group will enjoy free time for lunch on your own before continuing to the medieval city of Avila. Upon arrival, you will immediately notice the perfectly preserved 11th-century walls surrounding the old town. The conservation of architecture in this city, to which St. Teresa was born, deems its shrines, convents, and churches necessary to visit on any Catholic pilgrimage. The Cathedral de Avila encompasses the Romanesque, Gothic, and Renaissance styles of its time within its artwork and architecture. La Basilica de San Vicente in Avila stands on the site of the martyrdom of St. Vincent. Visit the Incarnation Convent, where St. Teresa became a nun. Saint Therese convinced Saint John of the Cross to reform the male Carmelite order, the reform she started when she met Saint John in Medina del Campo. After walking in the footsteps of St. Teresa, continue your journey to Burgos. Upon arrival in the historic capital of Old Castile, enjoy dinner. Following dinner, you will have the opportunity to explore the city of Burgos and admire its magnificent limestone Gothic-style cathedral. Late this evening, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 7
tourDays.description:
Burgos - Loyola - Lourdes Following breakfast, transfer from Burgos to Loyola to visit the birthplace of St. Ignatius, founder of the Jesuit Order. St. Ignatius dedicated himself to becoming a soldier of the Christian faith, and as a result of many tribulations, he wrote the ever-famous Spiritual Exercises. You will see the 17th-century Basilica dedicated to this remarkable Saint in Loyola. The Basilica is part of a series of buildings surrounding the âHoly House,â the birthplace of St. Ignatius. When you visit these Holy places, you will also have the opportunity to pray in the most venerated room, where St. Ignatius prayed and began his conversion. After meditating on the life of this founder of the Jesuit Order, you will enjoy free time for lunch and board the bus for the next destination. We will continue to Lourdes with a spectacular view of the Pyrenees Mountains. Upon arrival in Lourdes, you will check in to your hotel and enjoy a splendid dinner and peaceful overnight.
Days 8 & 9: Lourdes Over the next two days, you will stay in a small town in the Pyrenees Mountains. During your time in Lourdes, you will pray and meditate at the site of Our Ladyâs apparitions. Our Lady first appeared to Bernadette in 1858 and announced herself as âThe Immaculate Conceptionâ near the Grotto of Massabielle. During the first two apparitions, little Bernadette prayed the Rosary with Our Lady and left without exchanging words. During the following apparitions, Our Lady emphasized Godâs love for us and the necessity of performing acts of penance for sinners. Throughout your time in Lourdes, you will have the opportunity to attend Mass at the Grotto, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette. Watch a video presentation that explains the story of Lourdes. Wash your hands, wash your face, and drink the water of the miraculous spring. Finish with a short prayer: âOur Lady of Lourdes, pray for us. St. Bernadette, pray for us. O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.â Experience Christâs unconditional love as you meditate upon the life-size Stations of the Cross that overlook the Grotto of Massabielle. In Lourdes, you will walk in and meditate upon the footsteps of St. Bernadette. Your group will have the opportunity to see Boly Mill, the birthplace of St. Bernadette, and the âCachot,â an abandoned prison where Bernadetteâs impoverished family lived. Each evening, following dinner, you can attend the candlelight procession and pray the Rosary before a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 10
tourDays.description: Lourdes - Paris - Lisieux (St. Therese - the Little Flower) Today, you will enjoy breakfast before departing for Pau or Lourdes Airport for your short flight to Paris, continue on to Lisieux. According to Pope Pius X, St. Therese of Lisieux was the âgreatest saint of modern times.â Her extraordinary love for God and service to humanity will come alive as you walk in the great Saintâs footsteps. During your visit, you will see the beautiful Basilica of St. Therese and its magnificent mosaics and stained glass windows. You will have the opportunity to view relics, clothing, and personal objects that belonged to St. Therese when you visit her family home, Les Buissonnets. Additionally, you will tour the Carmelite Convent, which she entered in 1888 and where she is now buried. Dinner and overnight at your hotel in Lisieux.

tourDays.title: Day 11
tourDays.description: Lisieux - Landing Beaches - American Cemetery - Lisieux Upon waking up in Lisieux, enjoy breakfast, and then your group will celebrate Mass. After Mass we will travel to the Normandy Landing beaches. The Normandy landings were the landing operations, which took place on Tuesday, June 6, 1944 (termed D-Day) by the Allies of Normandy during World War II. As the largest seaborne invasion in history, the operation began the liberation of German-occupied northwestern Europe from Nazi control and contributed to the Alliesâ victory on the Western Front. Continue to visit The Normandy American Cemetery and Memorial, a World War II cemetery and memorial in Colleville-Sur-Mer, Normandy, France, honoring the American troops that died in Europe during World War II. Many of the brave American soldiers of World War II are buried here, and it is encouraged to say a prayer in thanksgiving for their courage. Return to Lisieux for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 12
tourDays.description: Lisieux - Chartres - Paris This morning, your day begins with an early breakfast before we depart for Chartres, known worldwide for its massive Cathedral Notre Dame and its incredible stained-glass windows from the 12th and 13th centuries. The World Heritage site, UNESCO, calls the Cathedral âthe high point of French Gothic artâ and a âmasterpieceâ. Pilgrims will also be able to venerate a precious relic of the Veil of Our Lady which is currently on display at the back of the main altar of the Cathedral of Chartres. You will have some free time for lunch in the quaint town of Chartres. After lunch, we will continue to Paris to check-in at your hotel, followed by some free time before a delicious dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 13
tourDays.description: Paris - Miraculous Medal â Notre Dame Cathedral Following breakfast, we will celebrate Mass. Following Mass enjoy a full day of sightseeing including the magnificent Sacre Coeur Basilica atop Montmartre Hill. The Basilica, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, was originally built in 1914 as an act of penance for infidelity that France experienced during that time. See the beautiful mosaic of the Risen Christ and the remarkable Grand Organ. Visit the the Tombs of many notable Cardinals. Time permitting, you may have the opportunity to ascend a staircase to the Dome, where you will take in a breathtaking panoramic view of Paris. Continue with a visit of the Chapel of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal, where we will have the opportunity to view the incorrupt body of St. Catherine Laboure. The Saintâs guardian angel led her to the chapel where the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared to her. During the apparitions, Our Lady repeatedly instructed the making and purpose of the Miraculous Medal. According to the Blessed Virgin Mary, those who wear the Miraculous Medal will receive special protection and abundant graces. Following this prayerful and reflective experience, we will walk to Saint Vincent de Paul Church. Next, on our tour of Paris, we will visit one of the most incredible churches in the world: Notre Dame Cathedral. The Cathedral has recently been re-opened to visitors. Guided group tours are scheduled to resume in June 2025. Board a bus tour and see some of the most recognizable symbols of Paris, including the Eiffel Tower, the Invalides, the LâArch de Triomphe, and the Champ-Elysees, the worldâs most famous boulevard. Your busy day ends with a lovely meal and a comfortable overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 14
tourDays.description: Paris - Rome Following breakfast at your hotel, your group will transfer to the Charles de Gaulle Airport and board your short flight to Rome. Upon arrival at Rome airport, collect your luggage in the baggage claim area and continue to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by a tour escort and/or driver. You will make your way to the bus and transfer to your hotel. Following check-in, you will have free time to unpack, relax, or explore Rome on your own. Your tour escort may suggest places to visit. Later in the afternoon, your group will meet in the hotel lobby for a âMeet and Greetâ with your fellow pilgrims and depart for Mass. Following Mass, you will attend a welcome dinner. After dinner, you can walk to St. Peterâs Square as a group for the Rosary (optional).

tourDays.title: Day 15
tourDays.description: Rome: Papal Audience - Basilica of St. John the Lateran - Holy Stairs - Basilica of St. Mary Major After a nice breakfast at your hotel, your first sightseeing day in Rome starts! The tour begins with the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square! The Audience is celebrated each Wednesday by His Holiness, the Pope (pending the papal schedule). Following the Audience, there will be free time for lunch, shopping, or to mail a postcard from the Vatican Post Office. This afternoon, you will visit the oldest of the four major Basilicas in Rome: The Basilica of St. John the Lateran. This Basilica houses the relics of Peter and Paul. It is where the Pope was installed as Bishop of Rome and where he officiates as the Bishop of Rome. Next, we will cross the street to visit the Holy Staircase. Tradition states that this Staircase is from Pontius Pilateâs palace in Jerusalem during the time of Jesus. It was brought to Rome by St. Helen in the 4th Century. If time permits, you may climb the steps on your knees while meditating on Christâs agonizing Passion. Proceed to the Basilica of St. Mary Major. This Basilica contains a relic from the Manger of the Infant Jesus. Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 16
tourDays.description: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica - Vatican Museum - Appian Way - Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls - Catacombs This morning, you will enjoy an early breakfast before making your way to the largest Church in Christendom: St. Peterâs Basilica. This Basilica was built on the site where St. Peter, the first Pope and Bishop of Rome, was martyred. Here, you can view Michelangeloâs Pieta. This stunning marble sculpture depicts the Virgin Mary holding Christ after His crucifixion, death, and removal from the cross before being placed in the tomb. Proceed to the Vatican Museum, where you will see the most impressive edifices, galleries, and awe-inspiring relics. Observe the Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, and the restored mural of the Last Judgment. The final stop on your Vatican tour is at the tomb of Saint John Paul II. Next, head to the Piazza Navona area for some free time and lunch (on your own). Continue on your short journey down the Appian Way, the earliest road of Ancient Rome. This road leads to the Domino Quo Vadis Chapel, the Baths of Caracalla, the Arch of Drusus, the Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and the catacombs of St. Callixtus. The day concludes with a visit to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls. Originally founded by Emperor Constantine in the 4th Century, this Basilica is the burial place of Saint Paul the Apostle. We will make our way to a local restaurant for dinner. Following dinner, feel free to explore the streets of Rome or return to the hotel for the evening.

tourDays.title: Day 17
tourDays.description: Rome - Montecassino - San Giovanni Rotondo Following breakfast, you will board your bus to enjoy the scenic route to Montecassino, passing through the Roman countryside, known for its villas and vineyards. During the bus ride, your tour escort will share interesting information regarding Italyâs spiritual, historical, and cultural history. Montecassino, the principal monastery of the Benedictine Order, was founded by Saint Benedict around 530 A.D. Following the tour, you can visit the gift shop before departing for San Giovanni Rotondo, the hometown of St. Padre Pio. Upon arrival in San Giovanni Rotondo, enjoy dinner at a local restaurant and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 18
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Monte Santâ Angelo Enjoy breakfast, and then we will visit the Old Church. After Mass, we will tour the sanctuary and see the crucifix, in front of which St. Pio received the stigmata. Visit the confessional from where St. Pio spent innumerable hours listening to confessions. Next, we will board the bus and travel along the beautiful Gargano Peninsula to the Grotto of St. Michael the Archangel. St. Michael appeared to a Bishop at this grotto to assure him that his diocese would not be destroyed as he feared. Following the visit to the grotto, enjoy some free time. On the way back to San Giovanni Rotondo, view breathtaking ocean views. Upon arrival, you will have time for devotion and reflection. Dinner and overnight. *Candlelight Procession: Between May and October, attend the weekly Candlelight Procession at the Sanctuary of St. Pio after dinner. These processions are lit by candlelight and are guided by the Most Holy Rosary. Following this prayerful experience, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 19
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Lanciano - Loreto - Assisi After breakfast, depart for Assisi. We will stop in Lanciano for a private Mass at the Convent/Church of Saint Francis built on top of the antique Church of St. Longinus. This Church is the site of a Eucharistic Miracle that occurred in the eighth Century. At the time of the miracle, there was a Basilian monk who struggled with the belief in the Real Presence in the Eucharist. During Mass, the monk, with doubt in his voice, said the words of consecration and saw the bread and wine transformed into Christâs physical flesh and blood. Leave for the Marian Shrine of Loreto to visit the Holy House of Nazareth and the beautiful Madonna of Loreto. Tradition holds that this is the house where Mary first prayed the Magnificat, where Jesus grew up, and where the Holy Family lived together in Nazareth. It was transported several times by angels to its current location. End the day in Assisi, hometown of St. Francis and St. Clare, with dinner and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 20
tourDays.description: Assisi Enjoy an early breakfast, followed by a full day of touring the hometown of St. Francis. St. Francis is the âPatron Saint of Animals and the Environment.â He founded the Franciscan Order and has inspired millions with his life of simplicity and humility. The atmosphere of Assisi has not changed since St. Francis began his ministry in the early 13th Century. We will start our tour at the Basilica of St. Francis. Visit his tomb, view a series of frescoes depicting his life, and a few of the Saintâs possessions. From there, we will continue on a walking tour through this picturesque town, including the birthplace of St. Francis. Visit the Santuario Della Spogliazione where St. Carlo Acutis is entombed. Carlo is the first millennial to have been declared a Saint. He had a great love for Jesus in the Eucharist and died of leukemia at the young age of 15. Our tour ends at the Church that honors St. Clare, the foundress of the Poor Clare Sisters. This Saint followed the teachings of St. Francis very closely by also living a life of poverty and humility. Enjoy some time for prayer, shopping, or a nice lunch. After lunch, we will board the bus, which will take us outside the walls of Assisi to the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels. This Basilica is where St. Francis spent most of his life, and it is made up of two structures. The first is the âPorziuncolaâ, where St. Francis founded his order of the Friar Minor (Franciscans). The second is the âCapella del Transitoâ, where St. Francis died. You will have the opportunity to visit the beautiful Rose Garden where St. Francis and other friars lived, as well as the cave where the Saint retired to pray. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 21
tourDays.description: Assisi - Orvieto - Assisi This morning, you will ride through the beautiful Umbrian mountains to Orvieto. This incredible town sits on a volcanic high rock formation. Here we visit one of the most beautiful Cathedrals in Italy. Its Christian history officially started in 1004. Because of its strategic location, Orvieto was built over preexisting Etruscan-era cave tunnels dating back 2,500 years. Some historians believe Christians used to celebrate Mass at a time when Christianity was forbidden. Return to Assisi for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 22
tourDays.description:
Rome - Medjugorje Today, depart from Italy for your flight(s) to Medjugorje. Upon arrival, you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver, who will take you on the 2.5-hour drive to the village of Medjugorje. Dinner and overnight.
Days 23 - 25: Medjugorje
The most beautiful features of Medjugorje are its simplicity and peace. While in Medjugorje, you will share in the faith journey of pilgrims from all over the world. A local guide will accompany your group throughout your stay in the village.
Some activities that will accompany you in your spiritual journey:
Attend Daily Mass: Each morning at 10:00 AM, your group will assemble at St. James Church for Mass (English-speaking). At the end of each Mass, regardless of language, there is a blessing of the religious articles that you have with you.
On Feast Days and Sundays, English Mass is at noon.
Climb Apparition Hill: This mountainous hill is where the visionaries first encountered Our Lady. At the base of this hill is a Blue Cross, where it is said Our Lady appeared to the children while they hid from the communist police in the early days of the alleged apparitions. While climbing, your group is invited to recite the Rosary, pausing five times for each decade of the Rosary. At the top of the hill, you will witness the exact location of the first alleged apparition of Our Lady to the visionaries and enjoy private time for prayer.
Climb Mt. Krizevac (Cross Mountain): In 1933, the villagers built a 30-foot high cross atop a mountain to commemorate Jesusâ passion and death on the cross. Your group will have the opportunity to climb this mountain and venerate the cross. While climbing, your group is invited to pray the Stations of the Cross (to meditate on Jesusâ suffering Road to Calvary), pausing fifteen times for each Station.
Apparitions: Each evening at 5:00 PM (or 6:00 PM, depending on Daylight Savings Time), your group can join the villagers and fellow pilgrims of Medjugorje at either St James Church or Apparition Hill to commemorate the time Our Lady appeared to the Visionaries. You can pray the Rosary as you all await that time of the apparition, 5:40 PM (or 6:40 PM during Daylight Savings Time).
*Afterward, all may attend the Croatian Mass at St. James Church. It is broadcast simultaneously over the radio to translate the service into many languages. Following the Croatian Mass, there is a Blessing of the Sick.
**For details about the Visionaries, please visit: www.206tours.com/visionaries
Adoration of the Blessed Sacrament: Our Lady has always called us to be close to her Son. For this, you may adore the Blessed Sacrament at the altar outside of St. James Church. Adoration is held on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Veneration of the Cross is held on Fridays inside the church. Additionally, there is an Adoration Chapel on the grounds of St. James Church, where Adoration is held in the afternoon hours.

tourDays.description: Depart Madrid toward Santiago de Compostela with stops in Astorga to visit the Bishopâs Palace (Museum of El Camino). Enter Galicia via Lugo and stop in O Cebreiro to view palooza-style houses and the site of a Eucharistic Miracle. In the evening proceed to Santiago de Compostela for dinner and overnight.

Dinner and overnight in Fatima.
tourDays.activities: Visit Little Chapel of the Apparitions; Visit Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary and tombs; Visit museum (Fatima: Light and Peace); Visit Holy Trinity Basilica; Participate in Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra; Visit Valinhos; Private devotions and candlelight procession

tourDays.title: Fatima - Salamanca
tourDays.description: After breakfast depart for Salamanca. Visit the Plaza Mayor, La ClerecÃ­a, Casa de las Conchas, the University, the cathedrals, the Roman Bridge, San Marcos and San Martin churches, and more. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant and overnight.

tourDays.title: Lourdes

tourDays.activities: Attend Mass at the Grotto; Participate in blessing of the sick; Attend candlelight procession and pray the Rosary; Wash in the baths; Visit sanctuary sites

tourDays.title: Budapest â Esztergom â Szentendre â Budapest
tourDays.description: Breakfast on-board followed by your departure to Esztergom, a medieval city lying picturesquely on the Danube Bend. We will also visit Szentendre, the charming, ethnic artist colony with its winding lanes, seven aspiring church towers, colorful houses, narrow side streets, genuine Mediterranean ambience and scores of museums, galleries, guest houses and warm restaurants. It is the most frequented tourist destination of the Danube Bend. Return to the ship for lunch. After lunch, depart for a tour of Buda, the upper part of Budapest. Visit the Castle District and see the main attractions of the area: Fisherman's Bastion which takes its name from the guild of fishermen that were responsible for defending this stretch of city walls in the Middle Ages, followed by Matyas Church, a gorgeous Romanesque style church whose Ecclesiastical Art museum houses numerous sacred relics and medieval stone carvings, including replicas of the Hungarian royal crown and coronation jewels. Return to the ship for dinner and a folklore show this evening.

tourDays.description: Board the bus and transfer to Alba de Tormes to celebrate Mass at the Carmelite Monastery where St. Teresa died and is buried, and visit the museum dedicated to St. Teresa (which holds her incorrupt heart and left arm). After free time for lunch, continue to Avila to see the 11th-century walls, the Cathedral de Avila, La Basilica de San Vicente and the Incarnation Convent. Continue on to Burgos for dinner, evening exploration and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to Alba de Tormes; Celebrate Mass at the Carmelite Monastery; Visit the St. Teresa museum; Free time for lunch; Visit Avila (city walls, Cathedral de Avila, La Basilica de San Vicente, Incarnation Convent); Travel to Burgos; Dinner, evening exploration and overnight

tourDays.title: Burgos - Loyola - Lourdes
tourDays.description: After breakfast transfer from Burgos to Loyola to visit the birthplace of St. Ignatius and the 17th-century Basilica and 'Holy House' where St. Ignatius prayed and began his conversion. After free time for lunch, continue to Lourdes with views of the Pyrenees Mountains. Upon arrival check in to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Transfer from Burgos to Loyola; Visit birthplace of St. Ignatius (Holy House); Visit the 17th-century Basilica at Loyola; Prayer in the venerated room; Free time for lunch; Transfer to Lourdes; Hotel check-in, dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Lourdes

Attend Mass at the Grotto of Massabielle, view a video presentation about Lourdes, wash hands/face and drink from the miraculous spring, and wash in the baths. Meditate on the life-size Stations of the Cross overlooking the Grotto, visit Boly Mill (birthplace of St. Bernadette) and the 'Cachot' where her family lived. Each evening attend the candlelight procession and pray the Rosary. Dinner and overnight in Lourdes.
tourDays.activities: Pray and meditate at the apparition sites; Attend Mass at the Grotto of Massabielle; Watch a video presentation about Lourdes; Drink from the miraculous spring; Wash in the baths; Meditate on the life-size Stations of the Cross; Visit Boly Mill (birthplace of St. Bernadette); Visit the Cachot; Attend candlelight procession and pray the Rosary; Dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Lourdes

Dinner and overnight in Lourdes.
tourDays.activities: Attend Mass at the Grotto of Massabielle; Watch video presentation; Drink from the spring and wash in the baths; Meditate on the Stations of the Cross; Visit Boly Mill and the Cachot; Attend candlelight procession and pray the Rosary; Dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Return Flights Home

Explore stalls of handcrafted goods, enjoy Polish culinary specialties, see the central Christmas tree, and attend live performances and choir concerts. Dinner at leisure (not included).
tourDays.activities: Visit KrakÃ³w Choinki (Christmas Market) in Main Market Square; Browse stalls offering handcrafted goods; Sample culinary specialties (pierogi, oscypek, mulled wine); Attend live performances and choir concerts; Dinner at leisure (not included)

tourDays.title: Krakow - Lagiewniki (Shrine of Divine Mercy) - Wieliczka - Krakow

This afternoon visit the Archbasilica of St. John the Lateran, the Holy Stairs brought to Rome by St. Helen, and the Basilica of St. Mary Major where Holy Mass will be celebrated. tourDays.activities: Tour St. Peter's Basilica (view Pieta; visit papal tombs); Visit Vatican Museum (Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel); Drive along Appian Way; Visit Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls; Visit Catacombs

tourDays.description: Board the bus and travel to the Abbey of Monte Cassino, the principal monastery of the Benedictine Order. Continue on to San Giovanni Rotondo, where St. Pio (Padre Pio) lived. Dinner and overnight in San Giovanni Rotondo.

tourDays.title: Assisi - Orvieto - Assisi

tourDays.activities: Drive through Umbrian mountains to Orvieto; Visit Orvieto Cathedral; Return to Assisi

tourDays.title: Assisi - Siena - Florence

Walking tour of Siena including the Duomo di Siena and Piazza del Campo with free time for lunch. Continue to Florence and enjoy free time to explore the city. Dinner and overnight in Florence.
tourDays.activities: Drive to Siena; Visit Basilica of St. Catherine and Shrine of St. Catherine; View incorrupt head of St. Catherine; Walking tour of Siena (Duomo di Siena, Piazza del Campo); Travel to Florence and explore at leisure

Visit L'Accademia to view works by Botticelli, Ghirlandaio, Pontormo and Michelangelo's David. Afternoon free to explore Florence. Dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Guided walking tour starting at Santa Croce; Walk by Piazza Signorina, Palazzo Vecchio, Uffizi, Ponte Vecchio, Republic Square; Visit Santa Maria del Fiore; Visit L'Accademia (see Michelangelo's David); Free time in the afternoon

tourDays.title: Shimizu (Mount Fuji)
tourDays.description: In the shadow of Mount Fuji, Shimizu is one of the most beautiful ports in Japan. Walk through the pine groves of Miho, home to a 650-year-old Japanese black pine, or enjoy spectacular views of Mount Fuji from the lush, forested hill of Nihondaira. Take in the seascapes on a bay cruise, or learn of undersea delights at Japanâs first sushi museum, and get a glimpse at feudal life in Japan in 200 BC at the archaeological site of Toro. Shop for traditional Japanese wooden handcrafts and fabrics unique to the region, and sample some yokan, a sweet jellied confection.
tourDays.activities: Walk through the pine groves of Miho; View Mount Fuji from Nihondaira; Take a bay cruise; Visit Japan's first sushi museum; Visit archaeological site of Toro; Shop for traditional wooden handcrafts and fabrics; Sample yokan (sweet jellied confection)

tourDays.title: Nagoya
tourDays.description: Japanâs fourth largest city by population, Nagoya, is a center of modern commerce, with Toyota, Noritake china, and a Legoland theme park calling this capital home. Tour the Toyota Exhibit Hall, experience Noritake Gardens and sit amongst the stars in the planetarium at the Science Museum. Nagoya Castle, deemed a National Treasure, is a must-see, as is exploring their entertainment district, Sakae. This busy hub is where youâll find Nagoya TV Tower, the cityâs symbol, and Oasis 21, a multi-level public park with a futuristic water theme.
tourDays.activities: Tour the Toyota Exhibit Hall; Visit Noritake Gardens; Visit the planetarium at the Science Museum; Visit Nagoya Castle; Explore Sakae entertainment district; See Nagoya TV Tower and Oasis 21

tourDays.title: Kyoto (Osaka)
tourDays.description: Cradled by rolling hills on three sides, Kyoto is considered the historical and cultural epicenter of the country. The city was Japanâs capital for more than 1,000 years (794 â 1868), and approximately 1,600 Buddhist temples and more than 400 ShintÅ shrines are peppered throughout the city. From numerous historic sites and tranquil gardens to delicious local cuisine and boutique shopping, Kyoto offers you a window into the heart of Japanâs traditions and culture.
tourDays.activities: Visit historic sites and temples; Explore tranquil gardens; Sample local cuisine; Boutique shopping

tourDays.title: Kochi
tourDays.description: Engage with locals and indulge in local flavors in this welcoming city, known for its famed dish Katsuo no tataki (a type of tuna tataki). The city center was initially settled in 1601 as a town surrounding Kochi Castle, which is now one of the regionâs principal attractions. Delve into times gone by as you stroll along the famed, red Harimaya-bashi â the basis for an old local folklore song. Discover the lovely Katsurahama beach area, where the Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial overlooks the sea and honors this legendary Japanese peace negotiator.
tourDays.activities: Engage with locals; Sample Katsuo no tataki; Visit Kochi Castle; Stroll Harimaya-bashi; Visit Katsurahama beach and Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial

tourDays.title: Hiroshima
tourDays.description: History is never far from mind in Hiroshima; thus the city has created one of the most important and breathtaking memorials in the world, the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and Museum. Statues, halls, and monuments at this World Heritage Site honor those who fell in World War II. As one of Japanâs largest islands, Hiroshima also offers rich natural beauty and a myriad of outdoor activities like biking, hiking, and beaching. The local cuisine is plentiful, especially the signature âOkonomiyaki,â a crepe filled with meat, seafood, cabbage, and vegetables. Oysters (usually grilled) serve as an additional fresh and delicious culinary draw.
tourDays.activities: Visit Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and Museum; Explore World Heritage Site monuments; Biking, hiking, beach activities; Try local cuisine such as okonomiyaki and grilled oysters

tourDays.title: Kagoshima
tourDays.description: Visit the exquisite Iso-Teien Garden and its villa, built in 1660, and enjoy gorgeous views before a short ferry ride to smoking Sakurajima for a close-up view of the volcano and its lava fields. Or journey into the countryside to Chiran and its well-preserved streets lined with samurai homes. Enjoy the beautiful landscape of Lake Ikeda and the stunning vistas of the Satsuma Peninsula. Local Satsuma dolls, unique cards printed with ink made from volcanic ash, and unusual wooden toys make interesting souvenirs. And be sure to try some miso soup, sashimi, or ramen, the areaâs famous noodles.
tourDays.activities: Visit Iso-Teien Garden and villa; Take a ferry to Sakurajima to view the volcano; Visit Chiran and samurai homes; See Lake Ikeda and Satsuma Peninsula vistas; Shop for local souvenirs; Try local dishes such as miso soup, sashimi, and ramen

tourDays.title: Nagasaki
tourDays.description: Nagasaki is often equated with the dropping of the atomic bomb, and there are many moving museums, memorials, and monuments dedicated to its World War II history that shouldnât be missed. Yet modern Nagasaki offers a vibrant and charming atmosphere thatâs waiting to be explored. Among its cobblestone and rolling hills, the city boasts a rich culinary scene that will excite your inner foodie. To capture Nagasakiâs scenic beauty, consider a cable car ride or harbor tour. Centuries-old shrines, temples, and churches dot the landscape and are a must-see.
tourDays.activities: Visit museums, memorials, and monuments related to WWII; Explore the city and culinary scene; Take a cable car ride or harbor tour; Visit shrines, temples, and churches

tourDays.title: Jeju
tourDays.description: The dormant volcano Hallasan formed many of the natural attractions found on Jeju. As South Koreaâs tallest mountain, Hallasan offers an abundance of hiking opportunities and is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve showcasing a crater lake and an abundance of plants and wildlife. The Manjang Cave, formed by cooling lava, is the worldâs longest lava tube and is partially open for tours. Head from the mountain to the magnificent beaches and watch the famed haenyo (powerful seawomen) dive for octopus, abalone, clams, and more without the aid of a breathing apparatus. Donât miss the opportunity to sample fresh seafood dishes at a local restaurant.
tourDays.activities: Hike Hallasan; Visit Manjang Cave (lava tube) for tours; Visit beaches and watch haenyo divers; Sample fresh seafood at local restaurants

tourDays.title: Arrive in Rome
tourDays.description: Welcome to Rome, also known as âThe Eternal Cityâ. Upon landing at Rome airport, claim your baggage and proceed to the Arrivals Hall, where your tour guide and/or driver will greet you. Following check-in at the hotel, enjoy some free time to unpack, relax or explore Rome on your own. Your tour escort may suggest places to visit. Later this afternoon, between 3:00 PM and 3:30 PM, your group will meet in the hotel lobby for a meet and greet with fellow pilgrims and your priest. You will depart together for Mass, and following Mass, you will attend a welcome dinner. After dinner you have to opportunity to join in a walk to St. Peterâs Square for the Rosary (optional).
tourDays.activities: Claim baggage; Meet tour guide/driver; Hotel check-in; Free time to unpack/relax/explore; Meet and greet with fellow pilgrims and priest; Attend Mass; Welcome dinner; Optional walk to St. Peter's Square for the Rosary

tourDays.title: Papal Audience and major basilicas in Rome
tourDays.description: After a nice breakfast at your hotel, your first sightseeing day in Rome starts! The tour begins with attending the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square! The Audience is celebrated each Wednesday by His Holiness (pending the papal schedule). Following the Audience, there will be free time for lunch, or shop, or mail a postcard from the Vatican Post Office. This afternoon you will visit the oldest of the four major Basilicas in Rome, and the home to the relics of Peter and Paul, the Basilica of St. John the Lateran. This Basilica is where the Pope is installed as Bishop of Rome, and where he officiates as the Bishop of Rome. Next, we will cross the street to visit the Holy Staircase. Tradition states that this staircase is from Pontius Pilateâs palace of Jerusalem during the time of Jesus. It is also said that this Staircase was brought to Rome by St. Helen in the 4th century. If time permits, you may climb the steps on your knees, in memory of Christâs agonizing Passion. To conclude your day, we will proceed to the Basilica of St. Mary Major. This Basilica contains a relic from the Manger of the Infant Jesus. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Attend the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square; Free time for lunch/shop/mail a postcard at Vatican Post Office; Visit Basilica of St. John the Lateran; Visit the Holy Staircase; Visit Basilica of St. Mary Major; Return to hotel for dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: St. Peter's Basilica, Vatican Museums and Appian Way
tourDays.description: This morning you will enjoy an early breakfast before making your way to the largest Christendom Church, St. Peterâs Basilica. This Basilica was built on the site where St. Peter, the first Pope and Bishop of Rome, was martyred. It is here that you will view Michelangeloâs Pieta. This stunning marble sculpture depicts the Virgin Mary holding Christ after His crucifixion, death, and removal off the cross before being placed in the tomb. Continue to proceed to the Vatican Museums. At the world-renowned museum, you will see the most impressive of edifices, galleries, and awe-inspiring relics. Additionally, you will observe the Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, and Michelangeloâs Masterpiece, the restored mural of the Last Judgment. The final stop on your Vatican tour is at the tomb of Saint John Paul II. Next, head to the Piazza Navona area for some free time and lunch (on your own). Continue your short journey down the Appian Way, the earliest road of Ancient Rome. This road leads to the Domino Quo Vadis Chapel, the Baths of Caracalla, the Arch of Drusus, the Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and the catacombs of St. Callixtus. The day concludes with a visit to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls. Originally founded by Emperor Constantine in the 4th Century, this Basilica is the burial place of Saint Paul the Apostle. We will make our way to a local restaurant for dinner. Following dinner, feel free to explore the streets of Rome, or return to the hotel for overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit St. Peterâs Basilica and view Michelangeloâs Pieta; Visit the Vatican Museums (Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, Last Judgment); Visit the tomb of Saint John Paul II; Free time / lunch at Piazza Navona (on your own); Drive down the Appian Way and visit Domino Quo Vadis Chapel, Baths of Caracalla, Arch of Drusus, Tomb of Cecilia Metella, catacombs of St. Callixtus; Visit Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls; Dinner at a local restaurant

tourDays.title: Orvieto and Assisi (St. Francis)
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast, you will head north through the Roman countryside of vineyards and villas. Throughout this bus ride, your tour escort will share very interesting information regarding the spiritual, historical, and cultural aspects of Italy. Arrive in Orvieto, a city known for its Duomo and considered one of the most architecturally important in Europe, for its Etruscan roots, and for the museums where one finds collections and displays that range over 2,500 years of history. During this tour, you will walk through Orvietoâs charming, narrow alleys, and small squares. Your tour will be a very memorable experience, perfect for reflecting over while you enjoy an Umbrian meal and a glass of Orvieto Classico wine. After lunch, board the coach and continue to Assisi. Upon arrival, your group will enjoy a tour of the hometown of St. Francis. St. Francis is the âPatron Saint of Animals and the Environment.â Additionally, he is responsible for founding the Franciscan Order and, the inspiration for our Holy Father, The Pope. He chose his name in admiration of the Saint of Nature, and Servant to the Poor. Known for being a humble man himself, The Pope spent most of his life denying the luxuries of life. He preferred to live in simplicity and humility while giving up all other worldly possessions, just as St. Francis did. As your group visits the birthplace of St. Francis, you will become captivated as the atmosphere has not changed since St. Francis began his ministry, in the early 13th-century. During the tour, your group will have the opportunity to visit the tomb of St. Francis at his Basilica. At the Basilica of St. Francis, you will have the opportunity to view a series of frescoes depicting his life, as well as view a few of the saintâs possessions. Additionally, your group will visit the Church of San Damiano. At this modest, yet beautiful Holy Church, you will have the opportunity to kneel before the crucifix where Jesus asked St. Francis, âto rebuild His church.â You will also be able to visit the Santuario Della Spogliazione where you can pray at the tomb of St. Carlo Acutis. Carlo is the first millennial to have been declared a Saint who loved the Real Presence of Jesus in the Eucharist. He died at the young age of 15 from leukemia. As the tour continues, your group will visit St. Mary of the Angels Basilica. This Basilica is where St. Francis spent most of life and is made up of two structures; both of which you will visit. The Porziuncola is where St. Francis founded his order of the Friar Minor (Franciscans), and the Capella del Transito, which is the place of St. Francisâ death. During this visit, your group will have the opportunity to visit the beautiful Rose Garden where St. Francis and other friars lived, as well as the cave where the Saint retired to pray. After visiting this beautiful Basilica, your group will enjoy some free time on your own. Feel free to take this time for additional prayer or shop in the Gift Shop. The last stop on your tour will be to the Church that honors St. Clare, the foundress of the Poor Clare Sisters. This Saint followed the teachings of St. Francis very closely by also living a life of poverty and humility. Lastly, your group will transfer to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Bus ride through Roman countryside; Walk through Orvieto's alleys and squares; Lunch with Umbrian fare and Orvieto Classico wine; Coach transfer to Assisi; Tour Assisi including tomb of St. Francis and frescoes; Visit Church of San Damiano; Visit Santuario Della Spogliazione (tomb of St. Carlo Acutis); Visit St. Mary of the Angels Basilica (Porziuncola, Capella del Transito); Visit Rose Garden and cave; Visit Church of St. Clare; Free time; Transfer to hotel for dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Umbria: Bevagna, Trevi and Montefalco
tourDays.description: Today youâll discover the Umbria region, also called âItalyâs green heartâ. Drive to the town of Bevagna, where ancient Roman monuments date back to the 1st century B.C. Just a few steps from the Forum, see the remains of a temple and check out the thermal baths which are still decorated with frescoes. Explore the medieval heart of the city, including the 13th-century Palazzo dei Consoli, and the 19th-century theater with decorations by Domenico Bruschi and a ceiling of dancing muses by Mariano Piervittori. After the visit of Bevagna, transfer to Trevi, the town famous for its olive oil, and enjoy a guided visit with light lunch at an oil mill. You will then visit the medieval city of Montefalco, with its Romanesque, Renaissance, and Gothic monuments: tour the Museo di San Francesco (Museum of St. Francis), a former Franciscan church with frescoes that tell the story of one of Italyâs most famous patron saints. Admire the 13th to14th-century Palazzo Comunale (Town Hall), and the former church of San Filippo Neri, now a town theater. Other historic churches include Santâ Agostino and Santa Illuminata. See handsome 16th-century residences in Santa Maria di Piazza. Then, visit a local wine producer, to taste the local wines, and especially the deep red Sagrantino wines, made from an Italian grape variety mainly found in the area. Return to the hotel in Assisi for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Bevagna (Roman monuments, thermal baths, Palazzo dei Consoli, theater); Transfer to Trevi; Guided visit and light lunch at an oil mill (olive oil tasting); Visit Montefalco (Museo di San Francesco, Palazzo Comunale, San Filippo Neri, Sant' Agostino, Santa Illuminata); Visit local wine producer and Sagrantino wine tasting; Return to hotel in Assisi for dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: San Gimignano and Siena
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast, celebrate Mass and depart Assisi for Siena, stopping at the walled medieval city of San Gimignano. Resting on the top of a hill, explore the areaâs impressive Romanesque and Gothic architecture, frescoes, towers, and more. Upon arrival, meet your local guide who will show you first to the medieval city of Siena. Siena is also the city of Saint Catherine of Siena: she is one of the two patron saints of Italy, together with St. Francis of Assisi. Begin with a private tour of the Siena Cathedral, admiring the unique marble stripes of its interior as well as the Piccolomini Library, which hosts illuminated choir books and frescoes. Your tour will continue to the Piazza del Campo, the famed site of the Palio di Siena, the horse races held twice a year. Afterward, soak up some free time to continue exploring independently or to purchase lunch. Continue to Siena for dinner at a local restaurant and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Celebrate Mass; Depart Assisi and stop at San Gimignano; Explore San Gimignano (architecture, frescoes, towers); Meet local guide in Siena; Private tour of Siena Cathedral and Piccolomini Library; Visit Piazza del Campo; Free time for independent exploration or lunch; Dinner at a local restaurant and overnight in Siena

tourDays.title: Tuscan day: Montalcino, Orcia Valley, Pienza and Montepulciano
tourDays.description: After breakfast, you will depart for a full dayâs Tuscan tour. The tour begins with a drive through the rolling, grape-clad scenery leading you to Montalcino. Once here, you can breathe in the timeless character of this hill town with its narrow and winding alleyways and squares. The town is also the home of the world-famous Brunello wines. Visit a famous and renowned wine cellar/museum set on an estate with a rich history. Here you can taste these rich and aged wines and receive expert advice and suggestions from a connoisseur. Go up to the top of the town along alleys and streets lined with flower-covered houses and peeks of the plains spreading out before you. Here you can feast your eyes and breath in the history and culture of the place. The next stop is one of the hidden gems of Tuscany â the Orcia Valley. Stop at San Quirico dâOrcia and you use your free time to visit the Romanesque Collegiate with its dragons and mermaids on its portals or the Horti Leonini â a beautiful box-garden. Having spent some time here you will understand why UNESCO has put the area on its list. Continue to the perfect Renaissance model of a city: Pienza. Perched on a hilltop, the town seeps history and offers one of the best cheeses in the world: Pecorino. Youâll be given the chance to taste the best of the cheeses and then youâll have free time to look at the palaces and piazzas of this Florence in miniature. The last stop is the elegant and refined hill town of Montepulciano. It stands 605 meters above sea level, encircled by massive fortifications. It really is like walking into the past. Later, itâs home to the highly esteemed Vino Nobile, where you will take part in a wine tasting session whilst visiting the cellar where the wine is stored. A perfectly tasteful way to explore one of the regions most loved by true and discerning Tuscans. Transfer to Florence for dinner in a local restaurant and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Drive to Montalcino; Visit wine cellar/museum and taste Brunello wines; Stop at San Quirico dâOrcia and visit Romanesque Collegiate or Horti Leonini; Visit Pienza and taste Pecorino cheese; Visit Montepulciano and wine tasting of Vino Nobile; Transfer to Florence for dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Florence sightseeing and cooking class
tourDays.description: After breakfast, meet your local guide and travel first to the neighborhood of San Lorenzo, a popular spot with visitors and locals alike for its open-air market, which sells a wide array of leather goods, clothing, and more. As you go, your guide will discuss the rule of the Medici family and their significant impact on the cityâs politics and art during the Renaissance. Head past the Medici Chapels, designed by Michelangelo and Matteo Nigetti, and check out the Basilica of San Lorenzo, where members of the Medici family are buried. Next, wander over to one of Florenceâs most iconic landmarks, the Duomo, where Brunelleschiâs Dome famously sits. Visit the Baptistery and Giottoâs Bell Tower while learning the history of the architecture. Continue through the bustling square of Piazza Della Signoria, home to the Palazzo Vecchio, outdoor cafes, and a collection of famous sculptures, including Giambolognaâs Rape of the Sabine Women. Visit Il Porcellino, the bronze piglet statue that offers luck to those who rub his nose. Visit the Academia and experience this world-renowned museum. In the afternoon, meet your Chef and get ready for a traditional Tuscan cooking lesson: prepare a delicious, full meal. Learn the principles of Tuscan produce, tips on how best to prepare it, and the fine art of creating pasta from scratch. Reward your efforts afterward by sitting down to feast on your dishes, complemented by local wine. After dinner, return to the hotel for overnight.
tourDays.activities: Meet local guide; Visit San Lorenzo neighborhood and open-air market; See Medici Chapels and Basilica of San Lorenzo; Visit the Duomo, Baptistery, and Giottoâs Bell Tower; Visit Piazza Della Signoria, Palazzo Vecchio, Il Porcellino; Visit the Academia; Afternoon cooking lesson with a Chef (prepare meal, dinner with local wine)

tourDays.title: Chianti wine region, Greve and Castellina
tourDays.description: Journey through the beautiful Tuscan countryside, viewing the olive groves, vineyards, and rolling hills of one of the most prestigious winemaking regions in the world before arriving in Chianti Fiorentino. Stop for the visit to a distinguished castle and wine estate, where youâll tour the historical cellars. Learn the winemakerâs secrets as you see where the grapes are crushed, and where the wine is matured and bottled. Then, get to tasting! Enjoy a glass of Chianti Classico, Chianti Reserve, Tuscan dessert wine, or a prominent white wine. Learn the complex character of each from your expert guide while you taste. Later, enjoy a typical Tuscan lunch, and afterward, head to the medieval village of Greve, where the most important wine fair of the Chianti region is held each year. Explore the main square and pursue the local artisan shops. Then make your way to Castellina, a hilltop village characterized by its large fortress and Etruscan settlements. Stroll past the medieval street of Via Delle Volte and explore the local shops and squares before returning to Florence. Farewell dinner in Florence, before returning to your hotel for overnight.
tourDays.activities: Drive through Tuscan countryside; Visit castle and wine estate and tour historical cellars; Wine tasting (Chianti Classico, Chianti Reserve, Tuscan dessert wine, white wine); Typical Tuscan lunch; Visit Greve (main square, artisan shops); Visit Castellina (Via Delle Volte); Return to Florence and farewell dinner

tourDays.title: Departure or extend stay
tourDays.description: Extend your stay! Or transfer to the airport in Florence for our return flights home! After breakfast, board the coach and transfer to Florence International airport for your return flight. Arrivederci, Italia!
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Board coach and transfer to Florence International airport; Return flight home; Option to extend stay

tourDays.title: Depart USA
tourDays.description: Depart USA for your overnight flight to Europe. Dinner and breakfast will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Overnight flight from USA to Europe; Dinner and breakfast served on board

tourDays.title: Lourdes
tourDays.description: Connect with your flight to Toulouse, Pau or Lourdes airport. Greeted by tour guide/driver, scenic drive to Lourdes, check in to hotel. Optional participation in the candlelight procession after dinner.
tourDays.activities: Connect flight to Toulouse/Pau/Lourdes; Scenic drive to Lourdes; Hotel check-in; Optional candlelight procession

tourDays.title: Lourdes
tourDays.description: Time to pray with fellow pilgrims. Opportunities to attend Mass at the Grotto, watch a video presentation about Lourdes, walk in the footsteps of St. Bernadette, visit Boly Mill and the Cachot, pray for the sick, drink water from the miraculous spring or use the healing baths, walk the life-sized Stations of the Cross, and kneel in the chapel built on the rock of the Grotto. Evenings free for optional Blessed Sacrament Procession.
tourDays.activities: Attend Mass at the Grotto; Watch Lourdes video presentation; Walk in the footsteps of St. Bernadette; Visit Boly Mill and the Cachot; Drink water from the miraculous spring / use healing baths; Walk the Stations of the Cross; Kneel in the chapel built on the rock of the Grotto; Optional Blessed Sacrament Procession (evening)

tourDays.title: Lourdes
tourDays.description: Continuation of pilgrim activities in Lourdes with opportunities listed for Day 3. Evenings free for optional Blessed Sacrament Procession.
tourDays.activities: Attend Mass at the Grotto; Visit Lourdes sites (Boly Mill, Cachot); Pray for the sick; use miraculous spring or baths; Walk the Stations of the Cross; Optional Blessed Sacrament Procession (evening)

tourDays.title: Lourdes to Paris
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast transfer to Lourdes or Pau Airport for a short flight to Paris. Greeted by tour guide, free time for lunch, Mass at the Shrine of the Miraculous Medal, then panoramic sightseeing including Notre Dame, the Eiffel Tower, L'Arc de Triomphe and the Champs Elysees. Dinner and overnight in Paris.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast and transfer to airport; Short flight to Paris; Mass at the Shrine of the Miraculous Medal; Panoramic sightseeing of Paris (Notre Dame, Eiffel Tower, L'Arc de Triomphe, Champs Elysees); Dinner and overnight in Paris

tourDays.title: Lisieux (St. Therese)
tourDays.description: Depart for Lisieux. Tour the home of St. Therese, visit the Basilica of Saint Therese, celebrate Mass, stop at Les Buissonets (St. Therese's family home) to see relics and personal objects, and tour the Cathedral of St. Peter and the Carmelite Convent. Return to Paris for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart for Lisieux; Tour Basilica of Saint Therese; Celebrate Mass in Lisieux; Visit Les Buissonets (St. Therese's family home); Tour Cathedral of St. Peter and the Carmelite Convent; Return to Paris

tourDays.title: Nevers (St. Bernadette)
tourDays.description: Depart for Nevers via the Loire Valley. Visit the convent of St. Gildard to see St. Bernadette's incorrupt body. Return to Paris for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart for Nevers via the Loire Valley; Visit the convent of St. Gildard and see St. Bernadette's incorrupt body; Return to Paris

tourDays.title: Paris to Rome
tourDays.description: Transfer to Paris Airport for a short flight to Rome. Upon arrival in Rome, greeted by tour escort/driver and escorted to hotel. Free afternoon for rest, relaxation or exploration.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to Paris Airport; Short flight to Rome; Transfer to hotel in Rome; Free afternoon in Rome

tourDays.title: Christian Rome sightseeing
tourDays.description: Sightseeing tour of significant Catholic sites in Rome: Basilica of St. Mary Major, the Holy Stairs, Basilica of St. John Lateran, St. Paul Outside the Walls, the Appian Way, Quo Vadis Chapel, Baths of Caracalla, Arch of Drusus, Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and a visit to one of the catacombs such as St. Callixtus. Time permitting visit the Trevi Fountain. Dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Basilica of St. Mary Major; See the Holy Stairs; Visit Basilica of St. John Lateran; Visit St. Paul Outside the Walls; See the Appian Way and Quo Vadis Chapel; See Baths of Caracalla, Arch of Drusus, Tomb of Cecilia Metella; Visit a catacomb (e.g., St. Callixtus); Time-permitting visit to the Trevi Fountain

tourDays.title: Vatican: Papal Audience & Museums
tourDays.description: Depart for Vatican City to attend the Papal Audience (pending papal schedule). Visit the Vatican Museums including the Tapestry Gallery, the Raphael Rooms and the Sistine Chapel. Enter St. Peter's Basilica to view the Pieta, Bernini's bronze canopy, and the tomb of Saint John Paul II. Dinner and overnight in Rome.
tourDays.activities: Attend the Papal Audience (pending papal schedule); Visit Vatican Museums (Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel); Enter St. Peter's Basilica and view the Pieta and Bernini's canopy; Visit the tomb of Saint John Paul II

tourDays.title: Rome to Siena to Assisi
tourDays.description: Depart Rome and head north to Siena. Stroll the Piazza del Campo, visit the Cathedral and the Basilica of St. Francis (containing the miraculous consecrated hosts), and view the incorrupt head of St. Catherine at the Basilica of St. Dominic. Continue on to Assisi for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart Rome for Siena; Stroll Piazza del Campo; Visit the Cathedral in Siena; Visit the Basilica of St. Francis; View the incorrupt head of St. Catherine at the Basilica of St. Dominic; Continue to Assisi

tourDays.title: Assisi: St. Francis & St. Clare sites
tourDays.description: Visit the tomb of St. Francis and explore his hilltop birthplace. Visit the 13th-century Basilica containing the saint's possessions and frescoes, kneel before the crucifix that spoke to St. Francis, visit St Mary of the Angels Basilica (Portiuncola, the rose bush, and the cave), stroll medieval streets, stop at an outdoor cafe with a view of an ancient Roman temple, and visit the Church of St. Clare to see her incorrupt body. Visit the two saints' tombs before dinner.
tourDays.activities: Visit the tomb of St. Francis; Explore the Basilica with frescoes and St. Francis's possessions; Kneel before the crucifix associated with St. Francis; Visit St Mary of the Angels Basilica (Portiuncola, rose bush, cave); Stroll medieval streets and stop at an outdoor cafe; Visit the Church of St. Clare and see St. Clare's incorrupt body

tourDays.title: Travel to Medjugorje
tourDays.description: After breakfast depart from the hotel to Rome or Florence Airport for flights to Medjugorje. Upon arrival, greeted by tour guide/driver and travel by private coach about 2 1/2 hours to the village of Medjugorje. Meet fellow pilgrims, spiritual leader and be introduced to host family/inn where you will stay for four nights. Local guide will be with you throughout your stay.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to Rome or Florence Airport; Flight to the region for Medjugorje; Private coach transfer (approximately 2 1/2 hours) to Medjugorje; Meet fellow pilgrims, spiritual leader, and host family/inn

tourDays.title: Medjugorje pilgrimage activities
tourDays.description: Experience the village of Medjugorje. Activities include daily English-language Mass at St. James Church, walking Apparition Hill, praying at the cross that commemorates the first apparition, evening rosary and Croatian Mass with Blessing of the Sick and blessing of personal items, and visits such as climbing Krizevac Mountain, visiting Blue Cross and the community Cenacolo. Meetings with the visionaries may be arranged if available.
tourDays.activities: English-language Mass at St. James Church; Walk up Apparition Hill and pray at the commemorative cross; Join evening rosary and Croatian Mass with Blessing of the Sick and blessing of items; Possible meetings with visionaries (pending availability); Climb Krizevac Mountain; Visit Blue Cross; Visit the community of Cenacolo

tourDays.title: Medjugorje pilgrimage activities
tourDays.description: Continuation of Medjugorje activities: daily Mass at St. James Church, Apparition Hill, evening rosary and Croatian Mass with Blessing of the Sick, opportunities to meet visionaries if available, climb Krizevac, visit Blue Cross and the community Cenacolo.
tourDays.activities: English-language Mass at St. James Church; Walk Apparition Hill and pray at the cross; Evening rosary and Croatian Mass with Blessing of the Sick; Meetings with visionaries (pending availability); Climb Krizevac Mountain; Visit Blue Cross and Community Cenacolo

tourDays.title: Medjugorje pilgrimage activities
tourDays.description: Final full day in Medjugorje with the same opportunities: daily English Mass, Apparition Hill, evening rosary and Croatian Mass (Blessing of the Sick and blessing of items), possible meetings with visionaries, climb Krizevac, visit Blue Cross and the community Cenacolo.
tourDays.activities: English-language Mass at St. James Church; Walk Apparition Hill and pray at the cross; Evening rosary and Croatian Mass with Blessing of the Sick; Possible meetings with the visionaries (pending availability); Climb Krizevac Mountain; Visit Blue Cross and Community Cenacolo

tourDays.title: Return to USA
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast and farewells, depart by motor coach for Dubrovnik Airport (or Split or Sarajevo) for return flights home.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast and farewells; Motor coach transfer to Dubrovnik Airport (or Split or Sarajevo); Return flights to USA

tourDays.title: Depart for Jordan
tourDays.description: Depart from your local airport on an overnight flight to Jordan. Meals served on board.
tourDays.activities: Board overnight flight; In-flight meals

tourDays.title: Arrive Amman
tourDays.description: Arrive in Amman, collect luggage, meet the tour guide/driver, transfer to the hotel, check in and enjoy dinner at the hotel.
tourDays.activities: Arrival procedures (baggage claim, meet guide); Transfer to hotel; Hotel check-in; Dinner at hotel

tourDays.title: Amman â Mt. Nebo - Madaba - Um Rassas â Mukawir - Amman
tourDays.description: Visit Mt. Nebo (site associated with Moses), the city of Madaba and St. George's Church with its ancient map, the Archaeological Park, Um Rassas with Byzantine mosaics, and Mukawir (Herodian fortress). Return to Amman for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Mt. Nebo; Tour St. George's Church, Madaba; Visit Archaeological Park; See Um Rassas mosaics; Stop at Mukawir (Herodian fortress)

tourDays.title: Amman â Um Qaiss - Tel Mar Elias â Anjara - Amman
tourDays.description: Travel north to Umm Qais to view ancient remains and panoramic vistas, visit Tel Mar Elias (associated with Elijah), then Anjara to see the shrine to Our Lady of the Mountain. Return to Amman for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Umm Qais; Visit Tel Mar Elias; Visit Anjara shrine

tourDays.title: Amman â Jabbok River - Jerash - Amman
tourDays.description: Drive to the Jabbok River for reflection, then explore Jerashâits colonnaded streets, temples, theaters and other well-preserved Roman ruins. Return to Amman.
tourDays.activities: Reflection at Jabbok River; Sightseeing in Jerash (Roman ruins)

tourDays.title: Amman - Petra â Amman
tourDays.description: Transfer to Petra for a walking tour through the Siq to Petra's carved structures, visit the Petra Museum, then afternoon at leisure before returning to Amman.
tourDays.activities: Walking tour of Petra (Siq and monuments); Visit Petra Museum; Free afternoon for shopping/leisure

tourDays.title: Amman â Kerak - Amman
tourDays.description: Drive to the Crusader castle of Kerak (Karak) to explore tunnels, chambers and stables, then return to Amman for a city tour including the citadel and Roman amphitheater.
tourDays.activities: Visit Kerak castle; Explore citadel and Roman amphitheater in Amman

tourDays.title: Amman - Bethany Beyond the Jordan - Dead Sea - Amman
tourDays.description: Visit the Baptism Site (Bethany Beyond the Jordan â Tell Al-Kharrar and churches of St. John the Baptist), then stop at the Dead Sea with time, weather permitting, to float. Return to Amman for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Bethany Beyond the Jordan (baptism site); See Roman and Byzantine remains and churches; Float or swim in the Dead Sea (time/weather permitting)

tourDays.title: Amman - Tel Aviv
