tourDays.activities: Drive to border and cross into Israel; Transfer to Tel Aviv

tourDays.title: Tel Aviv - Caesarea - Nazareth - Cana - Tiberias
tourDays.description: Depart Tel Aviv to Caesarea MarÃ­tima to see the Roman theater, Herod's Palace, hippodrome and harbor; visit Haifa (Mount Carmel) Carmelite Shrine; continue to Nazareth to visit the Church of the Annunciation, St. Joseph's Church and the Grotto, celebrate Mass; visit Cana (Wedding Church) where married couples may renew vows; continue to Tiberias on the Sea of Galilee.
tourDays.activities: Sightseeing in Caesarea MarÃ­tima; Visit Carmelite Shrine on Mount Carmel; Visit Church of the Annunciation and St. Joseph's Church in Nazareth; Celebrate Mass in Nazareth; Visit Wedding Church in Cana (renew vows for married couples); Transfer to Tiberias

tourDays.title: Tiberias: Sea of Galilee
tourDays.description: Boat ride on the Sea of Galilee, visit Capernaum (synagogue), Mount of Beatitudes, Tabgha (site of the multiplication of loaves and fishes), St. Peter's Primacy, and Magdala (Mary Magdalene's birthplace). Return to hotel in Tiberias.
tourDays.activities: Boat ride on the Sea of Galilee; Visit Capernaum and its synagogue; Visit Mount of Beatitudes; Visit Tabgha and St. Peter's Primacy; Visit Magdala

tourDays.title: Mt. Tabor - Jericho - Jerusalem
tourDays.description: Drive to Mount Tabor (site of the Transfiguration), celebrate Mass at the Basilica of the Transfiguration, then continue to Jericho to view the Mount of Temptation, and drive up to Jerusalem to check in to the hotel.
tourDays.activities: Visit Mount Tabor; Celebrate Mass at the Basilica of the Transfiguration; Visit Jericho and view Mount of Temptation; Transfer to Jerusalem and hotel check-in

tourDays.title: Jerusalem: Bethlehem & Ein Karem
tourDays.description: Visit Ein Karem (Church of St. John the Baptist and Church of the Visitation), then Bethlehem to see the fields of the shepherds, Manger Square and the Church of the Nativity; descend to the Grotto of the Nativity and attend Mass in Bethlehem before returning to the hotel in Jerusalem.
tourDays.activities: Visit Church of St. John the Baptist in Ein Karem; Visit Church of the Visitation; Visit fields near Bethlehem and Manger Square; Enter Church of the Nativity and Grotto of the Nativity; Celebrate Mass in Bethlehem

tourDays.title: Jordan River - Qumran - Dead Sea
tourDays.description: Drive through the Judean wilderness to the Jordan River for reflection on the Baptism of Christ, visit Qumran where the Dead Sea Scrolls were found, and have time to swim or float in the Dead Sea before returning to Jerusalem.
tourDays.activities: Reflection at the Jordan River (Baptism site); Visit Qumran (Dead Sea Scrolls site); Swim or float in the Dead Sea (time permitting)

tourDays.title: Jerusalem: Mt. Of Olives - Gethsemane - Mt. Zion (Upper Room)
tourDays.description: Visit the Mount of Olives for panoramic views, Pater Noster Shrine, Dominus Flevit, Gethsemane and the Church of All Nations (Rock of Agony), then visit the Western Wall, Church of St. Peter in Gallicantu (Caiaphas' house), the Upper Room on Mount Zion and the Benedictine Church of the Dormition. Return to hotel.
tourDays.activities: Panoramic view from Mount of Olives; Visit Pater Noster Shrine and Dominus Flevit; Visit Gethsemane and Church of All Nations; Visit Western Wall; Visit Church of St. Peter in Gallicantu; Visit Upper Room (Mount Zion); Visit Benedictine Church of the Dormition

tourDays.title: Jerusalem: Via Dolorosa - Holy Sepulchre - Western Wall
tourDays.description: Very early prayerful procession along the Via Dolorosa starting at the Antonia Fortress and ending at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre; celebrate Mass at the Holy Sepulchre, return to hotel for breakfast, then revisit the Old City to see the Church of St. Anne and Pool of Bethesda and conclude with a visit to the Western Wall.
tourDays.activities: Walk the Via Dolorosa in procession; Visit Antonia Fortress; Attend Mass at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre; Visit Church of St. Anne and Pool of Bethesda; Visit Western Wall

tourDays.title: Return Flights Home
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast, transfer to the Tel Aviv airport for return flights home.
tourDays.activities: Hotel checkout; Transfer to Tel Aviv airport; Board return flights

tourDays.title: Depart for Barcelona
tourDays.description: Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Travel to local airport; Board overnight flight(s)

tourDays.title: Arrive in Barcelona
tourDays.description: Upon arrival in Barcelona, collect your luggage in the baggage claim area and continue to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. Make your way to the vehicle for your transfer to your hotel. Upon arrival, check-in and have free time to rest, refresh, or explore. This evening, enjoy a welcome dinner, followed by an overnight in Barcelona.
tourDays.activities: Collect luggage; Transfer to hotel; Hotel check-in; Free time to rest or explore; Welcome dinner

tourDays.title: Barcelona - Manresa - Montserrat
tourDays.description: This morning, your day will begin with breakfast and a sightseeing tour of Barcelona including panoramic views of the Port of Barcelona, Montjuic, Plaza de EspaÃ±a, and Plaza de Catalunya. Continue with a guided walk through the Gothic Quarter and visit the Cathedral of Barcelona and La Sagrada Familia. In the afternoon travel to Manresa to visit the Sanctuary of Saint Ignatius of Loyola and the Holy Cave, then continue to Montserrat, home to the miraculous Black Madonna. Arrive in time for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Sightseeing tour of Barcelona; Guided walk through the Gothic Quarter; Visit Cathedral of Barcelona; Visit La Sagrada Familia; Visit Sanctuary of Saint Ignatius of Loyola and the Holy Cave in Manresa; Travel to Montserrat

tourDays.title: Montserrat
tourDays.description: After breakfast, visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Montserrat, located on a rugged mountainside. Learn about the tradition of the Black Madonna and the history of the monastery. Dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Shrine of Our Lady of Montserrat; Learn about the Black Madonna and monastery history

tourDays.title: Montserrat - Zaragoza - Madrid
tourDays.description: Following breakfast, depart for Zaragoza. In Zaragoza visit the Basilica del Pilar and La Seo Cathedral, and enjoy a walking tour of the city exploring local folklore and gastronomy. In the evening continue to Madrid for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart Montserrat for Zaragoza; Visit Basilica del Pilar; Visit La Seo Cathedral; Walking tour of Zaragoza; Travel to Madrid

tourDays.title: Madrid & Toledo
tourDays.description: After breakfast, tour Madrid including visits to the Royal Palace and Plaza Mayor. Then visit Toledo to see its historic churches, synagogues, mosques, and landmarks such as the Church of Santo TomÃ©, the TrÃ¡nsito Synagogue, Santa MarÃ­a la Blanca, and San Juan de los Reyes. Return to Madrid for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Tour Madrid (Royal Palace, Plaza Mayor); Visit Toledo and its historic sites; Return to Madrid

tourDays.title: Madrid - Astorga - O' Cebreiro - Santiago de Compostela
tourDays.description: Depart Madrid and head toward Santiago de Compostela. Stop in Astorga to visit the Bishopâs Palace by Gaudi and the Museum of El Camino. Enter Galicia via Lugo and stop in O' Cebreiro to view palooza-style houses and the site of a Eucharistic Miracle. In the evening proceed to Santiago de Compostela for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart Madrid; Visit Bishop's Palace in Astorga and Museum of El Camino; Enter Galicia via Lugo; Visit O' Cebreiro (view houses and Eucharistic Miracle site); Proceed to Santiago de Compostela

tourDays.title: Santiago de Compostela
tourDays.description: Walk a few miles of El Camino, experience the scenery and eucalyptus groves. Join in celebrating the International Pilgrim Mass at the Cathedral of St. James, then visit the Cathedral (including the crypt with the relics of St. James). Enjoy a sightseeing tour of the city with stops such as Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, Gelmirez Palace, and Franco Street. Evening at leisure until dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Walk part of El Camino; Celebrate International Pilgrim Mass at Cathedral of St. James; Visit Cathedral of St. James and descend into the crypt; Sightseeing tour of Santiago (Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, Gelmirez Palace, Franco Street); Free time

tourDays.title: Santiago de Compostela â Rome
tourDays.description: Breakfast at the hotel, transfer to Santiago Airport for flight to Rome. Upon arrival in Rome, collect luggage, transfer to hotel and check-in. Between 3:00 PM and 3:30 PM meet in the hotel lobby for a "Meet and Greet" with fellow pilgrims and depart for Mass. Attend a welcome dinner. After dinner, there is an optional walk to St. Peterâs Square to pray the Rosary.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Transfer to Santiago Airport; Fly to Rome; Collect luggage and transfer to hotel; Meet and Greet with fellow pilgrims; Attend Mass; Welcome dinner; Optional walk to St. Peter's Square to pray the Rosary

tourDays.title: Rome: Papal Audience and Major Basilicas
tourDays.description: After breakfast attend the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square (pending the papal schedule). Free time for lunch/shopping. Visit the Basilica of St. John the Lateran, the Holy Staircase (traditionally from Pontius Pilate's palace), and the Basilica of St. Mary Major. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Attend Papal Audience in St. Peter's Square; Free time for lunch and shopping; Visit Basilica of St. John the Lateran; Visit Holy Staircase; Visit Basilica of St. Mary Major

tourDays.title: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica, Vatican Museum and Ancient Rome
tourDays.description: Early breakfast then visit St. Peterâs Basilica to view Michelangeloâs Pieta. Proceed to the Vatican Museum (Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, Last Judgment) and the tomb of Saint John Paul II. Free time in Piazza Navona area. Travel the Appian Way to see Domino Quo Vadis Chapel, Baths of Caracalla, Arch of Drusus, Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and the catacombs of St. Callixtus. Conclude with a visit to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls and dinner at a local restaurant.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast; Visit St. Peter's Basilica and view Michelangelo's Pieta; Tour Vatican Museum (Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, Last Judgment); Visit tomb of Saint John Paul II; Free time at Piazza Navona; Visit Appian Way sites (Quo Vadis Chapel, Baths of Caracalla, Arch of Drusus, Tomb of Cecilia Metella, Catacombs of St. Callixtus); Visit Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls; Dinner at local restaurant

tourDays.title: Rome - Montecassino - San Giovanni Rotondo
tourDays.description: Board the bus and enjoy a scenic drive to Montecassino. Tour the principal monastery of the Benedictine Order founded by Saint Benedict, with time for the gift shop. Continue toward San Giovanni Rotondo, check in, enjoy dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Scenic bus drive to Montecassino; Tour Montecassino monastery; Visit gift shop; Travel to San Giovanni Rotondo; Hotel check-in and dinner

tourDays.title: San Giovanni Rotondo - Monte Sant' Angelo
tourDays.description: After breakfast visit the Old Church and celebrate Holy Mass. Tour the sanctuary, see the crucifix where St. Pio received the stigmata, and visit the confessional used by Padre Pio. Travel along the Gargano Peninsula to the Grotto of St. Michael the Archangel (Monte Sant' Angelo), visit the grotto and enjoy free time. Return to San Giovanni Rotondo for devotion, dinner and overnight. From MayâOctober pilgrims may attend the weekly Candlelight Procession at the Sanctuary of St. Pio after dinner at 9:00 PM.
tourDays.activities: Visit Old Church; Celebrate Holy Mass; Tour sanctuary and view crucifix (St. Pio's stigmata site); Visit Padre Pio's confessional; Bus travel along Gargano Peninsula; Visit Grotto of St. Michael the Archangel (Monte Sant' Angelo); Free time; Devotion and reflection; Optional Candlelight Procession (MayâOctober)

tourDays.title: San Giovanni Rotondo - Lanciano - Loreto - Assisi
tourDays.description: Leave for Assisi with stops in Lanciano for a private Mass at the Church of Saint Francis (site of an 8th-century Eucharistic Miracle) and then to the Marian shrine of Loreto to visit the Holy House of Nazareth and the Madonna of Loreto. End the day in Assisi with dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart San Giovanni Rotondo for Lanciano; Private Mass at the Church of Saint Francis (Lanciano); Visit Eucharistic Miracle site; Visit Holy House of Nazareth in Loreto and Madonna of Loreto; Travel to Assisi

tourDays.title: Assisi
tourDays.description: Tour Assisi beginning at the Basilica of St. Francis to visit his tomb and frescoes. Continue with a walking tour including the birthplace of St. Francis, visit the Santuario Della Spogliazione where St. Carlo Acutis is entombed, and the Church honoring St. Clare. After lunch, board the bus to the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels to visit the Porziuncola and the Capella del Transito, the Rose Garden and the cave where St. Francis prayed. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Basilica of St. Francis and tomb; View frescoes and Saint's possessions; Walking tour of Assisi (birthplace of St. Francis); Visit Santuario Della Spogliazione (tomb of St. Carlo Acutis); Visit Church of St. Clare; Visit Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels (Porziuncola, Capella del Transito); Visit Rose Garden and St. Francis' prayer cave

tourDays.title: Assisi - Orvieto - Assisi
tourDays.description: Ride through the Umbrian mountains to Orvieto. Visit Orvieto, including its renowned Cathedral, then return to Assisi for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Bus ride through Umbrian mountains; Visit Orvieto and Orvieto Cathedral; Return to Assisi

tourDays.title: Return Home
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast and farewells, head to Rome Fiumicino airport for return flight(s) home.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast; Transfer to Rome Fiumicino airport; Depart on return flight(s)

tourDays.title: Depart for the Holy Land Make your way to your local airport where you will board your overnight flight. Your meals are served on board.
tourDays.description:
Depart for the Holy Land
Make your way to your local airport where you will board your overnight flight. Your meals are served on board.

tourDays.title: Day 2
tourDays.description: Arrive in Tel Aviv Upon arrival at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, make your way to the baggage claim area and collect your luggage. Proceed to the arrivalâs hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. Transfer to your hotel in Tel Aviv in time to check-in. Enjoy dinner at the hotel before retiring for the evening.

tourDays.title: Day 3
tourDays.description: Caesarea - Haifa - Stella Maris - Nazareth - Tiberias - Cana Theme: The Annunciation Following breakfast, we will drive to Caesarea, the former capital of Judea. You will have the opportunity to visit the archaeological remains of this ancient port, which aided as base for the Herodian navy. Shortly after the time of Jesus Christ, it was revealed to Peter in Caesarea that the Good News (to repent) is not only intended for Jewish people, but also the entire world. This is the place which officially ended the tradition of adhering to the Jewish ceremonial laws. As a result, Peter baptized a group of gentiles, the Roman Centurion, Cornelius, and his family. Continue North to Haifa. In Haifa, you will find Stella Maris, a Carmelite Monastery. The monastery is located above the cave where Elijah, the prophet, once lived. A colorful painting of this âwonder-workerâ can be found on the ceiling of the Church. Following this visit, enjoy the scenic drive (with view of the bay of Acco) to Nazareth. In Nazareth you will experience the town where Mary once lived and where Jesus lived as a child (Matthew 2:23). During the visit to Nazareth we visit the church of the Annunciation which includes the church of St Joseph ( Itâs not Byzantine â itâs from 1914-21 built over Byzantine ruins) which tradition identifies it with the workshop of Joseph and the house of the Holy family. We will continue with a visit of the Church of the Incarnation, viewing at Grotto the remains of the house of the Blessed Virgin where the Angel appeared and announced the good news. Following Pilgrims path we visit Maryâs well, where often the Virgin Mary would have walked to draw water from the spring. The next stop will be to Cana where you will visit the Franciscan Wedding Church. Couples will have the opportunity to participate in the ceremony to renew their wedding vows. Your first day culminates with a transfer to Tiberias. Upon arrival in Tiberias, you will check-in to your hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 4
tourDays.description: Tiberias: Sea of Galilee Theme: The Ministry of Christ in the Galilee Today begin this day with breakfast at the hotel, followed by a boat ride on the beautiful and scenic Sea of Galilee (Luke 5:1). Upon docking the boat, you will have the opportunity to view the remains of a boat that dates back to the time of Jesus. Following the Sea of Galilee, we continue to the Mount of Beatitudes, where Jesus proclaimed His great Sermon on the Mount (Luke 6:20-49). Near the Mount, is Tabgha, one of Jesusâ miracle sites. At Tabgha, Jesus fed the crowd of 5,000 people from five loaves of bread and two fish (Luke 9:10-17). Also, in Tabgha is St. Peterâs Primacy where Jesus bestowed church leadership upon Peter (John 21:9). Continue to visit the birthplace of Mary Magdalene in Magdala. During the time of Jesus, this village was a prosperous fishing village that exported fish and garum (a fish sauce reduction; popular in Roman cooking). Your day concludes at Capernaum, the launching place of Jesusâ ministry. In Capernaum, see the Synagogue where Jesus taught (Mark 1:21-29) and gave His sermon on the Bread of Life. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 5
tourDays.description: Mt. Tabor - Jericho - Jerusalem Theme: The Transfiguration After breakfast, we will drive to the site of the Transfiguration, Mount Tabor (Matthew 17:1-50). At this site, you will have some time to reflect on Christâs Humanity and Divinity. Celebrate Mass at the Basilica of the Transfiguration. Continue south to the Jordan Valley to the oldest inhabited city in the world, Jericho (Joshua 6:12-25). In Jericho, you view the exact location, the Mount of Temptation, of where the Devil tempted Jesus during his forty-day fast (Luke 4:1). Following the view of the mountain, continue to Jesusâ baptismal site on the River Jordan (Matthew 3:13-17). After some time at the Jordan River, we will transfer to Jerusalem to check-in to your hotel and enjoy dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 6
tourDays.description: Jerusalem: Bethlehem & Ein Karem Theme: The Visitation and Nativity This morning, enjoy breakfast before we start our day in Jerusalem, which houses the temple to which Jesus was Presented (Luke 2:22). Visit a model of the Second Temple as it was in the time of Jesus. Following this visit, we will take a short drive to the village of Ein Karem, the birthplace of John the Baptist. It is known that there are two churches in Ein Karem, both representing the two homes of Zechariah and Elizabeth. The first is in a valley where the birth of St. John the Baptist is commemorated (Luke 1:39-80) in the Church of the Nativity of St. John the Baptist. The second is on a hill where Elizabeth spent five months in seclusion (Luke 1:24) at the Church of the Visitation. You will have a chance to visit both of these churches and have the opportunity to pray the Mystery of the Rosary as you walk up the hill to the Church of the Visitation. In the afternoon, transfer to Bethlehem, the birthplace of Jesus. In Bethlehem, you will have the opportunity to view the Shepherdâs Fields (Luke 2:8). In the caves of these fields, you are still able to see the soot marks of fires that shepherds lit to keep warm. The tour concludes at the Manger Square which stands in front of the Church of the Nativity. As you enter the Church, you will proceed down to the Grotto of the Nativity which marks the spot of Our Saviorâs birth (Matthew 2:1-18). Beneath the altar, there is a silver star and a Latin inscription that states: HIC DE VIRGINE MARIA JESUS CHRISTUS NATUS (Here Jesus Christ was born to the Virgin Mary). Following Mass in this Sacred space, return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 7
tourDays.description: Jordan River - Qumran - Dead Sea Theme: Early Years in Jerusalem & the Wilderness Following breakfast at your hotel, we will travel down the Jordan Valley to Qumran. Qumran is made up of 2,000 year old ruins from the days of the Second Temple and also the site where the Dead Sea Scrolls were written and discovered (Ezekial 47:8-10). These writings have helped further the understanding of Jewish background in Christianity. Time and weather permitting, you will have the opportunity to take a float in the Dead Sea, the lowest and saltiest spot on Earth. Continue as you travel through the Judean wilderness, the site where Jesus spent His 40 days of fasting. The day of touring culminates with a transfer to Bethany. Bethany is the site where Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead which foreshadows His own Resurrection (John 11:38-44). Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 8
tourDays.description: Jerusalem: Mt. Of Olives - Gethsemane - Mt. Zion - Western Wall Theme: Palm Sunday and the Agony in the Garden After breakfast, we will make our way to the Mount of Olives where you will be able to take in the beautiful, panoramic view of Jerusalem. Historically, the Mount of Olives was a mandatory transit point for Jesus during many iconic moments. Visit the Pater Noster Shrine where Jesus taught His disciples the Lordâs Prayer (Pater Noster) (Luke 11:1-4). You will have the opportunity to stop at Dominus Flevit which is a Church that commemorates where Jesus wept for Jerusalem (Luke 19:41). Continue on to Gethsemane, a garden at the foot of the Mount of Olives. Jesus brought His disciples here to pray the night before He was crucified (Luke 22:29-53). The Garden still contains trees with roots that date back to the time of Jesus. Your next stop, the Church of All Nations, built over the âRock of Agonyâ. This is where Jesus prayed alone on the night of His arrest. Throughout this time, you are invited to remain in prayer and to reflect on Christâs agony that He experienced. You will have the opportunity to visit the Western Wall, which is the last remnant of the Jewish Temple after it was destroyed in 70 A.D. Continue with a visit to the house of the High Priest Caiaphas (Church of St. Peter in Gallicantu). This Church commemorates where Jesus was examined and eventually imprisoned before the Council in Jerusalem. It also commemorates Peterâs Denial of Christ (John 18:15-18), Petersâ repentance, and Jesusâ forgiveness of Peter. You will also visit the Upper Room on Mt. Zion. The Upper Room is where Jesus and His disciples celebrated the Last Supper (Matthew 26:17-30) and where Jesus appeared to His disciples after His Death and Resurrection (Mark 16:14). In addition, visit the nearby Benedictine Church of the Dormition. Tradition tells us that this Church is where Mary, the Mother of Jesus, âfell asleep.â At the end of this prayerful day, return to your hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 9
tourDays.description: Jerusalem: Via Dolorosa - Holy Sepulchre- Western Wall Theme: The Way of the Cross, The Crucifixion, The Resurrection This morning you will have a very early wake-up to begin the Via Dolorosa (The Way of the Cross) at the Antonia Fortress. This is the spot where Jesus was condemned to death by Pontius Pilate (John 18:28-19:16). Following His condemnation, He was taken (on the Road to Calvary) to His place of Crucifixion. Reflect upon the Stations of the Cross as you travel through the markets of the Old City to the Church of the Holy Sepulcher (Luke 23:26-33). This sacred destination is the site of Calvary (Jesusâ crucifixion place) and His tomb (Luke 23: 50-55). Celebrate Mass at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. Following Mass, we will return to the hotel to enjoy breakfast. We will continue our day with a visit to the Church of St. Anneâs, the home of Jesusâ maternal grandparents (Anne and Joachim); and the Pool of Bethesda, where Jesus healed the crippled man (John 5:1-9). This afternoon, enjoy a revisit to the Old City. Following this visit return to the hotel to enjoy dinner and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 10
tourDays.description: Jerusalem - Lisbon Your journey to Lisbon begins with a departure for Tel Aviv Airport. Upon arrival, you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver and transferred to your hotel in time for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 11
tourDays.description: Lisbon - Santarem - Fatima After breakfast depart for Santarem, one of the oldest cities in the world. We will walk through its narrow streets to the Church of St. Stephen, containing the oldest recorded Eucharistic miracle. This miracle has been on continuous display since 1269 A.D. We will celebrate Mass at this holy site. We then continue on to Fatima, where the Blessed Mother appeared in 1917 to three simple shepherd children and exhorted mankind to pray for world peace. We arrive in time for dinner and retire for a restful evening.

tourDays.title: Day 12
tourDays.description: Fatima After breakfast, we begin our day celebrating Mass at the Little Chapel of the Apparitions. After Mass we begin our tour of Fatima where we will experience the beauty of this spiritual town. We will see the Basilica, the site of Francesco and Jacintaâs graves, the Hamlet of Aljustrel, where the children lived, and Valinhos, the site of Our Ladyâs appearance after the childrenâs return from prison. Experience Christâs love as you walk and follow the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra (The Sacred Way) culminating in the Chapel of Calvary, which overlooks all of Fatima. Join your prayers with those of pilgrims from around the world as you pray for the sick, drink water from the miraculous well. Attend the blessing of the sick and participate in nightly candlelight processions requested by Our Lady. Time for private devotions before dinner and a restful nightâs sleep.

tourDays.title: Day 13
tourDays.description: Fatima - Salamanca After a filling breakfast we depart towards the city of Salamanca. Salamanca is the most graceful city in Spain and for four centuries it was the seat of one of the most prestigious universities in the world. We will have a chance to see many of the cityâs sights including the grand Plaza Mayor, the hub of Salmantine life; the vast Baroque church of La Clerecia; the Casa de las Conchas (House of Shells), named after the rows of carved scallop shells symbol of the pilgrimage to Santiago which decorate its facade; the University; the cathedrals; the Roman Bridge; San Marcos and San Martin churches bridge; San Marcos and San Martin churches, and more. We will enjoy a delicious dinner in a local restaurant before continuing to our hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 14
tourDays.description: Salamanca - Alba de Tormes - Avila - Burgos After breakfast, we will depart to the quaint village of Alba de Tormes. Here we will visit and celebrate Mass at the Carmelite Monastery, where Saint Teresa died in 1582 A.D. and is buried. In the little museum of the Carmelite Monastery we will be able to see the incorrupt heart and left arm of the St. Teresa. We enjoy free time for lunch before we continue our journey to Avila. Two things distinguish Avila; the perfectly preserved eleventhcentury walls which surround the old town, and the mystic writer Santa Teresa, who was born here and whose shrines are a must see for all Catholic pilgrims! Avilaâs atmosphere has changed very little since the days of Santa Teresa, the first woman to be named a Doctor of the Church, to whom the city is dedicated. During our tour of Avila we will see the Cathedral and San Vicente church. We will visit the Incarnation Convent, where St. Teresa became a nun and home to the most comprehensive museum dedicated to her life. We also visit La Santa Monastery, built on the site of the house where she was born, and San Jose Convent, the first monastery founded by the Saint. After walking in the footsteps of St. Teresa we depart for Burgos, the historic capital of Old Castile. After dinner you will have free time to explore Burgos, and admire the magnificent limestone Cathedral.

tourDays.title: Day 15
tourDays.description:
Burgos - Loyola - Lourdes After breakfast, we depart Burgos for Loyola, the birthplace of St. Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits. Here, we will see the 17th-century Basilica dedicated to St. Ignatius. We will visit his family home which is behind the sanctuary. We will have time to pray at the most venerated room where Ignatius at age 30, was brought following his serious wounding at the Battle of Pamplona. After free time for lunch we motor through the spectacular Pyrenees Mountains. Nestled in the mountains stands picturesque Lourdes, the birthplace of St. Bernadette to whom Our Lady appeared in 1858 near the Grotto of Massabielle. We arrive in time for dinner at our hotel before retiring for a restful nightâs sleep.
Days 16 & 17: Lourdes Over the next two days, you will stay in a small town, nestled within the Pyrenees Mountains. During your time in Lourdes, you will pray and meditate in a site of Our Ladyâs apparitions. Our Lady first appeared to Bernadette in 1858, and announced herself as âThe Immaculate Conceptionâ, near the Grotto of Massabielle. During the first two apparitions, little Bernadette prayed the Rosary with Our Lady and left without any exchange of words. During the following apparitions, Our Lady emphasized Godâs love for us, penance, and the necessity of performing acts of penance for sinners. Throughout your time in Lourdes, you will have the opportunity to attend Mass at the Grotto, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette; watch a video presentation that explains in detail, the story of Lourdes; participate with the gesture of the miraculous spring ; Wash your hands, wash your face and drink the water. Finish with a short prayer: Our Lady of Lourdesâ¦Pray for us St. Bernadetteâ¦Pray for us Oh Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee Additionally, you will have the opportunity to experience Christâs unconditional love, as you meditate upon the âlife-sizeâ Stations of the Cross that overlook the Grotto of Massabielle. In Lourdes, you will walk in and meditate upon the footsteps of St. Bernadette. Your group will have the opportunity to see Boly Mill, the birthplace of St. Bernadette, and the âCachot,â an abandoned prison where Bernadetteâs impoverished family lived. Each evening following dinner, you will have an opportunity to attend the candlelight procession and the Rosary, before a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 18
tourDays.description: Lourdes - Rome Arrive Rome. Welcome to Rome, one of the most magnificent and interesting cities in the world, also known as the âEternal Cityâ! You will be transferred to your hotel. This afternoon our guide will introduce us to our fellow pilgrims and our priest who will be with us for the rest of the journey. We will make our way to Mass, followed by a welcome dinner with wine. This evening we will walk to St. Peterâs Square for Rosary (optional).

tourDays.title: Day 19
tourDays.description: Rome: Papal Audience - Piazza Navona - Basilica of St. John the Lateran and St. Mary Major - Holy Stairs Following breakfast, we will make our way to St. Peterâs Square to attend the Papal Audience, led by His Holiness, The Pope. (Papal Audience: Is scheduled to take place every Wednesday, pending the schedule of The Pope.) Following the audience, we will make our way to the Trevi Fountain built in the 15th Century to mark the ending destination of the Aqua Virgo â a man-made channel erected in 19 B.C or Piazza Navona where at the center: Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi âFountain of the Four Riversâ. After free time for lunch we will visit the Basilica of St. John the Lateran, the Popeâs Cathedral church where relics of both Peter and Paul remain under the main altar. It was here that The Pope was formally installed as Bishop of Rome. Next we cross the street to see the Holy Staircase which is believed to be a staircase from Pilateâs palace in Jerusalem and brought to Rome by St. Helen in the 4th century. Time permitting we may climb the steps on our knees in memory of Christâs Passion. Continue to the Basilica of St. Mary Major, the most important and the oldest church dedicated to Our Lady. St. Mary Major contains a relic from the Manger of the infant Jesus. We will celebrate Mass, and then make our way to dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 20
tourDays.description: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica - Vatican Museum - Appian Way - Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls - Catacombs Following breakfast, we will depart to celebrate Mass in the largest church in Christendom, St Peterâs Basilica, built on the site where St Peter was martyred. Unsurpassed in beauty, a monument to the long history of the Catholic Church, to which pilgrims come from around the world, St Peterâs is the grandest of the worldâs churches. Marvel Pieta and Berniniâs amazing bronze canopy. Following Mass, we will visit of the Vatican Museums, containing a group of the most impressive edifices with hundreds of galleries filled with art treasures. See awe-inspiring relics, and works of art donated throughout centuries as tributes of faith. Weâll cover The Tapestry Gallery, The Raphael Rooms and the most overwhelming Sistine Chapel, Michelangeloâs Masterpiece, restored mural of the Last Judgment. The tour ends as we make our way back into St. Peterâs Basilica. The Pope visited the tomb of St. Peter, following his elevation, for a visit of devotion that lasted 45 minutes. He is the first Pontiff to visit the necropolis since extensive archaeological excavations were conducted at the ancient site decades ago. We will also visit the tomb of Saint John Paul II located at the Vatican. There will be free time for lunch, and then we will continue on to visit St Paul. Outside the Walls. Continue our tour via the Appian Way â the oldest road from Roman timesâplus the famous Domino Quo Vadis Chapel; see the ancient Baths of Caracalla, Arch of Drusus; Tomb of Celilia Metella, and the catacombs of St Callixtus where the early Christians hid themselves to escape persecution. We will conclude our day and wonderful stay in Rome with dinner at a local restaurant in Rome.

tourDays.title: Day 21
tourDays.description: Rome - Montecassino - San Giovanni Rotondo Following breakfast, we will head south and cross through the Roman countryside with its villas and vineyards. During your drive, your tour escort will explain the spiritual, historical, and cultural overview of Italy, which will help to orient you to this beautiful country and prepare you for all that you will experience in the days to follow. We stop at Montecassino, a beautiful town founded by Saint Benedict in 529. Enjoy lunch and then continue through the countryside heading east to St. Padre Pioâs town, San Giovanni Rotondo, our base for the following two nights. Dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 22
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Monte Sant' Angel (View incorrupt body of St. Padre Pio) After celebrating Mass at the tomb of St. Padre Pio, we tour the sanctuary, see the old church and the crucifix from which he received the stigmata in 1918. You will see the confessional where St. Padre Pio spent innumerable hours with a multitude of pilgrims, directing them on their journey toward God. (We will have the opportunity to view and pray before the incorrupt body of St. Padre Pio.) Enjoy a breathtaking view of the Gargano Peninsula and a visit to the Grotto of Michael the Archangel. Six different popes, St Francis and at least four other saints have knelt in prayer at this grotto, seeking the protection of St Michael. Following lunch, take in the panoramic view of the ocean and the surrounding countryside awaits you at this most celebrated shrine of early Christianity, a shrine consecrated by St Michael himself in 490. Return to San Giovanni for devotions, reflection, and a restful overnight. *In the evening, you will have time to attend the weekly Candlelight Procession at the Sanctuary of St. Pio after dinner, at 9:00 PM. These processions are lit by candlelight, and guided by the Most Holy Rosary. Following this prayerful experience, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight. (May â October only).

tourDays.title: Day 23
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Lanciano - Loreto - Assisi After breakfast, you we leave for Assisi. On the way we stop in Lanciano for private Mass at the Convent/Church of Saint Francis built on top of the antique Church of St. Longinus â the site of a Eucharistic Miracle that occurred in the eighth century. At the time of the miracle, there was a Basilian monk, who struggled with the belief in the Real Presence in the Eucharist. During the time of Mass, the monk, with doubt in his voice, said the words of consecration and the bread and wine transformed into physical flesh and blood. Leave for Marian shrine of Loreto to visit the Holy House of Nazareth and the beautiful Madonna of Loreto. Tradition holds that this is the house in which Mary first prayed the Magnificat, in which Jesus grew to manhood, and in which the Holy Family lived, before it was transported several times by angels, to its current location. End the day in Assisi, hometown of St. Francis and St. Clare, with dinner and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 24
tourDays.description: Assisi (St. Francis) Today is a very special day, as we will spend a full day touring the home of the Saint that inspired our Holy Father. The Pope chose his name in admiration of the Saint of Nature and Servant to the Poor. Known for being a humble man himself, The Pope spent most of his life denying the luxuries of life, and preferring to live in simplicity and humility. Following breakfast, we will begin a tour of Assisi. Visit the tomb of St Francis. Explore the quaint hilltop birthplace of St Francis that still retains something of the atmosphere of the early 1200s, the period when St Francis began his ministry. Contained within the huge 13th-century Basilica are many of the saintâs possessions and a series of frescoes depicting his life. You may kneel before the crucifix from which Jesus spoke to St Francis, asking him to rebuild His church. It was in St Mary of the Angels Basilica where St Francis spent most of his life. Here we visit the Chapel, Portiuncola, the rose bush, and the cave where the saint retired for prayer. Stroll the medieval streets of the compact little town. You will have some free time to shop or eat lunch at an outdoor cafe with a view of an ancient Roman temple, we go to the Church of St. Clare to view the relics of St. Clare. The foundress of the Order of Poor Clares followed the teachings of St Francis by living a life of poverty and humility. We will visit these two saintsâ tombs before dinner and retiring for the evening.

tourDays.title: Day 25
tourDays.description: Assisi - Orvieto - Assisi This morning, you will ride through the beautiful Umbrian mountains to Orvieto. This incredible town sits on a volcanic high rock formation. Here we visit one of the most beautiful and most renowned Cathedrals in Italy. Because of its strategic location, itâs Christian history officially started in 1004, but Orvieto was built over preexisting Etruscan era cave tunnels dating back 2,500 years, which some historians believe Christians used to celebrate Mass when Christianity was forbidden. Return to Assisi for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 26
tourDays.description: Assisi - Siena - Florence Breakfast, followed by a scenic drive to the Tuscan city of Siena. This medieval city is the birthplace of St. Catherine âDoctor of the Churchâ, and the Apostle of Italy, St. Bernardine. Visit of the Basilica of St. Catherine (which is also known as the Basilica of St. Domenico). St. Catherine passed a large part of her life inside the walls of this Basilica. It is here you will also view the incorrupt head of St. Catherine. After, we will visit the Shrine of St. Catherine, which occupies the site of her family home. Enjoy our walking tour through the Siena including a visit to its Cathedral (Duomo di Siena). We will conclude at one of Italyâs finest squares, the Piazza Del Campo, where you will be given free time to spend at your own leisure. There are a number of restaurants surrounding the square to have lunch, as well as shops for gifts and souvenirs. Continuing to Florence. Upon arrival in Florence, you will notice immediately that it is the land for art lovers. Some of the most world renowned artists are from Florence such as, Dante, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, Botticelli, Donatello, and many others. Remainder of the afternoon, you will have the opportunity to explore the streets of Florence at leisure. In the evening gather for dinner, followed by an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 27
tourDays.description: Florence After breakfast, we are off to enjoy guided tour of Florence which includes magnificent Franciscan church of The Holy Cross or Santa Croce with the beautiful facade, church is a burial place of nobles, among which is Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli. Walking tour through Piazza Signoria, pass by Palazzo Vecchio, Uffizi and Ponte Vecchio. Continue through Republic Square to the Santa Maria del Fiore 13th century Cathedral. After lunch we will visit LâAccadamia where we will view Michelangeloâs âDavidâ as well as other works of art. You will have free time to explore the museum and city before we return to the Hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 28
tourDays.description: Florence - Padua After breakfast, we depart for Padua, where St. Anthony, patron saint of lost things is honored. We celebrate Mass at the Basilica built in his honor. Following Mass, begin our sightseeing tour including one of the oldest universities in Italy, the Tomb of St. Anthony and we have an opportunity to see several of his relics. We will pass by Pratto Della Valle, and see the Basilica of Santa Giustina. We arrive at our Hotel in time for dinner and a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 29
tourDays.description: Padua - Venice (Full Day Excursion) After breakfast, we depart for nearby Venice, where the streets are paved with water! We will enjoy a tour and visit to some of the greatest sights you will ever see: St. Markâs Square, The Golden Basilica of San Marco, the Bridge of Sighs, and we will even have an extraordinary visit of Dodgesâ Palace. After the tour you will have free time to explore Venice on own, shop and perhaps take a gondola ride. Donât forget to enjoy a cappuccino and gelato at one of the cafes in St. Markâs Square, a âmustâ for any visit to Venice. We will return to our Hotel in time for Dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 30
tourDays.description:
Venice - USA We will bid farewell to our new friends and to a Pilgrimage which will be in our memories and hearts for a long time to come. We depart for Venice Airport for our return flights home. We fondly say, Arrivederci Italia! *206 Tours Disclaimer: Occasionally local religious and national holidays, weather, traffic conditions and other events may necessitate changes in the sequence of events or the missing of certain events/places. Though every effort will be made to follow the itinerary, it should be considered as an indication, rather than a contract of events and places to be visited.

tourDays.title: Depart for Lisbon Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.description:
Depart for Lisbon
Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.

tourDays.title: Day 2
tourDays.description: Arrive in Lisbon Upon landing at Lisbon Airport, head to baggage claim and collect your luggage. Proceed to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. After meeting your group in the hotel lobby at 2:30 PM, board the bus and begin a panoramic sightseeing tour of Lisbon. We will stop at St. Jeromeâs Monastery, built to give thanks to the Virgin Mary for guiding Vasco da Gama on his voyage that linked Europe and Asia. Continue to drive by the Belem Quarter, which contains the iconic entryway to the Lisbon harbor, the Belem Tower. This important historic structure has many beautiful sculptures, such as depictions of St. Vincent and Our Lady of Safe Homecoming. The next stop is St. Anthonyâs Church, built upon the site of Saintâs birth; it is here that we will celebrate Mass. Although the patron Saint of lost things is known as St. Anthony of Padua (Italy), he was born in Lisbon, Portugal. This Church is built upon St. Anthonyâs birth site. After Mass, we will drive to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 3
tourDays.description: Lisbon - Santarem - Fatima Today, we will travel north to the old city of Santarem. We will attend Mass at the Church of St. Stephen, which holds a 13th-century Eucharistic Miracle. Continue to Fatima and visit the Hamlet of Aljustrel, the home of the three shepherd children. Visit the Parish Church and Fatima Parish Cemetery. Continue to your hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 4
tourDays.description: Fatima During your time in Fatima, pray at one of Our Blessed Motherâs apparition sites. Our Lady appeared to three shepherd children: Venerable Sister Lucia (age 10), St. Jacinta (age 7), and St. Francisco (age 9). These apparitions occurred monthly from May to October 1917. Historically, as the entire world was in turmoil, Our Ladyâs message was to pray for world peace. Our day begins with a visit to the Little Chapel of the Apparitions. This simple yet modern chapel is the site where the Virgin Mary first appeared on May 13, 1917. Continue with a visit to the stunning neoclassical church, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary. This Sacred space contains the tombs of St. Francisco, St. Jacinta, and Sister Lucia. View the monument that commemorates the Sacred Heart of Jesus in the square. The Basilica features fifteen altars dedicated to the fifteen mysteries of the Rosary. Visit the Museum and the Basilica of the Holy Trinity. After time for lunch, we will experience Our Lordâs unconditional love by participating in the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra. The âSacred Wayâ marks the path taken by the shepherd children of Fatima to their first apparition of the Virgin Mary. It is composed of fifteen small chapels in commemoration of the Passion of Our Lord. The fifteenth station, the Resurrection, is located near the Chapel of Calvary, dedicated to St. Stephen, King of Hungary. The day ends with a visit to Valinhos, the site of Our Ladyâs Apparition in August of 1917, as well as the first and third apparitions of the Angel. Your day concludes with private devotions and a candlelight procession, which Our Lady requested. Enjoy dinner and a comfortable nightâs rest in Fatima.

tourDays.title: Day 5
tourDays.description: Fatima - Salamanca Depart Fatima and head to Salamanca, following a full breakfast at the hotel. Salamanca is a city in the Castilla y Leon region and is known for its large University, the oldest in Spain that is still active, along with its prominent culture. Our walking tour will take us to several noteworthy sites in the city, including the grand Plaza Mayor, La Clerecia, and La Casa de las Conchas. See the University of Salamanca, which is the oldest University in Spain and the third oldest in Europe. Walk across the Roman Bridge, which extends along the River Tormes. See La Iglesia de San Marcos, which is constructed in the Romanesque style and contains breathtaking paintings that portray many scenes from the life of Our Lady. Say a prayer at La Iglesia de San Martin, a Church devoted to St. Martin of Tours, who is the patron saint of beggars and those most in need. Visit the inside of the two joint Salamanca Cathedrals (old and new), one of which is a Romanesque style and the other a Gothic style. Following this eventful day, you will return to your hotel for a delicious meal with your group and spend the night at your hotel in Salamanca.

tourDays.title: Day 6
tourDays.description: Salamanca - Alba de Tormes - Avila - Burgos This morning, after breakfast, you will board the bus and enjoy a short transfer to the village of Alba de Tormes. This town is home to the Carmelite Monastery that Saint Teresa founded in 1571. Upon arrival in Alba de Tormes, your group will celebrate Mass at this Monastery where the saint died and was buried. Visit the museum dedicated to St. Teresa of Avila, which also holds her incorrupt heart and left arm. Your group will enjoy free time for lunch on your own before continuing to the medieval city of Avila. Upon arrival, see the perfectly preserved eleventh-century walls that surround the old town. The conservation of architecture in this city, where St. Teresa was born, makes its shrines, convents, and churches necessary to visit on any Catholic pilgrimage. The Cathedral of Avila encompasses the Romanesque, Gothic, and Renaissance styles of its time within its artwork and architecture. La Basilica de San Vicente in Avila stands on the site of the martyrdom of St. Vincent. Visit the Incarnation Convent, where St. Teresa became a nun. Saint Teresa convinced Saint John of the Cross to reform the male Carmelite order, a reform she initiated when she met Saint John in Medina del Campo. After walking in the footsteps of St. Teresa, continue your journey to Burgos. Upon arrival in the historic capital of Old Castile, enjoy dinner. Following dinner, you will have the opportunity to explore the city of Burgos and admire its magnificent limestone Gothic-style cathedral. Late this evening, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 7
tourDays.description:
Burgos - Loyola - Lourdes Following breakfast, transfer from Burgos to Loyola to visit the birthplace of St. Ignatius, founder of the Jesuit Order. St. Ignatius dedicated himself to becoming a soldier of the Christian faith, and as a result of many tribulations, he wrote the ever-famous Spiritual Exercises. In Loyola, you will see the 17th-century Basilica dedicated to this remarkable Saint. The Basilica is part of a series of buildings that surround the âHoly House,â the birthplace of St. Ignatius. Pray in the very room where St. Ignatius prayed and began his conversion. After meditating on the life of this founder of the Jesuit Order, you will enjoy free time for lunch and board the bus for the next destination. We will continue to Lourdes with a spectacular view of the Pyrenees Mountains. Upon arrival in Lourdes, you will check in to your hotel and enjoy a splendid dinner, followed by a peaceful overnight stay.
Days 8 & 9: Lourdes Over the next two days, you will stay in a small town in the Pyrenees Mountains. During your time in Lourdes, you will pray and meditate at the site of Our Ladyâs apparitions. Our Lady first appeared to Bernadette in 1858 and announced herself as âThe Immaculate Conceptionâ near the Grotto of Massabielle. During the first two apparitions, little Bernadette prayed the Rosary with Our Lady and left without exchanging words. During the following apparitions, Our Lady emphasized Godâs love for us and the necessity of performing acts of penance for sinners. Throughout your time in Lourdes, you will have the opportunity to attend Mass at the Grotto, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette. Watch a video presentation that explains the story of Lourdes. Wash your hands, wash your face, and drink the water of the miraculous spring. Finish with a short prayer: âOur Lady of Lourdes, pray for us. St. Bernadette, pray for us. O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.â Experience Christâs unconditional love as you meditate upon the âlife-sizeâ Stations of the Cross that overlook the Grotto of Massabielle. In Lourdes, you will walk in and meditate upon the footsteps of St. Bernadette. Your group will have the opportunity to see Boly Mill, the birthplace of St. Bernadette, and the âCachot,â an abandoned prison where Bernadetteâs impoverished family lived. Each evening, following dinner, you can attend the candlelight procession and pray the Rosary before a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 10
tourDays.description: Lourdes - Paris - Lisieux (St. Therese - the Little Flower) Today, you will enjoy breakfast before departing for Pau or Lourdes Airport for your short flight to Paris, continue on to Lisieux. According to Pope Pius X, St. Therese of Lisieux was the âgreatest saint of modern times.â Her extraordinary love for God and service to humanity will come alive as you walk in the great Saintâs footsteps. During your visit, you will see the beautiful Basilica of St. Therese and its magnificent mosaics and stained glass windows. You will have the opportunity to view relics, clothing, and personal objects that belonged to St. Therese when you visit her family home, Les Buissonnets. Additionally, you will tour the Carmelite Convent, which she entered in 1888 and where she is now buried. Dinner and overnight at your hotel in Lisieux.

tourDays.title: Day 11
tourDays.description: Lisieux - Landing Beaches - American Cemetery - Lisieux Upon waking up in Lisieux, enjoy breakfast, and then your group will celebrate Mass. After Mass we will travel to the Normandy Landing beaches. The Normandy landings were the landing operations, which took place on Tuesday, June 6, 1944 (termed D-Day) by the Allies of Normandy during World War II. As the largest seaborne invasion in history, the operation began the liberation of German-occupied northwestern Europe from Nazi control and contributed to the Alliesâ victory on the Western Front. Continue to visit The Normandy American Cemetery and Memorial, a World War II cemetery and memorial in Colleville-Sur-Mer, Normandy, France, honoring the American troops that died in Europe during World War II. Many of the brave American soldiers of World War II are buried here, and it is encouraged to say a prayer in thanksgiving for their courage. Return to Lisieux for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 12
tourDays.description: Lisieux - Chartres - Paris This morning, your day begins with an early breakfast before we depart for Chartres, known worldwide for its massive Cathedral Notre Dame and its incredible stained-glass windows from the 12th and 13th centuries. The World Heritage site, UNESCO, calls the Cathedral âthe high point of French Gothic artâ and a âmasterpieceâ. Pilgrims will also be able to venerate a precious relic of the Veil of Our Lady which is currently on display at the back of the main altar of the Cathedral of Chartres. You will have some free time for lunch in the quaint town of Chartres. After lunch, we will continue to Paris to check-in at your hotel, followed by some free time before a delicious dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 13
tourDays.description: Paris â Miraculous Medal â Notre Dame Cathedral Following breakfast, we will celebrate Mass. Following Mass enjoy a full day of sightseeing including the magnificent Sacre Coeur Basilica atop Montmartre Hill. The Basilica, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, was originally built in 1914 as an act of penance for infidelity that France experienced during that time. See the beautiful mosaic of the Risen Christ and the remarkable Grand Organ. Visit the the Tombs of many notable Cardinals. Time permitting, you may have the opportunity to ascend a staircase to the Dome, where you will take in a breathtaking panoramic view of Paris. Continue with a visit of the Chapel of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal, where we will have the opportunity to view the incorrupt body of St. Catherine Laboure. The Saintâs guardian angel led her to the chapel where the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared to her. During the apparitions, Our Lady repeatedly instructed the making and purpose of the Miraculous Medal. According to the Blessed Virgin Mary, those who wear the Miraculous Medal will receive special protection and abundant graces. Following this prayerful and reflective experience, we will walk to Saint Vincent de Paul Church. Next, on our tour of Paris, we will visit one of the most incredible churches in the world: Notre Dame Cathedral. The Cathedral has recently been re-opened to visitors. Guided group tours are scheduled to resume in June 2025. Board a bus tour and see some of the most recognizable symbols of Paris, including the Eiffel Tower, the Invalides, the LâArch de Triomphe, and the Champ-Elysees, the worldâs most famous boulevard. Your busy day ends with a lovely meal and a comfortable overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 14
tourDays.description: Paris - Rome Following breakfast at your hotel, your group will transfer to the Charles de Gaulle Airport and board your flight to Rome. Upon arrival at Rome airport, collect your luggage in the baggage claim area and continue to the arrivals hall, where you will be greeted by a tour escort and/or driver. You will make your way to the bus and transfer to your hotel. Following check-in, you will have free time to unpack, relax, or explore Rome on your own. Your tour escort may suggest places to visit. Later in the afternoon, your group will meet in the hotel lobby for a âMeet and Greetâ with your fellow pilgrims and depart for Mass. Following Mass, you will attend a welcome dinner. After dinner, you can walk to St. Peterâs Square as a group for the Rosary (optional).

tourDays.title: Day 15
tourDays.description: Rome: Papal Audience - Basilica of St. John the Lateran - Holy Stairs - Basilica of St. Mary Major After a nice breakfast at your hotel, your first sightseeing day in Rome starts! The tour begins with the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square! The Audience is celebrated each Wednesday by His Holiness, The Pope (pending the papal schedule). Following the Audience, there will be free time for lunch, shopping, or to mail a postcard from the Vatican Post Office. This afternoon, you will visit the oldest of the four major Basilicas in Rome: St. John the Lateran. This Basilica is home to the relics of Peter and Paul. It is also where the Pope is installed as Bishop of Rome and officiates as the Bishop of Rome. Next, we will cross the street to visit the Holy Staircase. Tradition states that this Staircase is from Pontius Pilateâs palace in Jerusalem during the time of Jesus. It was brought to Rome by St. Helen in the 4th century. If time permits, you may climb the steps on your knees while reflecting on Christâs agonizing Passion. We will proceed to the Basilica of St. Mary Major to end our day. This Basilica contains a relic from the Manger of the Infant Jesus. Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 16
tourDays.description: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica - Vatican Museum - Appian Way - Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls - Catacombs Enjoy an early breakfast before going to the largest Church in Christendom, St. Peterâs Basilica. This Basilica was built on the site where St. Peter, the first Pope and Bishop of Rome, was martyred. Inside the Basilica, you will view Michelangeloâs Pieta. This stunning marble sculpture depicts the Virgin Mary holding Christ after His crucifixion, death, and removal from the cross before being placed in the tomb. Continue to proceed to the Vatican Museum. The world-renowned museum displays an impressive display of edifices, galleries, and awe-inspiring relics. Observe the Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, and the restored mural of the Last Judgment. The final stop on your Vatican tour is at the tomb of Saint John Paul II. Next, head to the Piazza Navona area for some free time and lunch (on your own). Continue on your short journey down the Appian Way, the earliest road of Ancient Rome. This road leads to the Domino Quo Vadis Chapel, the Baths of Caracalla, the Arch of Drusus, the Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and the catacombs of St. Callixtus. The day concludes with a visit to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls. Originally founded by Emperor Constantine in the 4th century, this Basilica is the burial place of Saint Paul the Apostle. We will make our way to a local restaurant for dinner. Following dinner, feel free to explore the streets of Rome or return to the hotel for the night.

tourDays.title: Day 17
tourDays.description: Rome - Montecassino - San Giovanni Rotondo Following breakfast, you will board your bus to enjoy the scenic route to Montecassino, passing through the Roman countryside, known for its villas and vineyards. During the bus ride, your tour escort will share interesting information regarding Italyâs spiritual, historical, and cultural history. Montecassino, the principal monastery of the Benedictine Order, was founded by Saint Benedict around 530 A.D. Following the tour, we can visit the gift shop before we board the bus to continue toward San Giovanni Rotondo, the hometown of Saint St. Padre Pio. Upon arrival in San Giovanni Rotondo, enjoy dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 18
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Monte Sant' Angelo This morning, after breakfast, we will visit the Old Church. After Mass, we will tour the sanctuary. View the crucifix, in front of which St. Pio received the stigmata. Visit the confessional where St. Pio spent innumerable hours listening to confessions. Next, we will board the bus and travel along the beautiful Gargano Peninsula to the Grotto of St. Michael the Archangel, a shrine consecrated by St. Michael. At this Grotto, St. Michael appeared to a Bishop to assure him that his diocese would not destroyed. Following the visit to the Grotto, enjoy free time. On the way back to San Giovanni Rotondo, view breathtaking ocean views. Upon arrival, you will have time for devotion and reflection. Dinner and overnight. *Candlelight Procession: Between May and October, attend the weekly Candlelight Procession at the Sanctuary of St. Pio at 9:00 PM. These processions are lit by candlelight and are guided by the Most Holy Rosary. Following this prayerful experience, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 19
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Lanciano - Loreto - Assisi After breakfast, we will depart for Assisi. On the way, we will stop in Lanciano for private Mass at the Convent/Church of Saint Francis built on top of the antique Church of St. Longinus â the site of a Eucharistic Miracle that occurred in the eighth century. At the time of the miracle, there was a Basilian monk who struggled with the belief in the Real Presence in the Eucharist. During Mass, the monk, with doubt in his voice, said the words of consecration and was astonished as he saw the bread and wine transformed into Christâs physical flesh and blood. Leave for the Marian shrine of Loreto to visit the Holy House of Nazareth and the beautiful Madonna of Loreto. Tradition holds that this is the house where Mary first prayed the Magnificat, where Jesus grew to manhood, and the Holy Family lived. It was transported several times by angels to its current location. End the day in Assisi, hometown of St. Francis and St. Clare, with dinner and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 20
tourDays.description: Assisi Enjoy an early breakfast, followed by a full day of touring the hometown of St. Francis. St. Francis is the âPatron Saint of Animals and the Environment.â He is responsible for founding the Franciscan Order and has been an inspiration for centuries because of his simplicity and humility. The atmosphere of Assisi has not changed since St. Francis began his ministry in the early 13th century. We will start our tour at the Basilica of St. Francis, where we will visit the Saintâs tomb and view a series of frescoes depicting his life, as well as a few of the Saintâs possessions. From there, we will continue on a walking tour through this picturesque town, including the birthplace of St. Francis. Visit the Santuario Della Spogliazione where St. Carlo Acutis is entombed. Carlo is the first millennial to have been declared a Saint. He had a great love for Jesus in the Eucharist and died of leukemia at the young age of 15. Our tour ends at the Church that honors St. Clare, the foundress of the Poor Clare Sisters. This Saint followed the teachings of St. Francis very closely by also living a life of poverty and humility. Take some time on your own for additional prayer, shop in the many gift shops, or enjoy a nice lunch. After lunch, we will board the bus, which will take us outside of the walls of Assisi to the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels. This is where St. Francis spent most of life. This Basilica is made up of two structures, both of which you will visit. The first structure is the âPorziuncolaâ, which is where St. Francis founded his order of the Friar Minor (Franciscans). The second is the âCapella del Transitoâ, which is the place of St. Francisâ death. During your time here, you will have the opportunity to visit the beautiful Rose Garden where St. Francis and other friars lived, as well as the cave where the Saint retired to pray. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 21
tourDays.description: Assisi - Orvieto - Assisi This morning, you will ride through the beautiful Umbrian mountains to Orvieto. This incredible town sits on a volcanic high rock formation. Here we visit one of the most beautiful and most renowned Cathedrals in Italy. Because of its strategic location, itâs Christian history officially started in 1004, but Orvieto was built over preexisting Etruscan era cave tunnels dating back 2,500 years, which some historians believe Christians used to celebrate Mass when Christianity was forbidden. Return to Assisi for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 22
tourDays.description: Assisi - Siena - Florence Breakfast, followed by a scenic drive to the Tuscan city of Siena. This medieval city is the birthplace of St. Catherine, âDoctor of the Church,â and the Apostle of Italy, St. Bernardine. Visit the Basilica of St. Catherine (which is also known as the Basilica of St. Domenico). St. Catherine spent a large part of her life inside the walls of this Basilica. Here, you will also view the incorrupt head of St. Catherine. After, we will visit the Shrine of St. Catherine, which occupies the site of her family home. Enjoy our walking tour through the Siena, including a visit to its Cathedral (Duomo di Siena). We will conclude at one of Italyâs finest squares, the Piazza Del Campo, where you will be given free time to spend at your leisure. There are several restaurants surrounding the square where you can have lunch, as well as shops offering gifts and souvenirs. Continue to Florence, which is the land of art lovers. Some of the worldâs most renowned artists are from Florence, including Dante, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, Botticelli, Donatello, and many others. For the remainder of the afternoon, you may explore the streets of Florence at leisure. In the evening, gather for dinner, followed by an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 23
tourDays.description: Florence In Florence, your day begins with breakfast, followed by a guided tour. The tour starts at the Church of the Holy Cross, also known as Santa Croce, where many nobles are buried, including Michelangelo, Galileo, and Machiavelli. Continue to walk by Piazza Signorina, Palazzo Vecchio, Uffizi, Ponte Vecchio, and Republic Square to the Santa Maria del Fiore. This Cathedral is an iconic piece of architecture of the city of Florence, designed by Filippo Brunelleschi in the 13th century. Next, visit LâAccademia, the well-known art gallery. At this gallery, you will have the opportunity to view the work of artists such as Botticelli, Ghirlandaio, Pontormo, and the ever-famous sculpture by Michelangelo, David. This afternoon, you will have time to explore Florence on your own. Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 24
tourDays.description: Florence - Padua Following breakfast at your hotel, board the motor coach for your transfer to Padua. This Northern Italy city honors the âPatron Saint of Lost Things and Causes,â St. Anthony. You will begin a sightseeing tour of the city, including a view of one of the oldest Universities in Italy, the University of Padua, as well as the Basilica of Santa Giustina, the âPatron Saint of Padua.â The tour will conclude at the Basilica of St. Anthony, where you will have the opportunity to visit his tomb. Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 25
tourDays.description: Padua - Venice - Padua Today, you will have an early breakfast and then board your bus to depart for the magical city of Venice. After Mass, enjoy a walking tour that visits several notable sites. See St. Markâs Square, the largest square in the city and the site of many government buildings. View the Golden Basilica of San Marco, renowned for its magnificent mosaics that depict scenes from the Old and New Testaments of the Bible. See the romantic Bridge of Sigh, a bridge that will bring eternal love to those who drift below it. You will also have the chance to view the Dogesâ Palace (Dukeâs Palace), which served as the seat of the Government for the Republic of Venice for centuries. Return to Padua for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 26
tourDays.description:
Depart Venice to Medjugorje This morning, depart from Italy and head to Medjugorje. Upon arrival in either Dubrovnik, Split, or Sarajevo Airport, collect your luggage in the baggage claim area and continue to the arrival hall. You will be greeted by a tour guide and/or driver, who will take you on the 2.5-hour drive to the village of Medjugorje. Enjoy dinner before retiring for the evening.
Days 27 - 29: Medjugorje
The most beautiful features of Medjugorje are its simplicity and peace. A local guide will accompany your group throughout your stay in the village.
Some activities that will accompany you in your spiritual journey:
Attend Daily Mass: Each morning at 10:00 AM, your group will assemble at St. James Church for Mass (English-speaking). At the end of each Mass, regardless of language, there is a blessing of the religious articles that you have with you.
On Feast Days, and Sundays, English Mass is at 12 PM.
Climb Apparition Hill: This mountainous hill is where the visionaries first encountered Our Lady. At the base of this hill is a Blue Cross, where it is said Our Lady appeared to the children while they hid from the communist police in the early days of the alleged apparitions. While climbing, your group is invited to recite the Rosary, pausing five times for each decade. At the top of the hill, you will witness the exact location of the first alleged apparition of Our Lady to the visionaries. Enjoy private time for prayer.
Climb Mt. Krizevac (Cross Mountain): In 1933, the villagers built a 30â² high cross atop a mountain to commemorate Jesusâ passion and death on the cross. Your group will have the opportunity to climb this mountain and venerate that very cross. While climbing, your group is invited to pray the Stations of the Cross (to meditate on Jesusâ suffering on the Road to Calvary), pausing fifteen times for each Station.
Apparitions: Each evening at 5:00 PM (or 6:00 PM depending on Daylight Savings Time), your group can join the villagers and fellow pilgrims of Medjugorje at either St James Church or Apparition Hill to commemorate the time Our Lady appears to the Visionaries. There you can pray the Rosary, as you all await that time: 5:40 PM (or 6:40 PM during Daylight Savings Time).
*Afterward, Croatian Mass is held at St. James Church and all may attend. It is simultaneously broadcasted by radio in order to translate the services from Croatian into many languages. Following the Croatian Mass, there is a Blessing of the Sick. **For details about the Visionaries, please visit: http://www.206tours.com/visionaries

tourDays.title: Day 30
tourDays.description:
Medjugorje - Home After an early breakfast and heartfelt farewells, depart by motor coach for Dubrovnik, Split, or Sarajevo Airport for our return flight(s) home. *206 Tours Disclaimer: Occasionally local religious and national holidays, weather, traffic conditions and other events may necessitate changes in the sequence of events or the missing of certain events/places. Though every effort will be made to follow the itinerary, it should be considered as an indication, rather than a contract of events and places to be visited.
