tourDays.activities: Visit Chartres Cathedral; Venerate the Veil of Our Lady relic; Lunch in Chartres (free time); Transfer to Paris and hotel check-in

tourDays.title: Paris
tourDays.description: Celebrate Mass, then a full day of Paris sightseeing including SacrÃ©-CÅur (Montmartre), the Chapel of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal (view incorrupt body of St. Catherine Laboure), Saint Vincent de Paul Church, Notre Dame Cathedral, and a bus tour seeing the Eiffel Tower, Les Invalides, Arc de Triomphe and Champs-ÃlysÃ©es. Dinner and overnight in Paris.
tourDays.activities: Celebrate Mass in Paris; Visit SacrÃ©-CÅur Basilica; Visit Chapel of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal; View incorrupt body of St. Catherine Laboure; Visit Saint Vincent de Paul Church; Visit Notre Dame Cathedral; Bus tour of Paris landmarks (Eiffel Tower, Les Invalides, Arc de Triomphe, Champs-ÃlysÃ©es)

tourDays.title: Paris â Medjugorje
tourDays.description: Early morning transfer from Paris to board flights to Medjugorje. On arrival, meet guide/driver and take a roughly 2.5-hour drive to the village. Dinner and overnight in Medjugorje.
tourDays.activities: Early transfer to airport in Paris; Flight(s) to Medjugorje; Meet guide/driver on arrival; Drive to Medjugorje (approx. 2.5 hours); Hotel check-in

tourDays.title: Medjugorje â Pilgrimage Activities
tourDays.description: Begin stay in Medjugorje with spiritual activities guided by a local guide. Opportunities include Daily Mass at St. James Church, climbing Apparition Hill and Mt. Krizevac, attending evening apparition gatherings, adoration, visiting the Community of Cenacolo, and prayer at the Statue of the Risen Christ.
tourDays.activities: Attend Daily Mass at St. James Church; Climb Apparition Hill and pray the Rosary while ascending; Climb Mt. Krizevac (Cross Mountain) and pray Stations of the Cross; Attend evening apparition gathering at St. James Church or Apparition Hill; Visit Community of Cenacolo; Prayer at the Statue of the Risen Christ; Attend Croatian Mass and Blessing of the Sick (optional); Adoration of the Blessed Sacrament (where scheduled)

tourDays.title: Medjugorje â Pilgrimage Activities
tourDays.description: Continued time in Medjugorje with the same opportunities for Mass, climbing Apparition Hill and Cross Mountain, participating in evening apparitions, adoration, visiting Cenacolo, and private prayer.
tourDays.activities: Attend Daily Mass at St. James Church; Climb Apparition Hill; Climb Mt. Krizevac and venerate the cross; Attend evening apparition gathering; Visit Community of Cenacolo; Adoration and veneration opportunities; Prayer at the Statue of the Risen Christ

tourDays.title: Medjugorje â Pilgrimage Activities
tourDays.description: Final full day in Medjugorje with continued participation in Mass, climbs, evening devotion, adoration, Cenacolo visit, and time for personal prayer and sacramental opportunities.
tourDays.activities: Attend Daily Mass at St. James Church; Climb Apparition Hill and Mt. Krizevac (if not already done); Attend evening apparition gathering; Visit Community of Cenacolo; Adoration and veneration opportunities; Prayer at the Statue of the Risen Christ

tourDays.title: Return Home
tourDays.description: Early breakfast, farewells, and transfer to Dubrovnik, Split, or Sarajevo airport for return flights home.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast; Transfer to airport for return flights; Depart for home

tourDays.title: Depart for Madrid
tourDays.description: Make your way to your local airport where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Make way to local airport; Board overnight flight(s); Have meals served on board

tourDays.title: Arrival in Madrid
tourDays.description: Upon arrival in Madrid, collect your luggage and meet your tour guide and/or driver. Transfer by bus to the hotel. Free time before dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Collect luggage; Meet tour guide/driver; Transfer to hotel by bus; Free time; Dinner

tourDays.title: Sightseeing in Madrid and Toledo
tourDays.description: Morning tour of Madrid including the Royal Palace and Plaza Mayor. In the afternoon depart for Toledo to visit the Gothic Cathedral, La Iglesia de Santo Tome (housing El Grecoâs painting), the Sinagoga del TrÃ¡nsito, and several city gates and monuments. Return to Madrid for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Sightseeing tour of Madrid (Royal Palace, Plaza Mayor); Travel to Toledo; Visit Toledo Cathedral; Visit La Iglesia de Santo Tome; Visit Sinagoga del TrÃ¡nsito; See La Puerta de Bisagras, La Puerta del Cambron, La Puerta del Sol; Return transfer to Madrid

tourDays.title: Travel to Santiago de Compostela (stops en route)
tourDays.description: Depart Madrid for Santiago de Compostela with stops en route: Calle del Agua in Villafranca del Bierzo (Romanesque Church of Santiago), Collegiate Church of Santa Maria, Church of St. Nicolas. Enter Galicia via Lugo and stop at O Cebreiro to view palooza-style houses and the site of a Eucharistic Miracle (1300). Proceed to Santiago de Compostela for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Travel from Madrid to Santiago de Compostela; Stop at Calle del Agua (Villafranca del Bierzo); Visit Romanesque Church of Santiago; Visit Collegiate Church of Santa Maria; Visit Church of St. Nicolas; Stop in Lugo and O Cebreiro; view Eucharistic Miracle site

tourDays.title: El Camino finale and Cathedral visit
tourDays.description: Join walking pilgrims at Monte del Gozo, walk the last miles of El Camino and attend the International Pilgrim Mass at the Cathedral of St. James. Hug the statue of St. James and descend into the crypt containing the relics. Enjoy a sightseeing tour of Santiago (Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, Gemerez Palace, Franco Street). Evening at leisure, dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Walk from Monte del Gozo (last miles of El Camino); Attend International Pilgrim Mass at the Cathedral of St. James; Hug statue of St. James; Visit the crypt with relics of St. James; Sightseeing tour of Santiago (Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, Gemerez Palace, Franco Street)

tourDays.title: Fly to Croatia/Bosnia region and transfer to Medjugorje
tourDays.description: Transfer to the airport and board a flight to either Dubrovnik, Split, Zagreb, or Sarajevo. After landing, collect luggage and continue by vehicle on an approximately 2.5 hour drive to the village of Medjugorje. Group dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to airport; Board flight to Dubrovnik, Split, Zagreb, or Sarajevo; Collect luggage on arrival; Drive to Medjugorje; Group dinner

tourDays.title: Medjugorje spiritual program
tourDays.description: Stay in Medjugorje accompanied by a local guide. Participate in daily spiritual activities and visits around the village, including Mass, climbs of Apparition Hill and Mt. Krizevac, evening prayers for the apparitions, visits to the Community of Cenacolo, and prayer at the Statue of the Risen Christ.
tourDays.activities: Attend Daily Mass (English-speaking); Climb Apparition Hill and pray the Rosary; Climb Mt. Krizevac (Cross Mountain) and pray the Stations of the Cross; Join evening prayers/commemoration for the apparitions; Attend Croatian Mass and Blessing of the Sick (when held); Adore the Blessed Sacrament (when scheduled); Visit the Community of Cenacolo; Pray at the Statue of the Risen Christ; Attend Confessions in English at St. James Church (when available)

tourDays.title: Medjugorje spiritual program
tourDays.description: Continuation of Medjugorje activities with a local guide: Mass, climbs to Apparition Hill and Mt. Krizevac, participation in evening prayers for the apparitions, visit Community of Cenacolo, adoration and opportunities for confession and personal prayer.
tourDays.activities: Attend Daily Mass (English-speaking); Climb Apparition Hill and pray the Rosary; Climb Mt. Krizevac (Cross Mountain) and pray the Stations of the Cross; Join evening prayers/commemoration for the apparitions; Attend Croatian Mass and Blessing of the Sick (when held); Adore the Blessed Sacrament (when scheduled); Visit the Community of Cenacolo; Pray at the Statue of the Risen Christ; Attend Confessions in English at St. James Church (when available)

tourDays.title: Medjugorje spiritual program
tourDays.description: Final full day in Medjugorje continuing spiritual activities and visits with the local guide: Mass, climbs, evening prayers, visit Cenacolo, adoration and personal prayer time.
tourDays.activities: Attend Daily Mass (English-speaking); Climb Apparition Hill and pray the Rosary; Climb Mt. Krizevac (Cross Mountain) and pray the Stations of the Cross; Join evening prayers/commemoration for the apparitions; Attend Croatian Mass and Blessing of the Sick (when held); Adore the Blessed Sacrament (when scheduled); Visit the Community of Cenacolo; Pray at the Statue of the Risen Christ; Attend Confessions in English at St. James Church (when available)

tourDays.title: Departure from Medjugorje
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast and farewells, depart by motor coach for Dubrovnik, Split, Zagreb, or Sarajevo Airport for return flights home.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast; Depart by motor coach to airport; Check in for return flights

tourDays.title: USA - Italy
tourDays.description: Depart USA for an overnight flight to Rome. Dinner and breakfast will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Depart USA; Overnight flight to Rome; Dinner and breakfast served on board

tourDays.title: Arrive Rome
tourDays.description: Upon arrival your escort will greet you and welcome you to Italy. Transfer to your hotel and enjoy a free afternoon for rest, relaxation, or exploration.
tourDays.activities: Arrive in Rome; Transfer to hotel; Free afternoon for rest or exploration

tourDays.title: Rome - Montecassino - San Giovanni Rotondo
tourDays.description: Leave Rome and head south through the Roman countryside, stopping at the Abbey of Montecassino. Continue east to San Giovanni Rotondo, which will be the base for the next two nights. Dinner and overnight in San Giovanni Rotondo.
tourDays.activities: Depart Rome; Visit Abbey of Montecassino; Travel to San Giovanni Rotondo; Dinner and overnight in San Giovanni Rotondo

tourDays.title: San Giovanni Rotondo - Monte Sant'Angelo
tourDays.description: After celebrating Mass at the tomb of St. Padre Pio, tour the sanctuary, see the old church and the crucifix from which he received the stigmata, and visit the confessional. Visit the Grotto of Michael the Archangel and enjoy panoramic views of the Cargano Peninsula. Return to San Giovanni for devotions, reflection, and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Celebrate Mass at the tomb of St. Padre Pio; Tour the sanctuary and old church; See the crucifix associated with St. Padre Pio; Visit the confessional used by St. Padre Pio; Visit the Grotto of Michael the Archangel; Devotions and reflection

tourDays.title: San Giovanni Rotondo - Lanciano - Loreto - Assisi
tourDays.description: After breakfast, drive up the Adriatic coast to Lanciano to see the Eucharistic Miracle and celebrate Mass. Continue to the Marian shrine of Loreto to visit the Holy House of Nazareth and the Madonna of Loreto. Continue on to Assisi for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast at hotel; Drive up the Adriatic coast; Visit the Eucharistic Miracle in Lanciano; Celebrate Mass in Lanciano; Visit the Holy House of Nazareth in Loreto; Visit the Madonna of Loreto; Travel to Assisi; Dinner and overnight in Assisi

tourDays.title: Assisi
tourDays.description: Visit the tomb of St. Francis and explore Assisi, including the 13th-century Basilica with frescoes, the crucifix that spoke to St. Francis, St Mary of the Angels Basilica (Chapel, Portiuncola, rose bush, and cave), and the Church of St Clare to see her incorrupt body. Stroll medieval streets and stop at an outdoor cafe with a view of an ancient Roman temple. Dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit tomb of St. Francis; Explore the Basilica of St. Francis and view frescoes; Kneel before the crucifix associated with St. Francis; Visit St Mary of the Angels Basilica (Chapel, Portiuncola, rose bush, cave); Stroll medieval streets of Assisi; Stop at an outdoor cafe overlooking an ancient Roman temple; Visit Church of St Clare to see incorrupt body; Dinner and overnight in Assisi

tourDays.title: Assisi - Siena - Rome
tourDays.description: After breakfast travel to Siena. Stroll the Piazza del Campo, visit the Cathedral and the Basilica of St. Francis (containing miraculous consecrated hosts), and view the incorrupt head of St. Catherine at the Basilica of St. Dominic. Continue on to Rome for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Travel from Assisi to Siena; Stroll Piazza del Campo; Visit Siena Cathedral; Visit the Basilica of St. Francis in Siena; View the incorrupt head of St. Catherine at the Basilica of St. Dominic; Travel to Rome; Dinner and overnight in Rome

tourDays.title: Rome - USA
tourDays.description: After breakfast, depart from the hotel to Rome Airport for the return flight to the USA.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Transfer from hotel to Rome Airport; Return flight to USA

tourDays.title: Depart USA
tourDays.description: Board your overnight transatlantic flights from your hometown. Meals are served on board.
tourDays.activities: Board overnight transatlantic flight; Meals served on board

tourDays.title: Arrive Dubrovnik
tourDays.description: Arrive at the Dubrovnik airport where you will be met and transferred to your hotel. Spend the afternoon in this city overlooking the Adriatic, at your leisure. Feel free to walk to the Old Town. This evening, you will have dinner at a typical Dalmatian restaurant that serves local delicacies and wines.
tourDays.activities: Meet and transfer to hotel; Leisure time in Dubrovnik; Walk to the Old Town (optional); Dinner at a Dalmatian restaurant

tourDays.title: Dubrovnik Walking Tour
tourDays.description: Following breakfast, enjoy a walking tour of the Old City beginning at St. Blasius Church and continuing to the Rectorâs Palace, Bell Tower Clock, Orlandoâs Column, Sponza Palace, and the Dominican and Franciscan Monasteries. Afternoon lunch on your own and remainder of the day at leisure. Dinner and overnight in Dubrovnik.
tourDays.activities: Walking tour of Dubrovnik Old City; Visit St. Blasius Church; Visit Rectorâs Palace; View Bell Tower Clock and Orlandoâs Column; Visit Sponza Palace; Visit Dominican and Franciscan Monasteries; Lunch on your own; Dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Excursion to Montenegro
tourDays.description: Depart for the Republic of Montenegro. Head towards the mouth of the Bay of Kotor and enjoy a boat ride to Our Lady of the Rocks. Stop in Perast and spend time in the city of Kotor before returning to Dubrovnik for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Drive/excursion to Montenegro; Boat ride to Our Lady of the Rocks; Visit Perast; Visit Kotor; Return to Dubrovnik

tourDays.title: Travel to Split / Split Sightseeing
tourDays.description: Depart Dubrovnik and travel north along the Adriatic coast to Split. Explore Splitâs Roman heritage built around Diocletianâs Palace and see sites such as Jupiterâs Temple, the Peristyle of Diocletianâs Palace, and the Cathedral of St. Domnius. Dinner at a local Konoba and overnight in Split.
tourDays.activities: Coach travel along the Adriatic coast; Sightseeing in Split; Visit Diocletianâs Palace and Roman sites; Dinner at a local Konoba

tourDays.title: Trogir and Travel to Plitvice Lakes
tourDays.description: Head north along the coast to Trogir, a small island known for Gothic and Renaissance influences. Continue the journey towards the Plitvice Lakes where you will have dinner and overnight after a full day of touring.
tourDays.activities: Visit Trogir; Drive to Plitvice Lakes; Dinner and overnight at Plitvice

tourDays.title: Plitvice National Park
tourDays.description: Enjoy Plitvice National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage site) and its scenery of terraced lakes, waterfalls, mountains, and limestone canyons. After a full day of exploring, enjoy dinner and overnight in Plitvice.
tourDays.activities: Explore Plitvice National Park; Sightseeing of lakes and waterfalls; Dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Opatija Orientation and Postojna Caves
tourDays.description: Return to the bay of Kvarner and tour Opatija with an orientation of the town. Drive across the border into Slovenia to Postojna Caves and tour the cave by miniature electric train. Continue to Bled for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Orientation tour of Opatija; Drive to Postojna Caves; Tour Postojna Caves by miniature electric train; Continue to Bled

tourDays.title: Bled Sightseeing and Ljubljana Excursion
tourDays.description: Sightseeing in Bled featuring the town and lakeshore and a visit to Bled Castle. In the afternoon, excursion to Ljubljana to view the Central open-air Market, Baroque Town Hall, Robbaâs Fountain, the Three Bridges, and the Parliament. Farewell dinner and overnight in Ljubljana.
tourDays.activities: Sightseeing in Bled; Visit Bled Castle; Excursion to Ljubljana and city sightseeing; Farewell dinner

tourDays.title: Departure from Ljubljana
tourDays.description: After breakfast transfer to Ljubljana airport for your flight home.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to Ljubljana airport; Flight home

tourDays.title: Depart for Greece
tourDays.description: Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Make way to local airport; Board overnight flight(s); Meals served on board

tourDays.title: Arrive in Thessaloniki
tourDays.description: Upon landing at Makedonia Thessaloniki Airport, make your way to the baggage claim area and collect your luggage. Proceed to the Arrivals Hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. Board the bus to transfer to your hotel. Enjoy some time to relax after check-in. After a delicious meal, overnight in Thessaloniki.
tourDays.activities: Collect luggage at baggage claim; Meet tour guide/driver in Arrivals Hall; Transfer by bus to hotel; Relax after check-in; Dinner/meal and overnight

tourDays.title: Philippi, Kavala and return to Thessaloniki
tourDays.description: After breakfast, start your journey in Greece with the first stop of the day in Philippi. Visit the Roman Forum, view the prison ruins where Paul and Silas were thrown, and the site associated with Lydia's baptism. Continue to the modern port city of Kavala (ancient Neapolis) to view a mosaic depicting St. Paul at St. Nicholas church, remains of ancient columns, the Roman Aqueduct, and ruins of the Acropolis in Kavala. After enjoying the city by the sea, return to Thessaloniki for a meal and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Roman Forum in Philippi; View prison ruins associated with Paul and Silas; Visit site of Lydia's baptistery in Philippi; Visit St. Nicholas church mosaic in Kavala; View Roman Aqueduct and Acropolis ruins in Kavala; Return to Thessaloniki

tourDays.title: Thessaloniki city tour and Veria (Berea)
tourDays.description: Breakfast at the hotel. In Thessaloniki see artifacts such as the triumphal Arch of Galerius at the start of Via Egnatia, St. Demetrios Church and its mosaics and frescoes, and walk to view the Roman Agora. Drive to the upper town for views and pass the modern church of St Paul and the site of the Monastery of Vlatadon. Following the city tour, drive to Veria (Berea) to see sites related to St. Paul's visits and the Triptych monument in remembrance of St. Paul's work. Return to Thessaloniki for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: See Arch of Galerius; Visit St. Demetrios Church; Walk to Roman Agora; Drive through upper town and view Monastery of Vlatadon site; Drive to Veria and view Triptych monument; Return to Thessaloniki

tourDays.title: Meteora Monasteries and Kalambaka
tourDays.description: After breakfast, board the motorcoach and drive to the Meteora Monasteries. Learn about the monks' settlements on the rocks and view Byzantine art and the surrounding breathtaking scenery. Dinner and overnight in Kalambaka.
tourDays.activities: Drive to Meteora; Visit Meteora Monasteries; View Byzantine art and scenery; Dinner and overnight in Kalambaka

tourDays.title: Delphi: Sanctuary of Apollo and museum
tourDays.description: Drive to Delphi and visit the center of the ancient world on the slopes of Mount Parnassus. Visit the ruins of the Sanctuary of Apollo Pythios and the Delphi museum, where among other artifacts you see the Gallio inscription. Visit the site and museum. The text also references continuing to Athens; dinner and overnight at your hotel in Delphi.
tourDays.activities: Drive to Delphi; Visit Sanctuary of Apollo Pythios; Visit Delphi museum; See the Gallio inscription; Visit archaeological site

tourDays.title: Nafpactos (Lepanto) and Patras
tourDays.description: Drive from Delphi to the seaside town of Nafpactos for a visit related to the Battle of Lepanto and the Memorial to Cervantes. Learn about the 1571 naval battle and its historical significance. Cross the RioâAntirrio (Charilaos Trikoupis) Bridge and drive to Patras, the third largest city of Greece. Dinner and overnight in Patras.
tourDays.activities: Drive to Nafpactos; Learn about the Battle of Lepanto and related history; Cross the RioâAntirrio (Charilaos Trikoupis) Bridge; Drive to Patras; Dinner and overnight in Patras

tourDays.title: Patras (St. Andrew), Ancient Corinth and travel to Athens
tourDays.description: Celebrate Mass at St Andrew Catholic Cathedral of Patras and visit the Basilica of Saint Andrew (Greek Orthodox) where the relics of St. Andrew are kept and venerated. Then drive to Ancient Corinth to view remains of first-century shops, the site of Saint Paul's trial by Gallio, the Fountain of Peirene, and the Temple of Apollo. Stop by Cachraee, the port from where St. Paul sailed to Ephesus, and continue to Athens for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Celebrate Mass at St Andrew Catholic Cathedral (Patras); Visit Basilica/Church of Saint Andrew and venerate relics; Drive to Ancient Corinth; View first-century shops, Gallio trial site, Fountain of Peirene, Temple of Apollo; Stop at Cachraee (port); Continue to Athens

tourDays.title: Athens: Acropolis, Agora, and city highlights
tourDays.description: Tour Athens beginning with the Acropolis to see the Parthenon, Erectheum, and Propylaea. Ascend Mars Hill where Saint Paul spoke to the Athenians. View the ancient Agora, drive through the city to view the House of Parliament on Syntagma Square, the University of Athens, and the National Library of Greece. Visit the Panathenaic Stadium and the New Acropolis Museum. Dinner and overnight in Athens.
tourDays.activities: Visit the Acropolis (Parthenon, Erectheum, Propylaea); Ascend Mars Hill (Areopagus); View the ancient Agora; Drive by Syntagma Square, University of Athens, National Library; Visit Panathenaic Stadium; Visit New Acropolis Museum

tourDays.title: Byzantine & Christian Museum and Cape Sounion
tourDays.description: Visit the Byzantine and Christian Museum featuring artefacts dating from the 3rd to 20th century AD. In the afternoon drive to Cape Sounion; on the way see the place where St Paul docked at his arrival by boat in Athens, continue along the seaside road to the Temple of Poseidon for views, and then return to Athens for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Byzantine and Christian Museum; Drive to Cape Sounion; See site where St Paul docked in Athens; Visit Temple of Poseidon; Return to Athens

tourDays.title: Return Home
tourDays.description: After breakfast transfer to Athens airport for your return flight(s) home.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Transfer to Athens airport; Board return flight(s)

tourDays.title: Depart for Lisbon
tourDays.description: Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Depart from local airport; Overnight flight; In-flight meals

tourDays.title: Arrive in Lisbon â sightseeing and Mass
tourDays.description: Upon landing at Lisbon Airport, collect luggage and proceed to the arrival hall to be greeted by your tour guide/driver. Meet the group in the hotel lobby at 2:30 PM, then board the bus for a panoramic sightseeing tour of Lisbon with stops including St. Jeromeâs Monastery, the Belem Quarter and Belem Tower, and St. Anthonyâs Church where Mass will be celebrated. Drive to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Arrival and luggage claim; Meet tour guide and group; Panoramic sightseeing tour; Visit St. Jeromeâs Monastery; See Belem Quarter and Belem Tower; Attend Mass at St. Anthonyâs Church; Hotel check-in, dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Santarem and Fatima visits
tourDays.description: Travel north to the old city of Santarem and attend Mass at the Church of St. Stephen (site of a 13th-century Eucharistic Miracle). Continue to Fatima to visit the hamlet of Aljustrel, the Parish Church, and Fatima Parish Cemetery. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Travel to Santarem; Attend Mass at Church of St. Stephen; Visit Aljustrel (home of the shepherd children); Visit Parish Church and Fatima Parish Cemetery; Hotel dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Fatima pilgrimage sites and devotions
tourDays.description: Visit the Little Chapel of the Apparitions, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary (containing the tombs of St. Francisco, St. Jacinta, and Sister Lucia), view the Sacred Heart of Jesus monument, visit the 'Fatima: Light and Peace' Museum and the Holy Trinity Basilica. After free time for lunch, participate in the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra, visit Valinhos, and conclude the night with private devotions and a candlelight procession.
tourDays.activities: Visit Little Chapel of the Apparitions; Visit Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary; View monument to the Sacred Heart of Jesus; Visit Fatima museum ("Light and Peace"); Visit Holy Trinity Basilica; Walk the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra; Visit Valinhos; Private devotions and candlelight procession

tourDays.title: Travel to Salamanca â walking tour
tourDays.description: Depart Fatima after breakfast and travel to Salamanca. Take a walking tour visiting Plaza Mayor, La Clerecia, La Casa de las Conchas, the University of Salamanca, the Roman Bridge, Iglesia de San Marcos, Iglesia de San Martin, and the two Salamanca Cathedrals (old and new). Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Travel to Salamanca; Walking tour of Salamanca; Visit Plaza Mayor, La Clerecia, Casa de las Conchas; See University of Salamanca and Roman Bridge; Visit Iglesia de San Marcos and Iglesia de San Martin; Visit Salamanca Cathedrals; Hotel dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: St. Teresa sites, Avila, and Burgos
tourDays.description: Board the bus to Alba de Tormes to celebrate Mass at the Carmelite Monastery where St. Teresa died and is buried; visit the museum housing her relics. After free time for lunch, continue to Avila to view the 11th-century city walls, Cathedral de Avila, Basilica de San Vicente, and the Incarnation Convent. Continue to Burgos for dinner and evening exploration of Burgos Cathedral.
tourDays.activities: Travel to Alba de Tormes; Celebrate Mass at Carmelite Monastery; Visit the museum dedicated to St. Teresa; Free time for lunch; Sightseeing in Avila (city walls, cathedral, basilica, convent); Travel to Burgos; Evening leisure and sightseeing at Burgos Cathedral

tourDays.title: Loyola visit and transfer to Lourdes
tourDays.description: After breakfast transfer from Burgos to Loyola to visit the birthplace of St. Ignatius, including the 17th-century Basilica and the 'Holy House' where he prayed and began his conversion. After free time for lunch, continue by bus to Lourdes, arriving with views of the Pyrenees, then check in to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Transfer from Burgos to Loyola; Visit Loyola Basilica and Holy House; Pray in the venerated room (St. Ignatius site); Free time for lunch; Bus transfer to Lourdes; Hotel check-in, dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Lourdes â Grotto, Mass, and devotions
tourDays.description: Begin stays in Lourdes: pray and meditate at the site of Our Ladyâs apparitions. Attend Mass at the Grotto of Massabielle, watch a video presentation about Lourdes, wash and drink from the miraculous spring, meditate at the life-size Stations of the Cross overlooking the Grotto, and visit Boly Mill and the Cachot. Each evening you may attend the candlelight procession and pray the Rosary.
tourDays.activities: Pray and meditate at apparition sites; Attend Mass at the Grotto (Massabielle); Watch Lourdes video presentation; Drink and wash with spring water; Meditate at Stations of the Cross; Visit Boly Mill and the Cachot; Attend evening candlelight procession and Rosary (optional)

tourDays.title: Second day in Lourdes â continued devotions
tourDays.description: Continue time in Lourdes with opportunities to attend Mass at the Grotto, visit the sanctuary and related sites, participate in devotions, and attend the nightly candlelight procession following dinner.
tourDays.activities: Attend Mass at the Grotto; Visit sanctuary sites and pilgrimage locations; Participate in devotions and Stations of the Cross; Attend evening candlelight procession and Rosary

tourDays.title: Flight to Rome and welcome Mass
tourDays.description: After breakfast transfer to the airport for a short flight to Rome. Upon arrival be greeted by a tour escort/driver, transfer to the hotel for check-in, relax or explore, then meet the group in the hotel lobby for a 'meet and greet' and depart for Mass followed by a welcome dinner. Optional walk to St. Peterâs Square to pray the Rosary after dinner.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to airport; Flight from Lourdes to Rome; Arrival transfer to hotel; Meet and greet with group; Attend Mass; Welcome dinner; Optional Rosary at St. Peterâs Square

tourDays.title: Papal Audience and major basilicas
tourDays.description: Attend the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square (subject to the papal schedule). Free time for lunch and shopping. Visit the Basilica of St. John Lateran (housing relics of Peter and Paul), the Holy Staircase (traditionally from Pontius Pilate's palace), and the Basilica of St. Mary Major (containing a relic from the Manger of the Infant Jesus). Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.description: Upon arrival in Madrid, you will collect your luggage in the baggage claim area and continue to the Arrivals Hall where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver, then transfer and check in at the hotel. tourDays.title: Madrid â Segovia - Avila
tourDays.description: After breakfast, we will depart for a visit to the town of Segovia. Segovia is the town where Saint John of the Cross was buried. Segovia is a relatively small city strategically situated on a rock ridge. It is deeply and haughtily Castilian, with a panoply of squares and mansions from its days of Golden Age grandeur â it was once a royal resort and a base for the Cortes (parliament). It was in Segovia that Isabel La CatÃ³lica was proclaimed queen of Castilla. We will find numerous impressive monuments and buildings inside its medieval walls, including the Roman aqueduct: Segovia Acueducto. It was built at the end of the first century during the reigns of the Emperors Nerva and Trajan. Over 800m long, it is supported by 166 arches and 120 pillars and stands up without a drop of mortar or cement. You will also see the Cathedral, the last major Gothic building in Spain; the AlcÃ¡zar, an extraordinary fantasy castle, with its narrow towers and flurry of turrets; the Vera Cruz church, built by the Templar Knights; the synagogue, very similar in style to Santa MarÃ­a la Blanca in Toledo; and many Romanesque churches such as San MillÃ¡n, San Justo, San MartÃ­n, and more. Continue to Avila for a delicious dinner and a restful overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart for Segovia after breakfast; Visit Segovia and its monuments; See Segovia Aqueduct; See Segovia Cathedral; See the AlcÃ¡zar; Visit Vera Cruz church and synagogue; See Romanesque churches (San MillÃ¡n, San Justo, San MartÃ­n); Transfer to Avila; Dinner and overnight in Avila

tourDays.title: Avila
tourDays.description: After breakfast, we will visit the city of Avila. Here the atmosphere has changed very little since the days of St. Teresa, to whom the city is dedicated. St. Teresa was a great mystic and was the first woman to be named a Doctor of the Church. while in Avila we will visit: the crypt of La Santa Convent, built on the site of the house where she was born; La Encarnacion Convent, where St. Teresa became a nun and home to the most comprehensive museum dedicated to her life; and the Cathedral and the Cuatro Postes (four columns) which commemorates St. Teresa. At the age of seven, she convinced her brother to run away with her to die as martyrs in the land of the Moors. Their uncle caught them at this site and returned them home. The day will end with dinner and an overnight in Avila.
tourDays.activities: Visit the crypt of La Santa Convent; Visit La Encarnacion Convent and its museum; Visit the Cathedral; Visit the Cuatro Postes; Dinner and overnight in Avila

tourDays.title: Avila â Alba de Tormes â Salamanca â Avila
tourDays.description: The day will begin with breakfast in the hotel. In the morning we will do an excursion to the surroundings of Avila including a visit to the town of Alba de Tormes and the city of Salamanca. Alba de Tormes is where St. Teresa died in 1582 and where she is buried. In the museum of the Carmelite Convent of the Annunciation, we will be able to see the incorrupt heart and left arm of the Saint. It was in Salamanca that Saint John of the Cross studied Theology and was ordained priest and where Santa Teresa founded the Carmelite Convent in 1570. For four centuries Salamanca was the seat of one of the most prestigious universities in the world and, despite losing this reputation in the XVII Century, it has kept the unmistakable atmosphere of being a seat of learning. It is a small place, and it is given a gorgeous harmony by the golden sandstone of which almost the entire city seems to be constructed. The cityâs architectural sights seem endless: two cathedrals â one Gothic, the other Romanesque â vie for attention with Renaissance palaces and gems of Plateresque decoration. The Plaza Mayor is the finest in Spain, and the surviving university buildings are tremendous throughout â all of them distinguished by the same warm stone. Today we will visit this impressive and beautiful city. The grand Plaza Mayor is the hub of Salmantine life with the vast Baroque church of La ClerecÃ­a, the Casa de las Conchas (House of Shells, named after the rows of carved scallop shells symbol of the pilgrimage to Santiago which decorate its faÃ§ade), the University, the cathedrals, the Roman Bridge, San Marcos, San Martin churches, and much more. We will wrap up the day with dinner and an overnight stay in Avila.
tourDays.activities: Excursion to Alba de Tormes (visit Carmelite Convent of the Annunciation and museum); Visit Salamanca (Plaza Mayor, La ClerecÃ­a, Casa de las Conchas, University, cathedrals, Roman Bridge, San Marcos, San Martin); Return to Avila for dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Avila - Malagon â Baeza
tourDays.description: We will begin the day with breakfast in the hotel, and then we will depart towards the South of Spain. On our way to Baeza, we will make stop in Malagon where we will find the Carmelite Convent founded by Santa Teresa in April 1568. We will continue on to Baeza for a delicious dinner and a restful overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart Avila after breakfast; Stop in Malagon and visit the Carmelite Convent; Continue to Baeza; Dinner and overnight in Baeza

tourDays.title: Baeza â Ubeda - Baeza
tourDays.description: The day will begin with breakfast in the hotel. We will spend the day visiting different places related to both Saints. In Baeza Saint John of the Cross worked like a teacher in its famous university, and in 1591 he died in Ubeda. Both cities, designated World Heritage sites by UNESCO, preserve magnificent buildings and monuments in their medieval and renaissance quarters: Incarnation Convent, Jabalquinto Palace, San Pablo Church, the Cathedral, Salvador Church, Santa Maria Church, and more. In Beas de Segura we will find the first convent founded by Saint Teresa in Andalucia (South of Spain) that holds many relics of both doctors of the Church. In Villanueva del Arzobispo we will visit the Sanctuary of La Fuensanta where Saint John of the Cross lived after running away from Toledoâs jail, helped by Saint Teresa. Return to Baeza for a delicious dinner and a restful overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Baeza sites related to the saints; Travel to and visit Ubeda (monuments and churches); Visit Beas de Segura (first convent in Andalucia); Visit Sanctuary of La Fuensanta in Villanueva del Arzobispo; Return to Baeza for dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Baeza â Granada
tourDays.description: Our day will begin with breakfast in the hotel before departing toward Granada. Saint John of the Cross was Prior in Granada for many years and we will be able to follow in his steps in the city. In the afternoon we will visit one of the most beautiful palaces in the World: The Alhambra Palace. The meaning of the word Alhambra is âthe red fortâ and comes from its reddish walls. The Alhambra was a palace, a citadel, a fortress, and the home of the Nasrid sultans, high government officials, servants of the court, and elite soldiers (from the 13th to the 14th century). Today, the monument is divided into four main areas: the Palaces, the military zone of Alcazaba, the city of Medina, and the agricultural estate of the Generalife. Beautiful woods, gardens, and orchards surround all of these areas. Other notable buildings belonging to a different period are also included, such as the Renaissance-style Palace of Charles V, which houses the Alhambra Museum (most of the items are from the site of the monument) and the Fine Art Museum. In the evening we will enjoy a beautiful view of the Alhambra from the San Nicholas viewpoint. The day will come to a close with dinner and an overnight in Granada.
tourDays.activities: Depart for Granada after breakfast; Visit Alhambra Palace (Palaces, Alcazaba, Medina, Generalife) in the afternoon; Visit Palace of Charles V and Alhambra Museum; Enjoy view from San Nicholas viewpoint in the evening; Dinner and overnight in Granada

tourDays.title: Granada â Sevilla
tourDays.description: Following an early breakfast, we will continue with the visit to downtown Granada where will we find the Cathedral and its Royal Chapel where the Catholic Monarchs Isabella and Ferdinand are buried. In the afternoon we will depart toward the city of Seville. Seville has important monuments and an illustrious history, but itâs essentially famous for its living self, the greatest city of the Spanish South, of Carmen, Don Juan, and Figaro, and the archetype of Andalucian promise. This reputation for gaiety and brilliance, for theatrically and intensity of life, does seem deserved. The city is bisected by the RÃ­o Guadalquivir. The old city takes up the east bank and at its heart stand three great monuments: the Giralda Tower, the minaret of the old mosque; the Cathedral, built in the XV Century in Gothic style; and the AlcÃ¡zar, the Moorish palaces. We will also find the Barrio de Santa Cruz, the medieval Jewish quarter, and now the heart of tourist life. The day will end with dinner and an overnight stay in Seville.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast; Visit downtown Granada (Cathedral and Royal Chapel); Depart for Seville in the afternoon; See Seville landmarks (Giralda, Cathedral, AlcÃ¡zar, Barrio de Santa Cruz); Dinner and overnight in Seville

tourDays.title: Sevilla
tourDays.description: We will begin the day with breakfast in the hotel. Today we will enjoy a half-day tour of Seville, the capital of Andalucia, and the site of the Cathedral of Saint Mary, the largest Cathedral in Spain and the third largest in Christendom. It is here where Santa Teresa established her 11th foundation in 1575, and it is in the Carmelite Convent of Saint Joseph that the original autographed copy of Saint Teresaâs Interior Castle is kept. The day will come to a close with dinner and an overnight in Seville.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast in hotel; Half-day tour of Seville; Visit Cathedral of Saint Mary; Visit Carmelite Convent of Saint Joseph (holds original autographed copy of Saint Teresaâs Interior Castle); Dinner and overnight in Seville

tourDays.title: Sevilla â Cordoba â Toledo
tourDays.description: The day will begin with breakfast in the hotel, then we will board our bus and make our way towards Madrid. On the way, we will visit Cordoba. The city of CÃ³rdoba lies upstream from Sevilla beside a loop of the Guadalquivir River, which was once navigable as far as here. Today it is a minor provincial capital, prosperous in a modest sort of way. Once, however, it was the largest city of Roman Spain, and for three centuries it formed the heart of the western Islamic Empire, the great medieval caliphate of the Moors. It is from this era that the cityâs major monument dates: the Mezquita-Catedral (Mosque-Cathedral) â the grandest and most beautiful mosque ever constructed by the Moors in Spain. It stands right in the center of the city, surrounded by the old Jewish and Moorish quarters, and is a building of extraordinary mystical and aesthetic power. Apart from the Mezquita, we will walk through the Jewish quarter and visit its synagogue. the day will come to a close with dinner and an overnight in Toledo.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast in hotel; Board bus; Visit Cordoba (Mezquita-Catedral, Jewish quarter, synagogue); Continue travel toward Madrid and overnight in Toledo

tourDays.title: Toledo - Madrid
tourDays.description: Following breakfast, we will visit the Imperial City of Toledo where Saint John of the Cross was imprisoned by the Inquisition. Toledo sits on a rocky mound isolated on three sides by a looping gorge of the RÃ­o Tajo. Every available inch of this outcrop has been built upon: churches, synagogues, mosques, and houses are heaped upon one another in a haphazard spiral which the cobbled lanes infiltrate as best they can. Toledo is known as the City of the Three Religions or Cultures because for many centuries the Christians, the Moors, and the Jews lived together in relative equality and peace. The city, surrounded by walls, hides great treasures: its awesome Cathedral, robust Gothic construction which took over 250 years (1227 â 1493) to complete; the church of Santo TomÃ©, where the Grecoâs masterpiece is located â The Burial of Mr. Orgaz; the TrÃ¡nsito Synagogue that houses the Museo Sefardita; Santa MarÃ­a La Blanca Synagogue; the superb church of San Juan de los Reyes, with its exterior bizarrely festooned with the chains worn by the Christians prisoners from Granada released on the reconquest of the city; the different doors that keep the city safe: Puerta de Bisagras, Puerta del CambrÃ³n, Puerta del Sol; and more. After a full day, we will continue on to Madrid for a delicious dinner and a restful overnight.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Visit Toledo (Cathedral, Santo TomÃ©, TrÃ¡nsito Synagogue, Santa MarÃ­a La Blanca Synagogue, San Juan de los Reyes, city gates); Continue to Madrid; Dinner and overnight in Madrid

Depart for Lisbon
Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.

tourDays.title: Day 2
tourDays.description: Arrive in Lisbon Upon landing at Lisbon Airport, head to baggage claim and collect your luggage. Proceed to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. After meeting your group in the hotel lobby at 2:30 PM, board the bus and begin a panoramic sightseeing tour of Lisbon. We will stop at St. Jeromeâs Monastery, built to give thanks to the Virgin Mary for guiding Vasco da Gama on his voyage that linked Europe and Asia. Continue to drive by the Belem Quarter, which contains the iconic entryway to the Lisbon harbor, the Belem Tower. This important historic structure has many beautiful sculptures, such as depictions of St. Vincent and Our Lady of Safe Homecoming. The next stop is St. Anthonyâs Church, built upon the site of Saintâs birth; it is here that we will celebrate Mass. Although the patron Saint of lost things is known as St. Anthony of Padua (Italy), he was born in Lisbon, Portugal. This Church is built upon St. Anthonyâs birth site and is also where Saint John Paul II visited in 1982. After Mass, we will drive to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 3
tourDays.description: Lisbon - Santarem - Fatima Today, we will travel north to the old city of Santarem. We will attend Mass at the Church of St. Stephen, which holds a 13th-century Eucharistic Miracle. Continue to Fatima and visit the Hamlet of Aljustrel, the home of the three shepherd children. Visit the Parish Church and Fatima Parish Cemetery. Continue to your hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 4
tourDays.description: Fatima Today will be a memorable experience as you pray and meditate upon one of Our Blessed Motherâs apparition sites. Our Lady appeared to three shepherd children: Venerable Sister Lucia (age 10), St. Jacinta (age 7), and St. Francisco (age 9). These apparitions occurred monthly from May until October of 1917. Historically, as the entire world was in turmoil, Our Ladyâs most prominent message was to pray for world peace. The destruction of the world at that point in history was also mentioned by Our Lady, particularly in her second secret to the children. Our profoundly reflective day begins with a visit to the Little Chapel of the Apparitions. This simple yet modern chapel is where the Virgin Mary first appeared on May 13, 1917. Next, you will see the stunning neoclassical church, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary. This Sacred space contains the tombs of St. Francisco, St. Jacinta, and Sister Lucia. View the monument that commemorates the Sacred Heart of Jesus in the square. In honor of Our Ladyâs requests to pray the Rosary, the Basilica also features fifteen altars each dedicated to a mystery of the Rosary. Visit the Museum with the âFatima: Light and Peaceâ exhibition. Continue with a visit to the Holy Trinity Basilica. After free time for lunch, we will experience Christâs unconditional love by participating in the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra. The âSacred Wayâ marks the path taken by the shepherd children of Fatima to their first apparition with Our Lady. It is composed of fifteen small chapels commemorating the Passion of Our Lord. The fifteenth station, the Resurrection, can be found close to the Chapel of Calvary, dedicated to St. Stephen, King of Hungary. Ending the day with a visit to Valinhos, the site of Our Ladyâs August 1917 apparition and the first and third apparition of the Angel. Your night will conclude with private devotions and a candlelight procession, as requested by Our Lady in 1917. Enjoy dinner and a comfortable nightâs rest in Fatima.

tourDays.title: Day 5
tourDays.description: Fatima â Porto â Santiago de Compostela After breakfast, we will board the motor coach and drive to Porto (Oporto). Porto is a historic city renowned for its production of Port, which is still stored and matured in the vast cellars that line the banks of the Douro River. After a city tour of Porto and celebrating Mass, enjoy some free time for lunch before we continue to the great city of Santiago de Compostela for dinner and a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 6
tourDays.description: Santiago de Compostela This morning, you will walk a few miles of El Camino. Immerse yourselves in the fragrant eucalyptus groves and experience the breathtaking scenery. Later this morning, attend the International Pilgrim Mass at the Cathedral of St. James. After Mass, there will be free time for lunch. In the afternoon, we will visit the Cathedral of Santiago. This Cathedral is one of the finest architectural examples in Europe as it encompasses Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. The Cathedral contains numerous valuable pieces of art. Upon entering the Cathedral, pilgrims traditionally hug the dazzling statue of St. James. You will then descend into the crypt where the Patron Saint of Pilgrimsâ relics are kept. After that, you will enjoy a sightseeing tour of the city. Some stops on your tour include Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, Gemirez Palace, Franco Street, and much more. Return to your hotel for dinner and an overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 7
tourDays.description: Santiago De Compostela - Our Lady of Covadonga Sanctuary â San Sebastian de Garabandal After breakfast, depart for Covadonga and visit the Covadonga Sanctuary. This Shrine gained popularity following the Battle of Covadonga in 722 when the Moors tried to invade Spain. A statue of the Virgin Mary, secretly hidden in one of the caves, was believed to have faithfully supported the Christian victory. Covadonga is where the re-conquest began under King Pelayo, whose remains are buried in the cave alongside Our Lady of Covadonga. The Basilica and Cave are places of worship and Pilgrimage for the people of Asturias. The Basilica was built in the neo-Romanesque style, featuring two high towers that flank the main entrance. Inside, there are works of great value, such as a canvas by Madrazo. The statue of King Pelayo is located in the square adjacent to the Basilica. The statue of Our Lady of Covadonga, the tomb of King Pelayo, and the tomb of King Alfonso I are located in the Holy Cave, which is accessible via a large staircase. A spring flows out of the cave, and below this, there is a fountain with seven spouts. On the altar, a gold panel represents the Battle of Covadonga. Continue through the scenic countryside of Cantabria, Spain. Enjoy the lush green mountains before arriving at the hamlet of Garabandal. Check into your hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 8
tourDays.description: San Sebastian de Garabandal - Santo Toribio de Liebana Monastery - San Sebastian de Garabandal After breakfast, start your day visiting Garabandal. Little has changed in this rural town since June 18, 1961, when four children had an apparition of an Angel. The angel said he had been sent to prepare the children for a visit from the Blessed Virgin. From July 2, 1961, until November 13, 1965, the Blessed Virgin visited the children and spoke to them about future events. The children reported a promised future miracle at the grove of pine trees on a bluff overlooking the village of Garabandal. It will be on the feast day of a little-known martyr of the Eucharist and coincide with an event in the Church. In the afternoon, travel to Santo Toribio de Liebana Monastery. The Monastery was founded before the 6th Century. According to tradition, the Monastery venerates the largest piece of the Lignum Crucis discovered in Jerusalem by Saint Helena of Constantinople. It was brought from the Church of the Holy Sepulchre by Saint Turibius of Astorga. The left arm of the True Cross is kept on a gilded silver reliquary. The Monastery was initially dedicated to St. Martin of Tours, but its name was changed in the 12th Century. On April 16, 1961, the Franciscan friars, custodians of the Holy Places, were entrusted with the safekeeping of the relic and with promoting devotion to the Holy Cross. Return to Garabandal for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 9
tourDays.description: San Sebastian de Garabandal â Loyola â Lourdes Following breakfast, transfer from Garabandal to Loyola to visit the birthplace of St. Ignatius, founder of the Jesuit Order. St. Ignatius dedicated himself to becoming a soldier of the Christian faith, and as a result of many tribulations, he wrote the ever-famous Spiritual Exercises. In Loyola, you will find the 17th-century Basilica dedicated to this remarkable Saint. The Basilica is part of a series of buildings that surround the âHoly House,â the birthplace of St. Ignatius. You will also have the opportunity to pray in the room where St. Ignatius began his conversion. After meditating on the life of the founder of the Jesuit Order, enjoy free time for lunch and board the bus for the next destination. We will continue to Lourdes with a spectacular view of the Pyrenees Mountains. Upon arrival in Lourdes, you will check in to your hotel and enjoy a splendid dinner, followed by a peaceful overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 10
tourDays.description: Lourdes During your time in Lourdes, you will pray and meditate at the site of Our Ladyâs apparitions. Our Lady first appeared to Bernadette in 1858 and announced herself as âThe Immaculate Conceptionâ near the Grotto of Massabielle. During the first two apparitions, little Bernadette prayed the Rosary with Our Lady and left without exchanging words. During the following apparitions, Our Lady emphasized Godâs love for us and the necessity of performing acts of penance for sinners. Attend Mass at the Grotto, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette. Watch a video presentation that explains the story of Lourdes. Wash your hands, wash your face, and drink the water of the miraculous spring. Finish with a short prayer: âOur Lady of Lourdes, pray for us. St. Bernadette, pray for us. O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.â Experience Christâs unconditional love as you meditate upon the life-size Stations of the Cross that overlook the Grotto of Massabielle. In Lourdes, you will walk in and meditate upon the footsteps of St. Bernadette. Your group will have the opportunity to see Boly Mill, the birthplace of St. Bernadette, and the âCachot,â an abandoned prison where Bernadetteâs impoverished family lived. Following dinner, you can attend the candlelight procession and pray the Rosary before a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 11
tourDays.description: Lourdes â Montserrat After breakfast, we will depart for Montserrat, home to the miraculous Black Madonna. We will visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Montserrat, located on a rugged mountainside. According to Catholic tradition, St. Luke is said to have carved the statue of the Black Madonna around 50 A.D. and brought it to Spain. It was hidden from the Moors for a time and later rediscovered by shepherds. In 880 A.D., the shepherds and the Bishop of Manresa were drawn to a grotto by a bright light and heavenly music. Upon discovering the statue of the Black Madonna in the grotto, the Bishop of Manresa suggested that it be moved to Manresa. However, the statue was so heavy it could not be lifted. As a result, the Virgin remained in Montserrat and continued to be venerated there for centuries. As the years progressed, several chapels were built on the site, and in the eleventh century, the Abbot-Bishop Oliba founded a monastery on Montserrat next to one of these chapels. Dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 12
tourDays.description: Montserrat â Manresa â Barcelona Following breakfast, we will travel to Manresa for a visit to the Sanctuary of Saint Ignatius of Loyola and the Holy Cave where St. Ignatius lived. Continue to Barcelona. Enjoy free time this afternoon before dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 13
tourDays.description: Barcelona This morning, your day will begin with breakfast and a sightseeing tour of Barcelona! Enjoy the stunning panoramic views of the Port of Barcelona, Montjuic, Plaza de EspaÃ±a, and Plaza de Catalunya. The Port was created 2,000 years ago in the coastal area to protect and provide access for ships and goods. Currently, it is home to numerous walking regions, businesses, cultural and sporting events. Plaza de EspaÃ±a is right outside the center of town and was formerly known for its old bull-fighting ring. Presently, the Plaza is renowned for containing the Museum of Catalan Art, situated on the side of Montjuic. Plaza de Catalunya is located in the heart of Barcelona and is famous for its fountains and statues. Your day of touring will continue with a guided walk through the Gothic Quarter, which contains remains from an ancient Roman village, including the Cathedral of Barcelona. We will continue to the Eixample quarter to visit Antoni Gaudiâs stunning Roman Catholic Basilica, La Sagrada Familia, which was finished after 144 years of construction. Afternoon at leisure. Enjoy dinner followed by an overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 14
tourDays.description: Barcelona - Depart for the Netherlands Your last day in Spain will begin with breakfast at your hotel, followed by a transfer to Barcelona airport for your flight to Amsterdam. Upon landing in Amsterdam, head to the baggage claim area and collect your luggage. Proceed to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. Transfer to your hotel. This afternoon, we will visit the Chapel of Our Lady of All Nations, one of the Virgin Maryâs apparition sites. From 1945 until 1959, Our Lady appeared to Ida Peerdeman with a continuous message of love, repentance, and a prayer for nations. Following Mass, we will visit the site of a Eucharistic Miracle. In 1345, as a result of a manâs illness, a Sacred Host was found preserved in his house even though it was moved numerous times and survived a fire that left the city in ruins. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight in Amsterdam.

tourDays.title: Day 15
tourDays.description: Amsterdam â Zaanse Schans â Amsterdam Following breakfast, we will celebrate Mass. After Mass, enjoy a guided tour of Amsterdam. Experience its seventeenth-century historical and picturesque atmosphere amidst its canals and squares. During your walking tour, you will have the opportunity to view the Royal Palace, the Vrijheidsbeeld (National Monument), the Flower Market, the Opera House, the City Hall, and the Begijnenhof. Additionally, you will experience a glimpse of the many cultural highlights Amsterdam has to offer, such as the Van Gogh Museum, Anne Frankâs House, Rembrandt House, and the Rijksmuseum. After lunch, we will proceed to the Zaanse Schans, a unique piece of Dutch history located on the river Zaan. It is a residential area where the 18th and 19th centuries come alive. Stroll past the bakery museum and enjoy the smell of fresh cookies. See where clogs are made, the cheese factory, the various windmills, and much more. The Zaanse Schans is a unique part of the Netherlands, featuring wooden houses, mills, barns, and workshops. Return to Amsterdam for dinner and an overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 16
tourDays.description: Amsterdam â Utrecht â Ghent - Bruges After breakfast, we will depart for Utrecht. Utrecht is one of the Netherlandsâ principal political, economic, and cultural centers. We will visit Katherineâs Convent Museum (Catharijne convent), located in the former hospice of the Order of St. John. This museum tells the history of Christianity in the Netherlands. It also holds an extensive collection of medieval art treasures. You will have free time for lunch before boarding the motor coach for your transfer to Ghent, Belgium, home to the famous painting âAdoration of the Mystic Lamb.â This large and complex altarpiece was painted by Jan and Hubert Van Eyck in 1432. It is currently housed in St. Bavo Cathedral. We will celebrate Mass at St. Bavo Cathedral. After Mass, continue to Bruges. The Zeebrugge Port in Bruges is a significant hub for European trade. Dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 17
tourDays.description: Bruges Following breakfast, visit the Church of Our Lady for Mass. You will inevitably notice the preserved culture of the Middle Ages that remains. View the magnificent marble statue of the Madonna and Child, sculpted by Michelangelo. Next, we visit the Holy Saviorâs Cathedral in Bruges. Continue with a visit to the Basilica of the Holy Blood. This Basilica famously holds a venerated relic of Christâs blood, collected by Joseph of Arimathea and brought from Jerusalem. Modeled on the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, it has a replica of Christâs tomb. This afternoon, you will have free time to enjoy lunch and a stroll in this enchanting city. Return to your hotel on time to enjoy a delicious meal and a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 18
tourDays.description: Bruges â Dinant - Beauraing - Banneux - Aachen Following breakfast, you will board the motor coach to head to Beaurin. We will make a stop in the charming town of Dinant to have lunch on your own. Visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Beauraing, also known as the Virgin of the Golden Heart. In 1932, the Blessed Mother appeared to a group of young children thirty-three times. The children described her as being dressed in white with a golden crown on her head and golden hair. Our Lady came to these children during the Great Depression and advised them to sacrifice themselves to her. Continue to Banneux â Notre Dame, also known as the Lourdes of Belgium. Upon arrival, you will visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Banneux. In 1933, the Blessed Mother appeared to twelve-year-old Mariette Boco as the âVirgin of the Poorâ. Our Lady appeared to little Mariette multiple times and said she had come to relieve the suffering of the ill and the conflicts of all nations. Continue to Aachen for dinner and an overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 19
tourDays.description: Aachen - Cologne - Aachen Today, you will enjoy a short sightseeing tour of the village of Aachen! We will attend Mass at the Aachen Cathedral, a Gothic Marian Shrine. The Church is the oldest in Germany and contains numerous treasures, including Jesusâ swaddling clothes, the Lordâs loincloth, the Blessed Virginâs cloak, and the cloth used to cover St. John the Baptistâs head. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to venerate the miraculous fourteenth-century statue of the Blessed Virgin. Later, you will depart for Cologne, where you will enjoy another sightseeing tour! Cologne was initially founded and established by the Romans in 50 A.D. When this city received relics of the Three Magi in 1194, it gained importance as a pilgrimage center. While in this city, you will have the opportunity to visit the magnificent Gothic Cathedral, âthe Kolner Domâ that houses the relics. Following this visit, you will learn about the cityâs two thousand years of history. In the Middle Ages, the city of Cologne served as one of the major trade routes between Eastern and Western Europe. Return to Aachen for a wonderful meal and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 20
tourDays.description: Aachen - Trier - Strasbourg After breakfast, drive to Trier, which is the oldest city in Germany. It is situated in the Mosel wine region and was founded before the year 16 B.C. Trier is known for its well-preserved Roman and medieval buildings, all of which you will visit during your time in this ancient city. The Porta Nigra is the only one of four Roman gates that still stands and was formally the home to a hermit monk named Simeon. Additionally, the Roman amphitheater and baths were places of relaxation for the ancient monks. Lastly, the style and size of the Constantine Basilica (Aula Palatina) truly exemplify the strength and power that the Roman Emperor had in ancient times. We will celebrate Mass at the Trier Cathedral, followed by free time for lunch. Continue with a visit to Trier Cathedral. This Cathedral contains a remarkable collection of artwork and is home to the Holy Robe that Our Lord Jesus Christ wore during the Crucifixion. Like the Shroud of Turin, the robe is very fragile and is only displayed every 10 â 15 years. Lastly, visit the Liebfrauenkirche, one of the first Gothic churches in Germany. The Church is located near the burial site of the Saint who replaced Judas Iscariot, St. Matthias. Proceed to Heidelberg for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 21
tourDays.description: Heidelberg â Rothenburg ob der Tauber - Heidelberg Following breakfast at the hotel, we will start your day with a tour of Heidelberg. Visit the Old Town, dominated by the ruins of Heidelberg Castle. Explore the marketplace, located near the Town Hall and the Church of the Holy Spirit, and take a stroll down the main street. Admire the panoramic view of the city as we pass down the Old Bridge to the other banks of the river. We will celebrate Mass at the local church, followed by free time for lunch. Proceed to Rothenburg ob der Tauber. In Rothenburg, explore picturesque lanes, half-timbered houses, and an old fortification wall that offers a glimpse into what a medieval town looked like nearly 1,000 years ago. Walk around the city on top of the wall and enjoy stunning views overlooking the old town. Return to Heidelberg for dinner and an overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 22
tourDays.description: Heidelberg â Neuhausen am Rheinfall (Rhine Falls) â Muri Monastery - Lucerne After breakfast, we depart for Neuhausen am Rheinfall for a boat trip to see the Rhine Falls. After a break for lunch, we will transfer to the Benedictine monastery of Muri, one of the most significant cultural monuments in the Canton of Aargau. It was founded in 1027 by Ita of Lorraine and her husband, Count Radbot of Habsburg. The Romanesque crypt, Gothic raised choir, and central octagon in Baroque style all bear witness to the continuation of architectural alteration, renewal, and addition throughout the ages. Celebrate Mass at Muri Monastery. Continue to Lucerne for dinner and an overnight stay.

tourDays.title: Day 23
tourDays.description: Lucerne â Einsiedlen - Lucerne Today, we will start with a guided tour of Lucerne. This central Switzerland city is known for its miraculous views of Mt. Pilatus and Rigi in the Swiss Alps. While in this breathtaking city, you will see the wooden Chapel Bridge, first erected in the fourteenth century. This afternoon, enjoy a scenic ride along Lake Lucerne and Lake Zug to Einsiedeln. Upon arrival, celebrate Mass at Einsiedeln Abbey. Visit the Benedictine Monastery of Einsiedeln dedicated to Our Lady of the Hermits. The Abbey received its dedication due to its first inhabitant in the region, around the year 850 A.D., a monk named St. Meinrad. This evening, you will return to your hotel in Lucerne. Enjoy a farewell dinner and overnight at the hotel in Lucerne.

tourDays.title: Exploring Salzburg
tourDays.description: Our day in Salzburg starts with a nourishing breakfast, after which we attend Mass at the ancient St. Peterâs Abbey, a spiritual center that has served the faithful for over a millennium. Following Mass, we immerse ourselves in the cityâs history with a walking tour of the heart of Salzburg. Narrow streets and secluded passageways whisper tales of its medieval roots, while the grandeur of the Archbishopâs Residence at DomPlatz speaks to the Catholic Churchâs enduring influence. The gardens of Mirabell Palace, a setting made famous by âThe Sound of Music,â offer a tranquil space for prayer and reflection. The grandeur of the Romanesque Cathedral and the serenity of the Nonnberg Convent of Benedictine nuns further inspire our faith. Mozartâs birthplace beckons us with its cultural significance, and the gardens and hidden trick fountains of Hellbrunn Palace provide a delightfully unexpected close to our day. As we gather for dinner, we share our experiences, impressions, and the ways in which our journey is touching our hearts.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Attend Mass at St. Peterâs Abbey; Walking tour of Salzburg; Visit Archbishopâs Residence at DomPlatz; Visit Mirabell Palace gardens; Visit Salzburg Cathedral; Visit Nonnberg Convent; Visit Mozartâs birthplace; Visit Hellbrunn Palace gardens and trick fountains; Dinner and group reflection

tourDays.title: Silent Night Chapel and Salzburg Christmas markets
tourDays.description: Following breakfast we will visit the Silent Night Chapel, commemorating the brief Christmas Day peace that took place during World War I. The chapel was built on the site of the former Nikolauskirche, where the Christmas carol was first performed on Christmas Eve in 1818. Return to Salzburg for a free afternoon to explore the magical Christmas markets: Salzburg Christkindlmarkt & Hellbrunner Adventzauber. Dinner and overnight and dinner.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Visit Silent Night Chapel; Free afternoon to explore Christmas markets; Visit Salzburg Christkindlmarkt; Visit Hellbrunner Adventzauber; Dinner and overnight

tourDays.title: Mariazell and Melk en route to Vienna
tourDays.description: As we depart from Salzburg after breakfast, we traverse the Austrian mountains towards Mariazell, a revered pilgrimage site. We visit the Mariazell Basilica, also known as the Basilica of the Birth of the Virgin Mary, housing the miraculous statue associated with the foundation of a monastic cell in 1157. We continue to Melk, known for the imposing baroque Melk Abbey. Overlooking the Danube River, the Abbey is the final resting place of Saint Coloman of Stockerau and members of the House of Babenberg, Austriaâs first ruling dynasty. After exploring and reflecting in Melk, we journey to Vienna, the capital of Austria, where we share a meal and prepare for the next leg of our journey.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Travel from Salzburg to Mariazell; Visit Mariazell Basilica; Travel to Melk; Visit Melk Abbey; Travel to Vienna; Group meal in Vienna

tourDays.title: Vienna cultural and religious tour
tourDays.description: Our day begins with breakfast and a tour of Vienna, home to great composers like Johann Strauss and Mozart. Our visit to St. Stephenâs Cathedral, a symbol of Vienna and a significant Gothic structure, allows us to witness the miraculous image of Our Lady of Mariapoch. We tour the cathedral, with (time permitting) the brave among us climbing the 343 steps to the top of the spire. Our journey continues to the Schonbrunn Royal Palace, a summer residence with a Hall of Mirrors where a young Mozart performed. The palaceâs inclusion in UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Sites further confirms its significance. Our day concludes with a visit to the Belvedere Palace, Karlsplatz and its Church of St. Charles Borromeo, and Otto Wagnerâs Stadtbahn pavilions. Amidst our explorations, we pause for a coffee break to savor famous Viennese pastries like the Sacher cake. We share dinner and reflect on the dayâs experiences as we return to our hotel.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast; Visit St. Stephenâs Cathedral; Optional climb of cathedral spire (343 steps); Visit Schonbrunn Palace; Visit Belvedere Palace; Visit Karlsplatz and Church of St. Charles Borromeo; See Otto Wagnerâs Stadtbahn pavilions; Coffee break (pastries like Sacher cake); Dinner and reflection

tourDays.title: Lourdes pilgrimage activities
tourDays.description: Mass at the Grotto, enjoy a video presentation telling the story of Lourdes, and walk in the footsteps of St Bernadette. See Boly Mill where St. Bernadette was born and the Cachot, an abandoned prison where Bernadette's impoverished family lived. Join your prayers with those of pilgrims from around the world as you pray for the sick, drink water from the miraculous spring or submerge yourself in the healing baths. Experience Christ's love as you walk the life-sized Stations of the Cross overlooking the holy Grotto. Kneel in the chapel built on the very rock of the Grotto. Evenings are for Blessed Sacrament Procession before dinner. (Candlelight procession and group rosary April through October only.)
