tourDays.title: Depart for Barcelona Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.description:
Depart for Barcelona
Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.

tourDays.title: Day 2
tourDays.description: Arrive in Barcelona Upon arrival in Barcelona, collect your luggage in the baggage claim area, and then continue to the arrivalâs hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. You will be escorted to the vehicle for your transfer to your hotel. Upon arrival, you will check-in and have free time to rest and refresh or explore. This evening, you will enjoy a welcoming dinner, followed by an overnight in Barcelona.

tourDays.title: Day 3
tourDays.description: Barcelona - Manresa - Montserrat This morning, your day will begin with breakfast and a sightseeing tour of Barcelona! Enjoy the stunning panoramic views of the Port of Barcelona, Montjuic, Plaza de EspaÃ±a, and Plaza de Catalunya. The Port was created 2,000 years ago on the coastal area, in order to protect and provide access for ships and goods. Currently, it is home to numerous walking areas, businesses, cultural and sporting events. Plaza de EspaÃ±a is right outside the center of town and was formerly known for its old bull-fighting ring. Presently, the Plaza is renowned for containing the Museum of Catalan art, situated on the side of Montjuic. Plaza de Catalunya is located in central Barcelona, and is known for its fountains and statues. Your day of touring will continue with a guided walk through the Gothic Quarter that contains remains from an ancient Roman village, including the Cathedral of Barcelona. We will continue to the Eixample Quarter to visit Antoni Gaudiâs stunning Roman Catholic Basilica, La Sagrada Familia, which was finished after 144 years of construction. In the afternoon, we will travel to Manresa, with a visit to the Sanctuary of Saint Ignatius of Loyola and the Holy Cave where St. Ignatius lived. Continue to Montserrat, home to the miraculous Black Madonna and arrive in time for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 4
tourDays.description: Montserrat After breakfast, we visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Montserrat, located on a rugged mountainside. According to Catholic tradition, St. Luke carved the statue of the Black Madonna around 50 A.D. and brought it to Spain. While in Spain, it was hidden from the Moor, and then later rediscovered by shepherds. In 880 A.D., the shepherds and the Bishop of Manresa were drawn to a grotto by a bright light and heavenly music. Upon discovery of the statue of the Black Madonna in the grotto, the Bishop of Manresa suggested that it be moved to Manresa. However, the status was too heavy that it could not be lifted. As a result, the Virgin remained in Montserrat and continued to be venerated there for centuries. As years progressed, a number of chapels were built upon the site and in the eleventh century, the abbot bishop Oliba founded a monastery on Montserrat, next to one of these chapels. Dinner and an overnight in Montserrat.

tourDays.title: Day 5
tourDays.description: Montserrat - Zaragoza - Madrid This morning, following breakfast, your group will depart for Zaragoza. While in Zaragoza, you will have the opportunity to visit the magnificent Basilica del Pilar that was built upon the site of where Our Lady appeared to St. James. In 44 A.D. St. James the Greater was spreading the Gospel in Spain, but, making very little progress and questioning his mission. According to Catholic Tradition, the Virgin Mary, who was still living in Jerusalem, bi-located and appeared to St. James the Greater to boost his morale. While inside the Basilica, you will view the pillar that was carried by angels and from where Our Lady appeared. Following your visit to the Basilica del Pilar, you will visit La Seo Cathedral (Cathedral of Zaragoza). Formally known as the Church of San Vicente during the Visigoth period, it contains architectural elements of Gothic, Mudejar, Renaissance and Baroque styles. In addition to the famous cathedral, Zaragoza is also known for its folklore and local gastronomy, both of which will be explored on your walking tour of the city. This evening, your group will continue on to Madrid, where you will eat your dinner and enjoy a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 6
tourDays.description: Madrid - Toledo This morning, you will awaken in the capital city of Spain! Following breakfast, you will enjoy a tour of Madrid, including the Prado Museum. This afternoon, you will depart for Toledo. Toledo is a city set upon a rocky mound, isolated on three sides by a looping gorge of the Rio Tajo. It is known as the City of Three Religions or Cultures because the Christians, Jews, and Moors have lived peacefully in this city for centuries. Each inch of this outcrop has churches, synagogues, mosques and houses heaped upon one another in a haphazard spiral in which the cobbled lanes infiltrate with its best efforts. During your time in this city, you will view the some of the grandest treasures such as, the glorious Gothic Cathedral that was built upon the Great Mosque of Toledo. Visit La Iglesia de Santo Tome, best known for housing El Grecoâs most famous painting and the Sinagoga del TrÃ¡nsito, known for its impeccable stucco inscriptions. Additionally, you will visit a number of monuments such as La Puerta de Bisagras, La Puerta del Cambron, La Puerta del Sol and many others. Your day will culminate with a return transfer to Madrid where you will enjoy dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 7
tourDays.description: Madrid - Astorga - O' Cebreiro - Santiago de Compostela Today, you will depart Madrid and head towards the city of Santiago de Compostela. While in route, you will make a stop in Astorga, with a visit to the Bishopâs Palace built by Antonio Gaudi, which holds the Museum of El Camino. Later this afternoon, you will enter Galicia, by way of the city Lugo. Your first stop will be to O Cebreiro, the first village in the region of Lugo and nestled in the mountains at an altitude of 1,300 meters. While in O Cebreiro, you will have the opportunity to view the iconic palloza styles houses, and the site of a Eucharistic Miracle that occurred in the year 1300. In the evening, you will proceed to Santiago de Compostela for your dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 8
tourDays.description: Santiago de Compostela This morning, you will walk a few miles of El Camino, and immerse yourselves in the fragrant eucalyptus groves and experience the breathtaking scenery. Later this morning attend the International Pilgrim Mass at the Cathedral of St. James. After Mass, there will be free time for lunch and visit the Cathedral of Santiago. Formed by Galician granite, this Cathedral is one of the finest architectural examples in Europe as it encompasses Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque styles. Additionally, the Cathedral contains numerous and valuable pieces of art that truly captivate the eye. Upon entering the Cathedral, tradition will lead as you hug the dazzling statue of St. James. Following this intimate embrace, you will descent into the crypt where the Patron Saint of Pilgrimsâ relics are kept. After that, you will enjoy a sightseeing tour of the city. Some stops on your tour include the Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, Gemirez Palace, Franco Street, and much more. Your evening will be free to spend at your leisure until a final dinner with your group. You will spend a final overnight in Santiago de Compostela.

tourDays.title: Day 9
tourDays.description: Santiago de Compostela â Rome Your last day in Spain will begin with breakfast at your hotel, followed by a transfer to the Santiago Airport for your flight to Rome. You will say âhasta luegoâ (see you later) to new friends made on this journey but welcome to Rome, also known as, âThe Eternal Cityâ! Upon landing at Rome airport, claim your baggage and proceed to the Arrivals Hall, where your tour guide and/or driver will greet you. Following check-in at the hotel, enjoy some free time to unpack, relax or explore Rome on your own. Your tour escort may suggest places to visit. Later this afternoon, between 3:00 PM and 3:30 PM, your group will meet in the hotel lobby for a meet and greet with fellow pilgrims and your priest. You will depart together for Mass, and following Mass, you will attend a welcome dinner. After dinner you have to opportunity to join in a walk to St. Peterâs Square for the Rosary (optional).

tourDays.title: Day 10
tourDays.description: Rome: Papal Audience - Piazza Navona - Pantheon - Basilica of St. John the Lateran - Holy Stairs - Basilica of St. Mary Major This morning we attend the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square or at the Audience Hall. The Audience is celebrated each Wednesday by His Holiness, The Pope (pending the papal schedule). (During the month of July, Papal Audiences are cancelled while the Holy Father resides in Castel Gandolfo. For tours occurring during this time, the Audience will be replaced with an excursion to Castel Gandolfo with the itinerary below: Upon arrival in Castel Gandolfo, we will visit Piazza della LibertÃ . Here, we will take a moment to admire the impressive facade of the Papal Palace, the Popeâs summer residence. Our visit continues with an exploration of the Papal Palace itself, including the Vatican Observatory and the breathtaking Barberini Gardens, which offer panoramic views of Lake Albano.) Next, head to the Piazza Navona area for some free time and lunch (on your own). This afternoon, visit the oldest of the four major Basilicas in Rome, the Archbasilica of St. John the Lateran, the cathedral church and seat of the Bishop of Rome. Cross the street to the very steps that lead up to the praetorium of Pontius Pilate in Jerusalem which Jesus climbed on His way to trial during his Passion. Holy Mass will be celebrated by our priest at the Basilica of St. Mary Major, dedicated to Our Blessed Mother. This Basilica contains a relic from the manger of the infant Jesus. Dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 11
tourDays.description: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica - Vatican Museum - Appian Way - Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls - Catacombs Today we tour St. Peterâs Basilica, built on the site where St. Peter the Apostle was martyred. Here, youâll have the opportunity to view Michelangeloâs Pieta sculpture, pray at the tombs of Pope Benedict XVI and St. John Paul II. Next you will visit the Vatican Museum, where you can see the Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, and Sistine Chapel. After lunch, continue down the Appian Way, one of the earliest roads built in ancient Rome to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls and the Catacombs. Dinner and overnight in Rome.

tourDays.title: Day 12
tourDays.description: Rome - Montecassino - San Giovanni Rotondo Following breakfast, you will board your bus to enjoy the scenic route to Montecassino. Passing through the Roman countryside that is known for its villas and vineyards. During the bus ride, your tour escort will share interesting information regarding the spiritual, historical, and cultural aspects of Italy. Montecassino, the principle monastery of the Benedictine Order, was founded by Saint Benedict around 530 A.D. Following the tour, there will be an opportunity to visit the gift shop, before you board the bus to continue toward San Giovanni Rotondo, the hometown of Saint St. Padre Pio. Upon arrival in San Giovanni Rotondo, you will check-in, enjoy dinner in a restaurant, and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 13
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo (View Incorrupt Body of St. Padre Pio) - Monte Sant' Angelo This morning, after breakfast, you will visit the Old Church. After Mass, you will tour the sanctuary, it is here you will view the crucifix, in front of which St. Pio received the stigmata. Visit the confessional from where St. Pio spent an innumerable amount of hours listening to confessions. Next, you will board the bus and travel along the beautiful Gargano Peninsula to the Grotto of St. Michael the Archangel, a shrine consecrated by St. Michael. At this grotto, St. Michael appeared to a Bishop to assure him that his diocese would not be annihilated as he feared. Following the visit to the grotto, enjoy free time. On the way back to San Giovanni Rotondo, view breathtaking views of the ocean and surrounding countryside. Upon arrival, you will have time for devotion and reflection. Dinner and an overnight in San Giovanni Rotondo. *Candlelight Procession â Between May and October attend the weekly Candlelight Procession at the Sanctuary of St. Pio after dinner, at 9:00 PM. These processions are lit by candlelight, and are guided by the Most Holy Rosary. Following this prayerful experience, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 14
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Lanciano - Loreto - Assisi After breakfast, you we leave for Assisi. On the way we stop in Lanciano for private Mass at the Convent/Church of Saint Francis built on top of the antique Church of St. Longinus â the site of a Eucharistic Miracle that occurred in the eighth century. At the time of the miracle, there was a Basilian monk, who struggled with the belief in the Real Presence in the Eucharist. During the time of Mass, the monk, with doubt in his voice, said the words of consecration and the bread and wine transformed into physical flesh and blood. Leave for Marian shrine of Loreto to visit the Holy House of Nazareth and the beautiful Madonna of Loreto. Tradition holds that this is the house in which Mary first prayed the Magnificat, in which Jesus grew to manhood, and in which the Holy Family lived, before it was transported several times by angels, to its current location. End the day in Assisi, hometown of St. Francis and St. Clare, with dinner and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 15
tourDays.description: Assisi As you visit the birthplace of St. Francis, you will become captivated as the atmosphere has not changed since St. Francis began his ministry, in the early 13th-century. You will start your tour at the St. Francis Basilica, visit his tomb of St. Francis, and have the opportunity to view a series of frescoes depicting his life, along with a few of the saintâs possessions. Followed by a visit to the Santuario Della Spogliazione where St. Carlo Acutisâ tomb is located. Carlo is the first millennial to be declared a Saint who loved the Real Presence of Jesus in the Eucharist. From there, you will continue on a walking tour through this picturesque town, including the birthplace of St. Francis, and end with a tour of the Church that honors St. Clare, the foundress of the Poor Clare Sisters. This Saint followed the teachings of St. Francis very closely by also living a life of poverty and humility. Enjoy some free time on your own â you may take this time for additional prayer, shop in the many gift shops or enjoy a nice lunch. After lunch, you will board the bus, which will take you outside of the walls of Assisi, to the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels. This is where St. Francis spent most of life. This Basilica is made up of two structures, both of which you will visit. The first structure, is the âPorziuncolaâ, which is where St. Francis founded his order of the Friar Minor (Franciscans). The second, is the âCapella del Transitoâ, which is the place of St. Francisâ death. During your time here, you will have the opportunity to visit the beautiful Rose Garden where St. Francis and other friars lived, as well as the cave where the Saint retired to pray. Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 16
tourDays.description: Assisi - Gubbio - La Verna - Assisi After breakfast, you will drive through the beautiful Umbrian mountains to Gubbio. Enjoy this medieval town with a visit of St. Francis Church, where you will be celebrating Mass. After Mass, visit a town that seems painted onto the hill, a succession of backdrops against which towers and houses stand out, all embraced by walls. The town had been freed by St. Francis from a terrible and fierce wolf who afflicted it. After lunch on your own, continue to La Verna, the place where St. Francis, over the years, had been seven times, the last time in 1224 where he received the stigmata. Here you will be able to pray in the Chapel of the Stigmata, the Basilica and the Chapel of Saint Mary of the Angels. You will also be able to admire the beautiful artworks of Andrea della Robbia. Return to Assisi for dinner and your last overnight in Italy.

tourDays.title: Day 17
tourDays.description: Assisi - Siena - Florence Breakfast, followed by a scenic drive to the Tuscan city of Siena. This medieval city is the birthplace of St. Catherine âDoctor of the Churchâ, and the Apostle of Italy, St. Bernardine. Visit of the Basilica of St. Catherine (which is also known as the Basilica of St. Domenico). St. Catherine passed a large part of her life inside the walls of this Basilica. It is here you will also view the incorrupt head of St. Catherine. After, visit the Shrine of St. Catherine, which occupies the site of her family home. Enjoy your walking tour through the Siena including a visit to its Cathedral (Duomo di Siena). Conclude at one of Italyâs finest squares, the Piazza Del Campo, where you will be given free time to spend at your own leisure. There are a number of restaurants surrounding the square to have lunch, as well as shops for gifts and souvenirs. Continue on to Florence. Upon arrival in Florence, you will notice immediately that it is the land for art lovers. Some of the most world renowned artists are from Florence such as, Dante, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, Botticelli, Donatello, and many others. For the remainder of the afternoon, you will have the opportunity to explore the streets of Florence at leisure. In the evening gather for dinner, followed by an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 18
tourDays.description: Florence In Florence, your day begins with breakfast, followed by a guided tour. The tour starts at the Church of the Holy Cross, the Santa Croce, where many nobles are buried, such as Michelangelo, Galileo, and Machiavelli. Continue to walk by Piazza Signorina, Palazzo Vecchio, Uffizi, Ponte Vecchio, and Republic Square to the Santa Maria del Fiore. This Cathedral is an iconic piece of architecture of the city of Florence. It was designed by Filippo Brunelleschi in the 13th century. Next, a visit to LâAccademia, the well-known art gallery. At this gallery, you will have the opportunity to view the work from artists such as Botticelli, Ghirlandaio, Pontormo and the ever famous sculpture by Michelangelo, David. This afternoon you will have time to explore Florence on your own. Return to hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 19
tourDays.description: Florence - Padua Following breakfast at your hotel, board the motor coach for your transfer to Padua. This Northern Italian city honors the âPatron Saint of Lost Things and Causesâ, St. Anthony. You will begin a sightseeing tour of the city, including a view of one of the oldest Universities in Italy, the University of Padua, as well as the Basilica of Santa Giustina, the âPatron Saint of Padua.â The tour will conclude at the Basilica of St. Anthony, where you will have the opportunity to visit his tomb. Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 20
tourDays.description: Padua - Venice (Full Day Excursion) Today, you will have early breakfast and then board your bus to depart to the magical city of Venice. After Mass, enjoy a tour of the âcity paved with water!â Your walking tour includes a visit to St. Markâs Square, the largest square in the city and the site of many government buildings; the Golden Basilica of San Marco, known for the great mosaics that depict the Old and New Testament of the Bible; the Bridge of Sigh, a bridge that will bring eternal love to those who drift below it. You will also have the chance to view the Dogesâ Palace (Dukeâs Palace), which served as the seat of the Government for the Republic of Venice for centuries. Return to Padua for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.description: Arrive in Santiago de Compostela Upon arrival, you will be met by your tour guide and/or driver and head to your hotel in Santiago de Compostela. You will have free time before dinner and an overnight in Santiago de Compostela.

tourDays.title: Day 3
tourDays.description: Santiago de Compostela This morning, you will awaken in the beautiful city of Santiago de Compostela! Formed by Galician granite, the cityâs Cathedral is one of the finest architectural structures in Europe as it encompasses Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. Additionally, the Cathedral contains numerous valuable pieces of art that truly captivate the eye. Upon entering the Cathedral, pilgrims traditionally hug the statue of St. James. You will then descend into the crypt where the Patron Saint of Pilgrimsâ relics is kept. Following your visit, enjoy free time for lunch on your own before your sightseeing tour of the city. Some stops on the tour include Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, Gelmirez Palace, Franco Street, and much more. Your evening will be free to spend at your leisure until dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 4
tourDays.description: Santiago de Compostela - Lisbon After breakfast, we depart for Lisbon. This afternoon, we will enjoy a panoramic sightseeing tour of the coastal city of Lisbon. Stop at St. Jeromeâs Monastery, built to give thanks to the Virgin Mary for guiding Vasco da Gama on his voyage that linked Europe and Asia. Drive by the Belem Quarter that contains the iconic entryway to the Lisbon harbor: the Belem Tower. This important landmark has many beautiful sculptures, including one of St. Vincent and Our Lady of Safe Homecoming. We will pass by the â25th of April Bridgeâ, which is the oldest bridge that connects the Tagus River of Lisbon. Drive by the Discoveries Monument, which commemorates the Great Explorers who, as a result of their explorations, brought Portugal to a standing of wealth and power during the Age of Discovery. This shipâs prow-shaped structure stands where the Great Explorers began their expeditions. Enjoy a view of the Basilica of the Star, Rossio Square, Commerce Square, and the Marquee of Pombal Square. Our last stop will be St. Anthonyâs Church, where we will celebrate Mass. Although the patron Saint of lost things is known as St. Anthony of Padua (Italy), he was born in Lisbon, Portugal. The Church was built upon the site of his birth. Saint John Paul II visited St. Anthonyâs Church in 1982 on his way to Fatima. The former Pope stopped at this Church on his way to Fatima to pray to Our Lady in thanksgiving. Saint John Paul II credited Our Lady for saving him from being killed when he was shot one year prior in 1981. After Mass, we will check in at the hotel and enjoy dinner followed by a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 5
tourDays.description: Lisbon - Santarem - Fatima Today, we will head to Fatima. On the way, we will stop in the town of Santarem for Mass at St. Stephenâs Church. Here you will have the opportunity to venerate a 13th-century Eucharistic Miracle. Continue to Fatima, a Hamlet of Aljustrel, the birthplace and home of the three shepherd children. Dinner and overnight in Fatima.

tourDays.title: Day 6
tourDays.description: Fatima Today will be a memorable experience as you pray and meditate upon one of Our Blessed Motherâs apparition sites. Our Lady appeared to three shepherd children: Venerable Sister Lucia (age 10), St. Jacinta (age 7), and St. Francisco (age 9). These apparitions occurred monthly from May until October of 1917. Historically, as the entire world was in turmoil, Our Ladyâs most prominent message was to pray for world peace. The destruction of the world at that point in history was also mentioned by Our Lady, particularly in her second secret to the children. Our profoundly reflective day begins with a visit to the Little Chapel of the Apparitions. This simple yet modern chapel is where the Virgin Mary first appeared on May 13, 1917. Next, you will see the stunning neoclassical church, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary. This Sacred space contains the tombs of St. Francisco, St. Jacinta, and Sister Lucia. View the monument that commemorates the Sacred Heart of Jesus in the square. In honor of Our Ladyâs requests to pray the Rosary, the Basilica also features fifteen altars each dedicated to a mystery of the Rosary. Visit the Museum with the âFatima: Light and Peaceâ exhibition. Continue with a visit to the Holy Trinity Basilica. After free time for lunch, we will experience Christâs unconditional love by participating in the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra. The âSacred Wayâ marks the path taken by the shepherd children of Fatima to their first apparition with Our Lady. It is composed of fifteen small chapels commemorating the Passion of Our Lord. The fifteenth station, the Resurrection, can be found close to the Chapel of Calvary, dedicated to St. Stephen, King of Hungary. Ending the day with a visit to Valinhos, the site of Our Ladyâs August 1917 apparition and the first and third apparition of the Angel. Your night will conclude with private devotions and a candlelight procession, as requested by Our Lady in 1917. Enjoy dinner and a comfortable nightâs rest in Fatima.

tourDays.title: Day 7
tourDays.description: Fatima - Salamanca Depart Fatima and head to Salamanca, following a full breakfast at the hotel. Salamanca is a city in the Castilla y Leon region known for its large university. It is the oldest university in Spain that is still active. Our walking tour will take us to many famous sites. Visit the grand Plaza Mayor, an iconic square filled with food, shopping, and city events. See La Clerecia, a church and college of the Jesuit Order that was constructed in the 17th century. Next, visit La Casa de las Conchas, which is currently a public library and a monument decorated with shells, which symbolizes the ever-famous pilgrimage to Santiago (El Camino). Walk by the University of Salamanca, the oldest University in Spain and the third oldest in Europe. Walk across the Roman Bridge, which extends along the River Tormes and is a national monument. See La Iglesia de San Marcos, which is constructed in the Romanesque style and contains breathtaking paintings that portray many scenes of Our Ladyâs life. You will also see La Iglesia de San Martin, a Church devoted to St. Martin of Tours, the patron saint of beggars and those most in need. Visit the inside of the two joint Salamanca Cathedrals (old and new). The first is a Romanesque style, and the other is a Gothic style. Following this eventful day, you will return to your hotel for a delicious meal with your group and an overnight at your hotel in Salamanca.

tourDays.title: Day 8
tourDays.description: Salamanca - Alba de Tormes - Avila - Burgos This morning, after breakfast, you will board the bus and enjoy a short transfer to the village of Alba de Tormes. This town is home to the Carmelite Monastery that Saint Teresa founded in 1571. Upon arrival in Alba de Tormes, your group will celebrate Mass at this Monastery where the Saint died and is buried. Following Mass, you can visit the museum dedicated to St. Teresa of Avila, which also holds her incorrupt heart and left arm. Your group will enjoy free time for lunch on your own before continuing to the medieval city of Avila. Upon arrival, you will immediately notice the perfectly preserved 11th-century walls surrounding the old town. The conservation of architecture in this city, to which St. Teresa was born, deems its shrines, convents, and churches necessary to visit on any Catholic pilgrimage. The Cathedral de Avila encompasses the Romanesque, Gothic, and Renaissance styles of its time within its artwork and architecture. La Basilica de San Vicente in Avila stands on the site of the martyrdom of St. Vincent. Visit the Incarnation Convent, where St. Teresa became a nun. Saint Therese convinced Saint John of the Cross to reform the male Carmelite order, the reform she started when she met Saint John in Medina del Campo. After walking in the footsteps of St. Teresa, continue your journey to Burgos. Upon arrival in the historic capital of Old Castile, enjoy dinner. Following dinner, you will have the opportunity to explore the city of Burgos and admire its magnificent limestone Gothic-style cathedral. Late this evening, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 9
tourDays.description:
Burgos - Loyola - Lourdes Following breakfast, transfer from Burgos to Loyola to visit the birthplace of St. Ignatius, founder of the Jesuit Order. St. Ignatius dedicated himself to becoming a soldier of the Christian faith, and as a result of many tribulations, he wrote the ever-famous Spiritual Exercises. You will see the 17th-century Basilica dedicated to this remarkable Saint in Loyola. The Basilica is part of a series of buildings surrounding the âHoly House,â the birthplace of St. Ignatius. When you visit these Holy places, you will also have the opportunity to pray in the most venerated room, where St. Ignatius prayed and began his conversion. After meditating on the life of this founder of the Jesuit Order, you will enjoy free time for lunch and board the bus for the next destination. We will continue to Lourdes with a spectacular view of the Pyrenees Mountains. Upon arrival in Lourdes, you will check in to your hotel and enjoy a splendid dinner and peaceful overnight.
Days 10 & 11: Lourdes Over the next two days, you will stay in a small town in the Pyrenees Mountains. During your time in Lourdes, you will pray and meditate at the site of Our Ladyâs apparitions. Our Lady first appeared to Bernadette in 1858 and announced herself as âThe Immaculate Conceptionâ near the Grotto of Massabielle. During the first two apparitions, little Bernadette prayed the Rosary with Our Lady and left without exchanging words. During the following apparitions, Our Lady emphasized Godâs love for us and the necessity of performing acts of penance for sinners. Throughout your time in Lourdes, you will have the opportunity to attend Mass at the Grotto, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette. Watch a video presentation that explains the story of Lourdes. Wash your hands, wash your face, and drink the water of the miraculous spring. Finish with a short prayer: âOur Lady of Lourdes, pray for us. St. Bernadette, pray for us. O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.â Experience Christâs unconditional love as you meditate upon the âlife-sizeâ Stations of the Cross that overlook the Grotto of Massabielle. In Lourdes, you will walk in and meditate upon the footsteps of St. Bernadette. Your group will have the opportunity to see Boly Mill, the birthplace of St. Bernadette, and the âCachot,â an abandoned prison where Bernadetteâs impoverished family lived. Each evening, following dinner, you can attend the candlelight procession and pray the Rosary before a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 12
tourDays.description: Lourdes - Paris - Lisieux (St. Therese - the Little Flower) Today, you will enjoy breakfast before departing for Pau or Lourdes Airport for your short flight to Paris, continue on to Lisieux. According to Pope Pius X, St. Therese of Lisieux was the âgreatest saint of modern times.â Her extraordinary love for God and service to humanity will come alive as you walk in the great Saintâs footsteps. During your visit, you will see the beautiful Basilica of St. Therese and its magnificent mosaics and stained glass windows. You will have the opportunity to view relics, clothing, and personal objects that belonged to St. Therese when you visit her family home, Les Buissonnets. Additionally, you will tour the Carmelite Convent, which she entered in 1888 and where she is now buried. Dinner and overnight at your hotel in Lisieux.

tourDays.title: Day 13
tourDays.description: Lisieux - Landing Beaches - American Cemetery Upon waking up in Lisieux, enjoy breakfast, and then your group will celebrate Mass. After Mass we will travel to the Normandy Landing beaches. The Normandy landings were the landing operations, which took place on Tuesday, June 6, 1944 (termed D-Day) by the Allies of Normandy during World War II. As the largest seaborne invasion in history, the operation began the liberation of German-occupied northwestern Europe from Nazi control and contributed to the Alliesâ victory on the Western Front. Continue to visit The Normandy American Cemetery and Memorial, a World War II cemetery and memorial in Colleville-Sur-Mer, Normandy, France, honoring the American troops that died in Europe during World War II. Many of the brave American soldiers of World War II are buried here, and it is encouraged to say a prayer in thanksgiving for their courage. Return to Lisieux for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 14
tourDays.description: Lisieux â Chartres â Paris This morning, your day begins with an early breakfast before we depart for Chartres, known worldwide for its massive Cathedral Notre Dame and its incredible stained-glass windows from the 12th and 13th centuries. The World Heritage site, UNESCO, calls the Cathedral âthe high point of French Gothic artâ and a âmasterpieceâ. Pilgrims will also be able to venerate a precious relic of the Veil of Our Lady which is currently on display at the back of the main altar of the Cathedral of Chartres. You will have some free time for lunch in the quaint town of Chartres. After lunch, we will continue to Paris to check-in at your hotel, followed by some free time before a delicious dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 15
tourDays.description: Paris Following breakfast, we will celebrate Mass. Following Mass enjoy a full day of sightseeing including the magnificent Sacre Coeur Basilica atop Montmartre Hill. The Basilica, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, was originally built in 1914 as an act of penance for infidelity that France experienced during that time. See the beautiful mosaic of the Risen Christ and the remarkable Grand Organ. Visit the the Tombs of many notable Cardinals. Time permitting, you may have the opportunity to ascend a staircase to the Dome, where you will take in a breathtaking panoramic view of Paris. Continue with a visit of the Chapel of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal, where we will have the opportunity to view the incorrupt body of St. Catherine Laboure. The Saintâs guardian angel led her to the chapel where the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared to her. During the apparitions, Our Lady repeatedly instructed the making and purpose of the Miraculous Medal. According to the Blessed Virgin Mary, those who wear the Miraculous Medal will receive special protection and abundant graces. Following this prayerful and reflective experience, we will walk to Saint Vincent de Paul Church. Next, on our tour of Paris, we will visit one of the most incredible churches in the world: Notre Dame Cathedral. The Cathedral has recently been re-opened to visitors. Guided group tours are scheduled to resume in June 2025. Board a bus tour and see some of the most recognizable symbols of Paris, including the Eiffel Tower, the Invalides, the LâArch de Triomphe, and the Champ-Elysees, the worldâs most famous boulevard. Your busy day ends with a lovely meal and a comfortable overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 16
tourDays.description: Paris - Rome Join an early morning departure from Paris for your short flight to Rome. Upon arrival, your escort will warmly greet you and welcome you to Italy. Transfer to your hotel, where your guide will introduce you to your fellow pilgrims and the priest who will be with you for the rest of the journey. Make your way to Mass, followed by a welcome dinner with wine. This evening, you may walk to St. Peterâs Square to pray the Rosary (optional).

tourDays.title: Day 17
tourDays.description: Rome: Papal Audience - Piazza Navona â Pantheon - Basilica of St. John the Lateran â Holy Stairs - Basilica of St. Mary Major This morning we will attend the Papal Audience at St. Peterâs Square or inside the Audience Hall. The Audience is celebrated each Wednesday by His Holiness, the Pope (pending the papal schedule). (During the month of July, Papal Audiences are cancelled while the Holy Father resides in Castel Gandolfo. For tours occurring during this time, the Audience will be replaced with an excursion to Castel Gandolfo with the following itinerary: Upon arrival in Castel Gandolfo, we will visit Piazza della LibertÃ . Here, we will take a moment to admire the impressive facade of the Papal Palace, the Popeâs summer residence. Our visit continues with an exploration of the Papal Palace itself, including the Vatican Observatory and the breathtaking Barberini Gardens, which offer panoramic views of Lake Albano.) Next, head to the Piazza Navona area for some free time and lunch (on your own). This afternoon, visit the oldest of the four major Basilicas in Rome, the Archbasilica of St. John the Lateran, the cathedral church and seat of the Bishop of Rome. Cross the street to the very steps that lead up to the praetorium of Pontius Pilate in Jerusalem, which Jesus climbed on His way to trial during His Passion. Our priest will celebrate Holy Mass at the Basilica of St. Mary Major, which is dedicated to Our Blessed Mother. Enjoy dinner and an overnight in Rome.

tourDays.title: Day 18
tourDays.description: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica - Vatican Museum - Appian Way - Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls - Catacombs Today, we will tour St. Peterâs Basilica, which was built on the site where St. Peter the Apostle was martyred. Here, you will have the opportunity to view Michelangeloâs Pieta sculpture and pray at the tombs of Pope Benedict XVI and St. John Paul II. Next, you will visit the Vatican Museum, where you can see the Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, and Sistine Chapel. After lunch, continue down the Appian Way, one of the earliest roads built in ancient Rome, to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls and the Catacombs. Have dinner and a restful overnight in Rome.

tourDays.title: Budapest â Esztergom â Szentendre â Budapest
tourDays.description: Breakfast on-board followed by your departure to Esztergom, a medieval city lying picturesquely on the Danube Bend. We will also visit Szentendre, the charming, ethnic artist colony with its winding lanes, seven aspiring church towers, colorful houses, narrow side streets, genuine Mediterranean ambience and scores of museums, galleries, guest houses and warm restaurants. It is the most frequented tourist destination of the Danube Bend. Return to the ship for lunch. After lunch, depart for a tour of Buda, the upper part of Budapest. Visit the Castle District and see the main attractions of the area: Fisherman's Bastion which takes its name from the guild of fishermen that were responsible for defending this stretch of city walls in the Middle Ages, followed by Matyas Church, a gorgeous Romanesque style church whose Ecclesiastical Art museum houses numerous sacred relics and medieval stone carvings, including replicas of the Hungarian royal crown and coronation jewels. Return to the ship for dinner and a folklore show this evening.

tourDays.title: Depart for Lisbon Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.description:
Depart for Lisbon
Make your way to your local airport, where you will board your overnight flight(s). Your meals will be served on board.

tourDays.title: Day 2
tourDays.description: Arrive in Lisbon Upon landing at Lisbon Airport, head to baggage claim and collect your luggage. Proceed to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. After meeting your group in the hotel lobby at 2:30 PM, board the bus and begin a panoramic sightseeing tour of Lisbon. We will stop at St. Jeromeâs Monastery, built to give thanks to the Virgin Mary for guiding Vasco da Gama on his voyage that linked Europe and Asia. Continue to drive by the Belem Quarter, which contains the iconic entryway to the Lisbon harbor, the Belem Tower. This important historic structure has many beautiful sculptures, such as depictions of St. Vincent and Our Lady of Safe Homecoming. The next stop is St. Anthonyâs Church, built upon the site of Saintâs birth; it is here that we will celebrate Mass. Although the patron Saint of lost things is known as St. Anthony of Padua (Italy), he was born in Lisbon, Portugal. This Church is built upon St. Anthonyâs birth site and is also where Saint John Paul II visited in 1982. After Mass, we will drive to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 3
tourDays.description: Lisbon - Santarem - Fatima Today, we will travel north to the old city of Santarem. We will attend Mass at the Church of St. Stephen, which holds a 13th-century Eucharistic Miracle. Continue to Fatima and visit the Hamlet of Aljustrel, the home of the three shepherd children. Visit the Parish Church and Fatima Parish Cemetery. Continue to your hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 4
tourDays.description: Fatima Today will be a memorable experience as you pray and meditate upon one of Our Blessed Motherâs apparition sites. Our Lady appeared to three shepherd children: Venerable Sister Lucia (age 10), St. Jacinta (age 7), and St. Francisco (age 9). These apparitions occurred monthly from May until October of 1917. Historically, as the entire world was in turmoil, Our Ladyâs most prominent message was to pray for world peace. The destruction of the world at that point in history was also mentioned by Our Lady, particularly in her second secret to the children. Our profoundly reflective day begins with a visit to the Little Chapel of the Apparitions. This simple yet modern chapel is where the Virgin Mary first appeared on May 13, 1917. Next, you will see the stunning neoclassical church, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary. This Sacred space contains the tombs of St. Francisco, St. Jacinta, and Sister Lucia. View the monument that commemorates the Sacred Heart of Jesus in the square. In honor of Our Ladyâs requests to pray the Rosary, the Basilica also features fifteen altars each dedicated to a mystery of the Rosary. Visit the Museum with the âFatima: Light and Peaceâ exhibition. Continue with a visit to the Holy Trinity Basilica. After free time for lunch, we will experience Christâs unconditional love by participating in the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra. The âSacred Wayâ marks the path taken by the shepherd children of Fatima to their first apparition with Our Lady. It is composed of fifteen small chapels commemorating the Passion of Our Lord. The fifteenth station, the Resurrection, can be found close to the Chapel of Calvary, dedicated to St. Stephen, King of Hungary. Ending the day with a visit to Valinhos, the site of Our Ladyâs August 1917 apparition and the first and third apparition of the Angel. Your night will conclude with private devotions and a candlelight procession, as requested by Our Lady in 1917. Enjoy dinner and a comfortable nightâs rest in Fatima.

tourDays.title: Day 5
tourDays.description: Fatima - Salamanca Depart Fatima and head to Salamanca, following a full breakfast at the hotel. Salamanca is a city in the Castilla y Leon region known for its large university. It is the oldest university in Spain that is still active. Our walking tour will take us to many famous sites. Visit the grand Plaza Mayor, an iconic square filled with food, shopping, and city events. See La Clerecia, a church and college of the Jesuit Order that was constructed in the 17th century. Next, visit La Casa de las Conchas, which is currently a public library and a monument decorated with shells, which symbolizes the ever-famous pilgrimage to Santiago (El Camino). Walk by the University of Salamanca, the oldest University in Spain and the third oldest in Europe. Walk across the Roman Bridge, which extends along the River Tormes and is a national monument. See La Iglesia de San Marcos, which is constructed in the Romanesque style and contains breathtaking paintings that portray many scenes of Our Ladyâs life. You will also see La Iglesia de San Martin, a Church devoted to St. Martin of Tours, the patron saint of beggars and those most in need. Visit the inside of the two joint Salamanca Cathedrals (old and new). The first is a Romanesque style, and the other is a Gothic style. Following this eventful day, you will return to your hotel for a delicious meal with your group and an overnight at your hotel in Salamanca.

tourDays.title: Day 6
tourDays.description: Salamanca - Alba de Tormes - Avila - Burgos This morning, after breakfast, you will board the bus and enjoy a short transfer to the village of Alba de Tormes. This town is home to the Carmelite Monastery that Saint Teresa founded in 1571. Upon arrival in Alba de Tormes, your group will celebrate Mass at this Monastery where the Saint died and is buried. Following Mass, you can visit the museum dedicated to St. Teresa of Avila, which also holds her incorrupt heart and left arm. Your group will enjoy free time for lunch on your own before continuing to the medieval city of Avila. Upon arrival, you will immediately notice the perfectly preserved 11th-century walls surrounding the old town. The conservation of architecture in this city, to which St. Teresa was born, deems its shrines, convents, and churches necessary to visit on any Catholic pilgrimage. The Cathedral de Avila encompasses the Romanesque, Gothic, and Renaissance styles of its time within its artwork and architecture. La Basilica de San Vicente in Avila stands on the site of the martyrdom of St. Vincent. Visit the Incarnation Convent, where St. Teresa became a nun. Saint Therese convinced Saint John of the Cross to reform the male Carmelite order, the reform she started when she met Saint John in Medina del Campo. After walking in the footsteps of St. Teresa, continue your journey to Burgos. Upon arrival in the historic capital of Old Castile, enjoy dinner. Following dinner, you will have the opportunity to explore the city of Burgos and admire its magnificent limestone Gothic-style cathedral. Late this evening, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 7
tourDays.description:
Burgos - Loyola - Lourdes Following breakfast, transfer from Burgos to Loyola to visit the birthplace of St. Ignatius, founder of the Jesuit Order. St. Ignatius dedicated himself to becoming a soldier of the Christian faith, and as a result of many tribulations, he wrote the ever-famous Spiritual Exercises. You will see the 17th-century Basilica dedicated to this remarkable Saint in Loyola. The Basilica is part of a series of buildings surrounding the âHoly House,â the birthplace of St. Ignatius. When you visit these Holy places, you will also have the opportunity to pray in the most venerated room, where St. Ignatius prayed and began his conversion. After meditating on the life of this founder of the Jesuit Order, you will enjoy free time for lunch and board the bus for the next destination. We will continue to Lourdes with a spectacular view of the Pyrenees Mountains. Upon arrival in Lourdes, you will check in to your hotel and enjoy a splendid dinner and peaceful overnight.
Days 8 & 9: Lourdes Over the next two days, you will stay in a small town in the Pyrenees Mountains. During your time in Lourdes, you will pray and meditate at the site of Our Ladyâs apparitions. Our Lady first appeared to Bernadette in 1858 and announced herself as âThe Immaculate Conceptionâ near the Grotto of Massabielle. During the first two apparitions, little Bernadette prayed the Rosary with Our Lady and left without exchanging words. During the following apparitions, Our Lady emphasized Godâs love for us and the necessity of performing acts of penance for sinners. Throughout your time in Lourdes, you will have the opportunity to attend Mass at the Grotto, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette. Watch a video presentation that explains the story of Lourdes. Wash your hands, wash your face, and drink the water of the miraculous spring. Finish with a short prayer: âOur Lady of Lourdes, pray for us. St. Bernadette, pray for us. O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.â Experience Christâs unconditional love as you meditate upon the life-size Stations of the Cross that overlook the Grotto of Massabielle. In Lourdes, you will walk in and meditate upon the footsteps of St. Bernadette. Your group will have the opportunity to see Boly Mill, the birthplace of St. Bernadette, and the âCachot,â an abandoned prison where Bernadetteâs impoverished family lived. Each evening, following dinner, you can attend the candlelight procession and pray the Rosary before a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 10
tourDays.description: Lourdes - Paris - Lisieux (St. Therese - the Little Flower) Today, you will enjoy breakfast before departing for Pau or Lourdes Airport for your short flight to Paris, continue on to Lisieux. According to Pope Pius X, St. Therese of Lisieux was the âgreatest saint of modern times.â Her extraordinary love for God and service to humanity will come alive as you walk in the great Saintâs footsteps. During your visit, you will see the beautiful Basilica of St. Therese and its magnificent mosaics and stained glass windows. You will have the opportunity to view relics, clothing, and personal objects that belonged to St. Therese when you visit her family home, Les Buissonnets. Additionally, you will tour the Carmelite Convent, which she entered in 1888 and where she is now buried. Dinner and overnight at your hotel in Lisieux.

tourDays.title: Day 11
tourDays.description: Lisieux - Landing Beaches - American Cemetery - Lisieux Upon waking up in Lisieux, enjoy breakfast, and then your group will celebrate Mass. After Mass we will travel to the Normandy Landing beaches. The Normandy landings were the landing operations, which took place on Tuesday, June 6, 1944 (termed D-Day) by the Allies of Normandy during World War II. As the largest seaborne invasion in history, the operation began the liberation of German-occupied northwestern Europe from Nazi control and contributed to the Alliesâ victory on the Western Front. Continue to visit The Normandy American Cemetery and Memorial, a World War II cemetery and memorial in Colleville-Sur-Mer, Normandy, France, honoring the American troops that died in Europe during World War II. Many of the brave American soldiers of World War II are buried here, and it is encouraged to say a prayer in thanksgiving for their courage. Return to Lisieux for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 12
tourDays.description: Lisieux - Chartres - Paris This morning, your day begins with an early breakfast before we depart for Chartres, known worldwide for its massive Cathedral Notre Dame and its incredible stained-glass windows from the 12th and 13th centuries. The World Heritage site, UNESCO, calls the Cathedral âthe high point of French Gothic artâ and a âmasterpieceâ. Pilgrims will also be able to venerate a precious relic of the Veil of Our Lady which is currently on display at the back of the main altar of the Cathedral of Chartres. You will have some free time for lunch in the quaint town of Chartres. After lunch, we will continue to Paris to check-in at your hotel, followed by some free time before a delicious dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 13
tourDays.description: Paris Following breakfast, we will celebrate Mass. Following Mass enjoy a full day of sightseeing including the magnificent Sacre Coeur Basilica atop Montmartre Hill. The Basilica, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, was originally built in 1914 as an act of penance for infidelity that France experienced during that time. See the beautiful mosaic of the Risen Christ and the remarkable Grand Organ. Visit the the Tombs of many notable Cardinals. Time permitting, you may have the opportunity to ascend a staircase to the Dome, where you will take in a breathtaking panoramic view of Paris. Continue with a visit of the Chapel of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal, where we will have the opportunity to view the incorrupt body of St. Catherine Laboure. The Saintâs guardian angel led her to the chapel where the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared to her. During the apparitions, Our Lady repeatedly instructed the making and purpose of the Miraculous Medal. According to the Blessed Virgin Mary, those who wear the Miraculous Medal will receive special protection and abundant graces. Following this prayerful and reflective experience, we will walk to Saint Vincent de Paul Church. Next, on our tour of Paris, we will visit one of the most incredible churches in the world: Notre Dame Cathedral. The Cathedral has recently been re-opened to visitors. Guided group tours are scheduled to resume in June 2025. Board a bus tour and see some of the most recognizable symbols of Paris, including the Eiffel Tower, the Invalides, the LâArch de Triomphe, and the Champ-Elysees, the worldâs most famous boulevard. Your busy day ends with a lovely meal and a comfortable overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 14
tourDays.description: Paris - Rome Following breakfast at your hotel, your group will transfer to the Charles de Gaulle Airport and board your short flight to Rome. Upon arrival at Rome airport, collect your luggage in the baggage claim area and continue to the arrival hall, where you will be greeted by a tour escort and/or driver. You will make your way to the bus and transfer to your hotel. Following check-in, you will have free time to unpack, relax, or explore Rome on your own. Your tour escort may suggest places to visit. Later in the afternoon, your group will meet in the hotel lobby for a âMeet and Greetâ with your fellow pilgrims and depart for Mass. Following Mass, you will attend a welcome dinner. After dinner, you can walk to St. Peterâs Square as a group for the Rosary (optional).

tourDays.title: Day 15
tourDays.description: Rome: Papal Audience - Basilica of St. John the Lateran - Holy Stairs - Basilica of St. Mary Major After a nice breakfast at your hotel, your first sightseeing day in Rome starts! The tour begins with the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square! The Audience is celebrated each Wednesday by His Holiness, the Pope (pending the papal schedule). Following the Audience, there will be free time for lunch, shopping, or to mail a postcard from the Vatican Post Office. This afternoon, you will visit the oldest of the four major Basilicas in Rome: The Basilica of St. John the Lateran. This Basilica houses the relics of Peter and Paul. It is where the Pope was installed as Bishop of Rome and where he officiates as the Bishop of Rome. Next, we will cross the street to visit the Holy Staircase. Tradition states that this Staircase is from Pontius Pilateâs palace in Jerusalem during the time of Jesus. It was brought to Rome by St. Helen in the 4th Century. If time permits, you may climb the steps on your knees while meditating on Christâs agonizing Passion. Proceed to the Basilica of St. Mary Major. This Basilica contains a relic from the Manger of the Infant Jesus. Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 16
tourDays.description: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica - Vatican Museum - Appian Way - Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls - Catacombs This morning, you will enjoy an early breakfast before making your way to the largest Church in Christendom: St. Peterâs Basilica. This Basilica was built on the site where St. Peter, the first Pope and Bishop of Rome, was martyred. Here, you can view Michelangeloâs Pieta. This stunning marble sculpture depicts the Virgin Mary holding Christ after His crucifixion, death, and removal from the cross before being placed in the tomb. Proceed to the Vatican Museum, where you will see the most impressive edifices, galleries, and awe-inspiring relics. Observe the Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, and the restored mural of the Last Judgment. The final stop on your Vatican tour is at the tomb of Saint John Paul II. Next, head to the Piazza Navona area for some free time and lunch (on your own). Continue on your short journey down the Appian Way, the earliest road of Ancient Rome. This road leads to the Domino Quo Vadis Chapel, the Baths of Caracalla, the Arch of Drusus, the Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and the catacombs of St. Callixtus. The day concludes with a visit to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls. Originally founded by Emperor Constantine in the 4th Century, this Basilica is the burial place of Saint Paul the Apostle. We will make our way to a local restaurant for dinner. Following dinner, feel free to explore the streets of Rome or return to the hotel for the evening.

tourDays.title: Day 17
tourDays.description: Rome - Montecassino - San Giovanni Rotondo Following breakfast, you will board your bus to enjoy the scenic route to Montecassino, passing through the Roman countryside, known for its villas and vineyards. During the bus ride, your tour escort will share interesting information regarding Italyâs spiritual, historical, and cultural history. Montecassino, the principal monastery of the Benedictine Order, was founded by Saint Benedict around 530 A.D. Following the tour, you can visit the gift shop before departing for San Giovanni Rotondo, the hometown of St. Padre Pio. Upon arrival in San Giovanni Rotondo, enjoy dinner at a local restaurant and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 18
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Monte Sant' Angelo Enjoy breakfast, and then we will visit the Old Church. After Mass, we will tour the sanctuary and see the crucifix, in front of which St. Pio received the stigmata. Visit the confessional from where St. Pio spent innumerable hours listening to confessions. Next, we will board the bus and travel along the beautiful Gargano Peninsula to the Grotto of St. Michael the Archangel. St. Michael appeared to a Bishop at this grotto to assure him that his diocese would not be destroyed as he feared. Following the visit to the grotto, enjoy some free time. On the way back to San Giovanni Rotondo, view breathtaking ocean views. Upon arrival, you will have time for devotion and reflection. Dinner and overnight. *Candlelight Procession: Between May and October, attend the weekly Candlelight Procession at the Sanctuary of St. Pio after dinner. These processions are lit by candlelight and are guided by the Most Holy Rosary. Following this prayerful experience, you will return to your hotel for a restful overnight.

tourDays.title: Day 19
tourDays.description: San Giovanni Rotondo - Lanciano - Loreto - Assisi After breakfast, depart for Assisi. We will stop in Lanciano for a private Mass at the Convent/Church of Saint Francis built on top of the antique Church of St. Longinus. This Church is the site of a Eucharistic Miracle that occurred in the eighth Century. At the time of the miracle, there was a Basilian monk who struggled with the belief in the Real Presence in the Eucharist. During Mass, the monk, with doubt in his voice, said the words of consecration and saw the bread and wine transformed into Christâs physical flesh and blood. Leave for the Marian Shrine of Loreto to visit the Holy House of Nazareth and the beautiful Madonna of Loreto. Tradition holds that this is the house where Mary first prayed the Magnificat, where Jesus grew up, and where the Holy Family lived together in Nazareth. It was transported several times by angels to its current location. End the day in Assisi, hometown of St. Francis and St. Clare, with dinner and overnight at your hotel.

tourDays.title: Day 20
tourDays.description: Assisi Enjoy an early breakfast, followed by a full day of touring the hometown of St. Francis. St. Francis is the âPatron Saint of Animals and the Environment.â He founded the Franciscan Order and has inspired millions with his life of simplicity and humility. The atmosphere of Assisi has not changed since St. Francis began his ministry in the early 13th Century. We will start our tour at the Basilica of St. Francis. Visit his tomb, view a series of frescoes depicting his life, and a few of the Saintâs possessions. From there, we will continue on a walking tour through this picturesque town, including the birthplace of St. Francis. Visit the Santuario Della Spogliazione where St. Carlo Acutis is entombed. Carlo is the first millennial to have been declared a Saint. He had a great love for Jesus in the Eucharist and died of leukemia at the young age of 15. Our tour ends at the Church that honors St. Clare, the foundress of the Poor Clare Sisters. This Saint followed the teachings of St. Francis very closely by also living a life of poverty and humility. Enjoy some time for prayer, shopping, or a nice lunch. After lunch, we will board the bus, which will take us outside the walls of Assisi to the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels. This Basilica is where St. Francis spent most of his life, and it is made up of two structures. The first is the âPorziuncolaâ, where St. Francis founded his order of the Friar Minor (Franciscans). The second is the âCapella del Transitoâ, where St. Francis died. You will have the opportunity to visit the beautiful Rose Garden where St. Francis and other friars lived, as well as the cave where the Saint retired to pray. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

Return Home After an early breakfast and heartfelt farewells, you will head to Rome Fiumicino airport for your return flight(s) home. tourDays.title: Barcelona - Manresa - Montserrat
tourDays.description: This morning, your day will begin with breakfast and a sightseeing tour of Barcelona, including panoramic views of the Port of Barcelona, Montjuic, Plaza de EspaÃ±a, and Plaza de Catalunya. Continue with a guided walk through the Gothic Quarter and visit the Cathedral of Barcelona and Antoni Gaudiâs La Sagrada Familia. In the afternoon, travel to Manresa to visit the Sanctuary of Saint Ignatius of Loyola and the Holy Cave, then continue to Montserrat, home to the miraculous Black Madonna. Arrive in time for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Sightseeing tour of Barcelona; Guided walk through the Gothic Quarter; Visit Cathedral of Barcelona; Visit La Sagrada Familia; Visit Sanctuary of Saint Ignatius and the Holy Cave in Manresa; Travel to Montserrat

tourDays.title: Montserrat
tourDays.description: After breakfast, visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Montserrat, located on a rugged mountainside, and learn about the history and veneration of the Black Madonna. Dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit the Shrine of Our Lady of Montserrat; Learn about the Black Madonna and site history

tourDays.title: Montserrat - Zaragoza - Madrid
tourDays.description: Following breakfast, depart for Zaragoza. In Zaragoza, visit the Basilica del Pilar (site where Our Lady appeared to St. James) and La Seo Cathedral. Enjoy a walking tour of the city and its gastronomy and folklore. In the evening, continue to Madrid for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart for Zaragoza; Visit Basilica del Pilar; Visit La Seo Cathedral; Walking tour of Zaragoza; Continue to Madrid

tourDays.title: Madrid & Toledo
tourDays.description: After breakfast, tour Madrid including visits to the Royal Palace and Plaza Mayor. Then visit Toledo and its many historic sites, including the Church of Santo TomÃ©, the TrÃ¡nsito Synagogue, Santa MarÃ­a la Blanca, the Church of San Juan de los Reyes, and several city gates. Return to Madrid for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Tour Madrid (Royal Palace, Plaza Mayor); Visit Toledo and its historic sites; Return to Madrid

tourDays.title: Madrid - Astorga - O' Cebreiro - Santiago de Compostela
tourDays.description: Depart Madrid and head toward Santiago de Compostela, stopping in Astorga to visit the Bishopâs Palace by Antonio Gaudi (Museum of El Camino). Enter Galicia via Lugo and stop in O' Cebreiro to view traditional houses and the site of a Eucharistic Miracle. In the evening proceed to Santiago de Compostela for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Depart Madrid; Visit Bishopâs Palace in Astorga / Museum of El Camino; Enter Galicia via Lugo; Visit O' Cebreiro; Proceed to Santiago de Compostela

tourDays.title: Santiago de Compostela
tourDays.description: Walk a few miles of El Camino through eucalyptus groves, celebrate the International Pilgrim Mass at the Cathedral of St. James, visit the Cathedral (including descending into the crypt to see the relics of St. James), and enjoy a sightseeing tour of the city including Obradoiro Square, Fonseca Palace, and Gelmirez Palace. Evening at leisure until dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Walk a few miles of El Camino; Celebrate International Pilgrim Mass at the Cathedral of St. James; Visit the Cathedral of Santiago and descend into the crypt; Sightseeing tour of Santiago de Compostela

tourDays.title: Santiago de Compostela â Rome
tourDays.description: After breakfast, transfer to Santiago Airport for your flight to Rome. Upon arrival, transfer to your hotel, check in and have free time. Between 3:00 PM and 3:30 PM meet in the hotel lobby for a Meet and Greet with fellow pilgrims and depart for Mass, followed by a welcome dinner. After dinner, there is an optional walk to St. Peterâs Square to pray the Rosary.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to Santiago Airport; Flight to Rome; Transfer to hotel and check-in; Meet and Greet in hotel lobby; Attend Mass; Welcome dinner; Optional walk to St. Peterâs Square to pray the Rosary

tourDays.title: Rome: Papal Audience - Piazza Navona â Pantheon - Basilica of St. John the Lateran â Holy Stairs - Basilica of St. Mary Major
tourDays.description: After breakfast attend the Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square (pending the papal schedule). There will be free time for lunch. This afternoon visit the Basilica of St. John the Lateran, the Holy Staircase (with the option to climb on your knees), and the Basilica of St. Mary Major. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Attend Papal Audience in St. Peterâs Square; Free time for lunch; Visit Basilica of St. John the Lateran; Visit the Holy Staircase (optional to climb on knees); Visit Basilica of St. Mary Major

tourDays.title: Rome: St. Peter's Basilica - Vatican Museum - Appian Way - Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls - Catacombs
tourDays.description: Early breakfast followed by a visit to St. Peterâs Basilica to view Michelangeloâs Pieta. Proceed to the Vatican Museum (Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, Last Judgment) and see the tomb of Saint John Paul II. After free time in the Piazza Navona area, continue down the Appian Way to visit sites such as the Quo Vadis Chapel, Baths of Caracalla, Arch of Drusus, Tomb of Cecilia Metella, and the catacombs of St. Callixtus. Conclude the day with a visit to the Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls and dinner at a local restaurant.
tourDays.activities: Visit St. Peterâs Basilica; View Michelangeloâs Pieta; Visit the Vatican Museum (Tapestry Gallery, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, Last Judgment); Visit tomb of Saint John Paul II; Free time in Piazza Navona area; Visit Appian Way sites and catacombs; Visit Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls; Dinner at a local restaurant

tourDays.title: Rome - Montecassino - Saint Philomena Sanctuary, Mugnano - Sorrento
tourDays.description: After breakfast board the bus to Montecassino for a tour of the Benedictine monastery and visit the gift shop. Then visit the Shrine of Saint Philomena in Mugnano del Cardinale. Drive to Sorrento with panoramic views of the Bay of Naples, followed by time to relax before dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Bus to Montecassino and tour the monastery; Visit gift shop; Visit Shrine of Saint Philomena in Mugnano del Cardinale; Drive to Sorrento; Relax before dinner

tourDays.title: Sorrento - Amalfi Coast - Sorrento
tourDays.description: Tour the Amalfi Coast, following winding coastal roads with a stop to view Positano, drive through Praiano by St. Gennaro Church, visit Amalfi and view the Amalfi Cathedral, have free time for lunch, then stop in Ravello to view its Cathedral and Villa Rufolo before returning to Sorrento for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Tour the Amalfi Coast; Stop to view Positano; Drive through Praiano (by St. Gennaro Church); Visit Amalfi and view Amalfi Cathedral; Free time for lunch; Visit Ravello (Cathedral, Villa Rufolo); Return to Sorrento

tourDays.title: Sorrento - Pompeii - Assisi
tourDays.description: After breakfast board the motorcoach to Pompeii to walk through the archaeological ruins and visit the Shrine of the Rosary of Pompei (La Madonna Del Rosario), which houses venerated paintings and relics. Enjoy time to relax before dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Board motorcoach to Pompeii; Walk through the archaeological site of Pompeii; Visit the Shrine of the Rosary of Pompei (La Madonna Del Rosario)

tourDays.title: Assisi
tourDays.description: Tour Assisi starting at the Basilica of St. Francis to visit his tomb, view frescoes and possessions, then continue on a walking tour including the birthplace of St. Francis, visit the Santuario Della Spogliazione (where St. Carlo Acutis is entombed), and the Church of St. Clare. After lunch, visit the Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels (Porziuncola and Capella del Transito), the Rose Garden, and the cave where St. Francis prayed. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Basilica of St. Francis (tomb, frescoes, possessions); Walking tour of Assisi including birthplace of St. Francis; Visit Santuario Della Spogliazione (tomb of St. Carlo Acutis); Visit Church of St. Clare; Visit Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels (Porziuncola, Capella del Transito); Visit Rose Garden and cave where St. Francis prayed

tourDays.title: Assisi - Orvieto - Assisi
tourDays.description: Ride through the Umbrian mountains to Orvieto, visit the renowned Orvieto Cathedral, then return to Assisi for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Ride through Umbrian mountains to Orvieto; Visit Orvieto Cathedral; Return to Assisi

tourDays.title: Return Home
tourDays.description: After an early breakfast and farewells, head to Rome Fiumicino airport for your return flight(s) home.
tourDays.activities: Early breakfast; Transfer to Rome Fiumicino airport; Board return flight(s)

tourDays.title: Day 1 - USA - Krakow
tourDays.description: Depart USA for your overnight flight to Krakow, Poland. Dinner and breakfast will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Overnight flight from USA to Krakow; In-flight dinner and breakfast

tourDays.title: Day 2 - Arrive Krakow â Zakopane - Krakow
tourDays.description: Upon arrival in Krakow you will be greeted by a tour guide and/or driver and escorted to the vehicle that will bring you to Zakopane where you will enjoy a short walk on one of John Paul II's favorite walking trails, visit the Hermitage of Brother Albert, walk Krupowki Street for shopping, stop at the Wieliczka Salt Mines, then return to Krakow for dinner and an optional stroll in the old city.
tourDays.activities: Meet guide/driver on arrival; Transfer to Zakopane; Short walk on John Paul II's favorite trail; Visit Hermitage of Brother Albert; Walk Krupowki Street for shopping; Visit Wieliczka Salt Mines; Return to Krakow; dinner; optional stroll in old city

tourDays.title: Day 3 â Krakow â Auschwitz - Krakow
tourDays.description: Explore Krakow's Market Square, hear the bugler from St. Mary's Tower, tour the Cathedral (including the Coronation Chapel, Royal Chambers and Wit Stwosz altar), then visit Auschwitz concentration camp to see the cell of St. Maximilian Kolbe and the Martyrdom Museum. Return to hotel for dinner.
tourDays.activities: Visit Krakow Market Square; Hear bugler from St. Mary's Tower; Tour the Cathedral, Coronation Chapel and Royal Chambers; Pray before the Wit Stwosz altar; Visit Auschwitz concentration camp; See St. Maximilian Kolbe's cell and Martyrdom Museum; Return to hotel for dinner

tourDays.title: Day 4 â Krakow â Divine Mercy â Lagiewniki - Krakow
tourDays.description: Day excursion to Åagiewniki (the Sanctuary of Divine Mercy). Visit the Sanctuary housing the Divine Mercy image and relics of St. Faustina, St. Faustina's convent chapel and tomb, the newly constructed Shrine of Divinity dedicated by Saint John Paul II, celebrate Mass at the Shrine, visit the 'Have no Fear' center and pray by the relic of Saint John Paul II, then return to the hotel for dinner.
tourDays.activities: Travel to Åagiewniki (Sanctuary of Divine Mercy); Visit Divine Mercy image and relics of St. Faustina; Visit St. Faustina's convent chapel and tomb; Visit the new Shrine of Divinity; Celebrate Mass at the Shrine; Visit 'Have no Fear' center and pray by relic of St. John Paul II; Return to hotel for dinner

tourDays.title: Day 5 â Krakow - Lisbon
tourDays.description: After breakfast transfer to the airport for a connection flight to Lisbon. On arrival you will be greeted and escorted on a sightseeing tour of Lisbon visiting the Cathedral, St. Jerome's Monastery, Saint Anthony's Church, Belem Quarter (including Belem Tower), 25 April Bridge, Discoveries Monument, Basilica of the Star, Rossio Square, Commerce Square and MarquÃªs de Pombal Square. Arrive at the hotel in time for dinner.
tourDays.activities: Transfer to airport and fly Krakow to Lisbon; Meet guide on arrival in Lisbon; Sightseeing tour of Lisbon including listed monuments and squares; Arrive at hotel for dinner

tourDays.title: Day 6 - Lisbon - Santarem - Fatima
tourDays.description: Depart Lisbon for SantarÃ©m. Walk through narrow streets to the Church of St. Stephen to see the Eucharistic miracle (on display since 1269) and celebrate Mass there. Continue on to Fatima, arriving in time for dinner.
tourDays.activities: Transfer from Lisbon to SantarÃ©m; Walk to Church of St. Stephen and view the Eucharistic miracle; Celebrate Mass at Church of St. Stephen; Continue to Fatima; arrive for dinner

tourDays.title: Day 7 - Fatima
tourDays.description: Celebrate Mass at the Little Chapel of the Apparitions. Tour Fatima: the Basilica, the graves of Francisco and Jacinta, the Hamlet of Aljustrel, and Valinhos. Walk the Stations of the Cross along the Via Sacra to the Chapel of Calvary, drink water from the miraculous well, attend blessing of the sick and participate in nightly candlelight processions. Time for private devotions before dinner.
tourDays.activities: Celebrate Mass at the Little Chapel of the Apparitions; Tour the Basilica and visit graves of Francisco and Jacinta; Visit Hamlet of Aljustrel and Valinhos; Walk the Stations of the Cross (Via Sacra) to Chapel of Calvary; Drink water from the miraculous well; Attend blessing of the sick; Participate in nightly candlelight procession; Private devotions

tourDays.title: Day 8 - Fatima - USA
tourDays.description: After breakfast depart for the return flight home.
tourDays.activities: Breakfast at hotel; Transfer to airport and depart Fatima for return flight to USA

tourDays.title: Depart for the Holy Land
tourDays.description: Make your way to your local airport where you will board your overnight flight. Your meals will be served on board.
tourDays.activities: Board overnight flight; Meals served on board

tourDays.title: Arrive in Tel Aviv
tourDays.description: Upon arrival at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, collect luggage and proceed to the Arrivals Hall to be greeted by your tour guide and/or driver. Transfer to your hotel in Tel Aviv, check in, and enjoy dinner at the hotel.
tourDays.activities: Collect luggage; Meet tour guide/driver; Transfer to hotel; Hotel check-in; Dinner at hotel

tourDays.title: Tel Aviv - Caesarea - Nazareth - Cana - Tiberias
tourDays.description: Depart Tel Aviv to Caesarea MarÃ­tima to see the Roman Theater, Herodâs Palace, Hippodrome, and harbor. Continue to Haifa (Mt. Carmel) to visit the Carmelite Shrine and Elijah's cave. Continue to Nazareth for lunch and visit the Church of the Annunciation, museum, archaeological garden, and St. Josephâs Church and grotto. Celebrate Mass in the Church of the Annunciation. Visit Cana (Wedding Church) where married couples may renew wedding vows. Continue on to Tiberias for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Caesarea MarÃ­tima (Roman Theater, Herodâs Palace, Hippodrome, harbor); Visit Carmelite Shrine and pray at Elijah's cave; Lunch in Nazareth; Visit Church of the Annunciation, museum/archaeological garden, St. Joseph's Church and grotto; Celebrate Mass in the Church of the Annunciation; Visit Cana (Wedding Church) and renew wedding vows (ceremony, not a Mass); Travel to Tiberias; dinner and overnight

Visit the Mount of Beatitudes, Tabgha (site of the miracle of the 5,000 and St. Peter's Primacy), Magdala (birthplace of Mary Magdalene), and Capernaum (including the Synagogue). Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.

tourDays.title: Mt. Tabor - Jericho - Jerusalem
tourDays.description: Drive to Mount Tabor (site of the Transfiguration). Celebrate Mass at the Basilica of the Transfiguration. Continue south to the Jordan Valley and visit Jericho, viewing the Mount of Temptation. Drive up to Jerusalem, check in to your hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Reflect at Mount Tabor; Celebrate Mass at the Basilica of the Transfiguration; Visit Jericho and view the Mount of Temptation; Drive to Jerusalem and hotel check-in

tourDays.title: Jerusalem: Bethlehem & Ein Karem
tourDays.description: Visit a model of the Second Temple in Jerusalem. Drive to Ein Karem to visit the Church of the Nativity of St. John the Baptist and the Church of the Visitation, with opportunity to pray the Mystery of the Rosary. In the afternoon transfer to Bethlehem to view Shepherdâs Fields and Manger Square, proceed down to the Grotto of the Nativity and celebrate Mass. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Second Temple model; Visit Ein Karem churches (Nativity of St. John the Baptist and Church of the Visitation); Pray the Mystery of the Rosary; Transfer to Bethlehem; view Shepherd's Fields; Visit Manger Square and Grotto of the Nativity; Celebrate Mass in the Church of the Nativity

tourDays.title: Jordan River - Qumran - Dead Sea
tourDays.description: Travel down the Jordan Valley to Qumran to see the 2,000-year-old ruins and learn about the Dead Sea Scrolls. Time and weather permitting, have the opportunity to float in the Dead Sea. Travel through the Judean wilderness and transfer to Bethany, the site associated with Lazarus. Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight.
tourDays.activities: Visit Qumran ruins (Dead Sea Scrolls site); Opportunity to float in the Dead Sea (time/weather permitting); Travel through the Judean wilderness; Visit Bethany (site of Lazarus)

tourDays.title: Jerusalem: Mt. Of Olives - Gethsemane - Mt. Zion (Upper Room)
